children.translated_text: Oṃ. Salutation to <s>Vighnavināyaka</s> (Gaṇeśa, the remover of obstacles).
I bow to the cause of the creation, sustenance, and dissolution of the universe,

children.text: viśveśvaraṃ viśvadharaṃ viśvaṃ ca viśvahetukam // Valc_1.1 //
children.translated_text: the lord of the universe, the supporter of the universe, the universe itself, and the cause of the universe. // Valc_1.1 //
The seed of the universe, of the form of truth, the witness of all, the imperishable,
the omniscient, dwelling in all beings, bearing all powers, the all-pervading lord. // Valc_1.2 //
Having made obeisance to the Brahmins, by the command of the king of <s>Navadvīpa</s>,
comprising the origin of Brahmins and the divisions thereof,
along with the <s>gotras</s> (lineages) and family names of the <s>Rāḍhīya</s> and <s>Varendrā</s> [Brahmins] —
that royal chronicle called the <s>Vallālacarita</s> is now recounted. // Valc_1.3 //
From the left ear of <s>Brahmā</s>, who desired to create, <s>Pulaha</s> was born;
<s>Aṅgiras</s> arose from the nostril; <s>Ruci</s> from the mouth. // Valc_1.4 //
<s>Marīci</s> from the shoulder region, and <s>Pracetas</s> from the lower lip;

children.text: ekādaśa caiva rudrā lalāṭāt krodhasambhavāḥ // Valc_1.5 //
children.translated_text: and the eleven <s>Rudras</s>, born of wrath, from the forehead. // Valc_1.5 //

children.text: pulahasya suto vātsyaḥ śāṇḍilyaśca ruceḥ sutaḥ /
children.translated_text: The son of <s>Pulaha</s> was <s>Vātsya</s>, and the son of <s>Ruci</s> was <s>Śāṇḍilya</s>;
<s>Bharadvāja</s> is remembered as the son of <s>Bṛhaspati</s> of the <s>Āṅgirasa</s> [line]. // Valc_1.6 //
From the mind of <s>Marīci</s> was born <s>Kaśyapa</s>, the lord of creatures;
and from the mind of <s>Pracetas</s>, the blessed sage <s>Gautama</s>. // Valc_1.7 //
From <s>Gautama</s> was born <s>Sāvarṇi</s>, that foremost among sages;

children.text: babhūvuḥ pañcagotrāṇi caiteṣāṃ pravarā bhave // Valc_1.8 //
children.translated_text: from these arose the five <s>gotras</s> (lineages), and their <s>pravaras</s> (distinguished ancestors) in this world. // Valc_1.8 //
Other Brahmin communities arose from the mouth of <s>Brahmā</s>;

children.text: tāḥ sthitāḥ deśabhedena gotraśūnyāśca bhūpate // Valc_1.9 //
children.translated_text: they are situated in different regions and are without <s>gotra</s>, O king. // Valc_1.9 //
<s>Kaśyapa</s> begot the twelve <s>Ādityas</s> upon <s>Aditi</s>;

children.text: atrernetramalāccandraḥ kṣīrode ca babhūva ha // Valc_1.10 //
children.translated_text: and from the eye-filth of <s>Atri</s>, the moon was born in the ocean of milk. // Valc_1.10 //
Those of the lineages of the moon, the sun, and <s>Manu</s> are considered the foremost <s>Kṣatriyas</s>;
other <s>Kṣatriya</s> communities [arose] from the arm region of <s>Brahmā</s>,
the <s>Vaiśyas</s> from the thigh region, and the <s>Śūdra</s> communities from the feet. // Valc_1.11 //
By birth one is born a <s>Śūdra</s>; through <s>saṃskāras</s> (sacraments) one is called a twice-born (<s>dvija</s>);
through the study of the <s>Vedas</s> one becomes a learned one (<s>vipra</s>); through knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>, one becomes a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. // Valc_1.12 //
The <s>Sārasvatas</s>, <s>Kānyakubjas</s>, <s>Gauḍas</s>, <s>Maithilas</s>, and <s>Kolkalas</s> —
these are declared as the five <s>Gauḍa</s> [groups], dwelling north of the <s>Vindhya</s>. // Valc_1.13 //
The <s>Karṇāṭas</s>, <s>Tailaṅgas</s>, <s>Gurjaras</s>, dwellers of the <s>Rāṣṭra</s> (Maharashtra),
the <s>Andhras</s>, and the <s>Drāviḍas</s> — [these] five dwell south of the <s>Vindhya</s>. // Valc_1.14 //

children.text:
sarvve dvijāḥ kānyakujāḥ māthuraṃ māgadhaṃ vinā /
māgadho brahmaṇā parvvūṃ kalpito dvija eva ca /
varāhasya ca gharmmeṇa māthuro jāyate tathā // Valc_1.15 /
children.translated_text: and the <s>Māthura</s> was born likewise from the sweat of <s>Varāha</s> (the Boar). // Valc_1.15 //
With the marks of <s>Vedic</s> speech and the goad (?), the Brahmins arrived in <s>Gauḍa</s> (Bengal),
riding on horses, proficient in all scriptures. // Valc_1.16 //
All twice-born are [originally] <s>Kānyakubjas</s>, except the <s>Māthura</s> and <s>Māgadha</s>; the <s>Māgadha</s> was formerly designated by <s>Brahmā</s> as a twice-born indeed,
<s>Medhātithi</s>, <s>Kṣitīśa</s>, <s>Vītarāga</s>, and <s>Suṣeṇaka</s>,

children.text: saubhariratnagarbhau ca tathā vipraḥ sudhānidhiḥ // Valc_1.17 //
children.translated_text: <s>Saubhari</s>, <s>Ratnagarbha</s>, and also the Brahmin <s>Sudhānidhi</s> — // Valc_1.17 //
by the king's word, those seven married seven hundred women each;
by the will of the gods, seven excellent sons were born to them;

children.text: varandaraṃ gatāḥ pañca kaniṣṭho rāḍhasaṃsthitau // Valc_1.18 //
children.translated_text: five went to <s>Varendara</s> (Varendra), and the youngest settled in <s>Rāḍha</s>. // Valc_1.18 //
By the foremost king <s>Ādiśūra</s>, a group of five Brahmins was brought,

children.text: pañcagotrānvitaṃ teṣāṃ nāma gotrañca kathyate // Valc_1.19 //
children.translated_text: having five <s>gotras</s>; their names and <s>gotras</s> are now stated: // Valc_1.19 //
The <s>gotra</s> of <s>Śrīharṣa</s> is <s>Bhāradvāja</s>; that of <s>Dakṣa</s> is remembered as <s>Kāśyapa</s>;
that of <s>Vedagarbha</s> is <s>Sāvarṇa</s>; and of <s>Chāndaḍa</s>, <s>Vātsya</s>;
the <s>gotra</s> of <s>Bhaṭṭanārāyaṇa</s> is stated to be <s>Śāṇḍilya</s>. // Valc_1.20 //
From <s>Bhaṭṭa</s> arose sixteen [descendants]; from <s>Dakṣa</s> also sixteen;
four were born of <s>Śrīharṣa</s>, upholders of the <s>Bhāradvāja</s> lineage;
twelve from <s>Vedagarbha</s>, and then eleven from <s>Chāndaḍa</s>. // Valc_1.21 //
Some Brahmins came who were <s>Vaidika</s> (Vedic scholars), well-versed in the <s>Vedas</s>;

children.text: pāścātyā dākṣiṇātyāśca śeṣoktā drāviḍāḥ smṛtāḥ // Valc_1.22 //
children.translated_text: those from the west and the south are known as the remaining <s>Drāviḍas</s>. // Valc_1.22 //
In the domain of <s>Vallāla</s>, the <s>Kulīnas</s> (those of noble family) are indeed like deities themselves;

children.text: śrotriyā meravo jñeyā ghaṭakāḥ stutipāṭhakāḥ // Valc_1.23 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Śrotriyas</s> are to be known as [solid as] mountains, and the <s>Ghaṭakas</s> are reciters of praise. // Valc_1.23 //
Conduct, humility, learning, repute, visiting sacred places,
devotion, good behavior, austerity, and charity — these nine are the marks of a [noble] family. // Valc_1.24 //
One may keep a daughter at home even until death, even if she has attained puberty,

children.text: na caivaināṃ prayacchettu kulahīnāya karhicit // Valc_1.25 //
children.translated_text: but one should never give her to a man of inferior family. // Valc_1.25 //

children.text: ekāṃ śākhāṃ sakalpāṃ vā ṣaḍbhiraṅgairadhītya ca /
children.translated_text: Having studied one branch [of the Veda] with its <s>kalpa</s> (ritual manual), along with the six auxiliary sciences,

children.text: ṣaṭkarmmanirato vipraḥ śrotriyo nāma dharmmavit // Valc_1.26 //
children.translated_text: a Brahmin devoted to the six duties is called a <s>Śrotriya</s>, a knower of <s>dharma</s>. // Valc_1.26 //
A <s>Kulīna</s> and a <s>Maulika</s> — [distinguished] according to qualities —

children.text: vaṃśajaśca purā rājñā vallālena suniścitam // Valc_1.27 //
children.translated_text: and a <s>Vaṃśaja</s> (one of lineage) — these were formerly determined by King <s>Vallāla</s>. // Valc_1.27 //
Thus in the <s>Vallālacarita</s>, the account of the origin of the <s>varṇas</s> (social classes).
Now, the account of the reason for the designation '<s>Pratigrāhin</s>' (acceptor of gifts).

children.text: dhenuṃ svarṇamayīṃ yajñe viprebhyaḥ pradadau nṛpaḥ /
children.translated_text: The king gave a golden cow at a sacrifice to the Brahmins;
in the cutting of that golden cow, [a goldsmith] fell [into transgression]. // Valc_1.28 //
Then a certain goldsmith was banished by the king;
the Brahmins who accepted gifts became excluded from all religious duties. // Valc_1.29 //
Thus the reason for the [designation] <s>Pratigrāhin</s>.
Now, the village-names of those designated as <s>Pratigrāhins</s>.

children.text: śaṅkare pītamuṇḍī ca gaḍopi ca divākaraḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Śaṅkara</s> [and] <s>Pītamuṇḍī</s>, and <s>Gaḍa</s> and <s>Divākara</s>,

children.text: guḍo dāḍakanāmā ca dokaḍiścaiva pippalī // Valc_1.30 //
children.translated_text: <s>Guḍa</s> [and] one named <s>Dāḍaka</s>, and <s>Dokaḍi</s> and <s>Pippalī</s>. // Valc_1.30 //

children.text: vandyo mārttaṇḍanāmā ca brāhmaṇo nāma nāmataḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Vandya</s> [and] one named <s>Mārttaṇḍa</s>, and one named <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>;

children.text: āyāniśca gaṇāyiśca hāḍo gopī ca vandyajāḥ // Valc_1.31 //
children.translated_text: <s>Āyāni</s> and <s>Gaṇāyi</s>, <s>Hāḍa</s> and <s>Gopī</s> — born of <s>Vandya</s>. // Valc_1.31 //

children.text: māṣo dokaḍināmā ca rāyo ca madhusūdanaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Māṣa</s>, one named <s>Dokaḍi</s>, and <s>Rāya</s> and <s>Madhusūdana</s>,

children.text: kuśiko yavanāmā ca haḍo nārāyaṇo 'pi ca // Valc_1.32 //
children.translated_text: <s>Kuśika</s>, one named <s>Yavana</s>, <s>Haḍa</s>, and <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> also. // Valc_1.32 //
<s>Mahintā</s>, one named <s>Dividha</s>, <s>Dāvāri</s>, and <s>Keśava</s>,
<s>Caṭṭa</s>, one named <s>Śakuni</s>, <s>Tailavāṭī</s>, and <s>Nayārika</s>. // Valc_1.33 //
<s>Kunda</s>, one named <s>Viśveśvara</s>, born of <s>Vandya</s>, designated <s>Viṭhu</s>;
born of <s>Ghoṣa</s>, the two brothers <s>Madana</s> and <s>Viśvarūpaka</s>. // Valc_1.34 //

children.text: parāśarākhyaḥ śimlī ca śaṅkaro ḍiṇḍisaṃjñakaḥ // Valc_1.35 /
children.translated_text: one called <s>Parāśara</s>, namely <s>Śimlī</s>, and <s>Śaṅkara</s>, designated <s>Ḍiṇḍi</s>. // Valc_1.35 //
These Brahmins, born of noble Brahmin families, accepted the gift of a cow;

children.text: teṣāṃ sambandhamātreṇa paṅke gauriva sīdati // Valc_1.36 //
children.translated_text: by mere association with them, one sinks like a cow in mud. // Valc_1.36 //
<s>Gāṅguli</s>, one named <s>Hāsya</s>, <s>Pūti</s>, designated <s>Gautama</s>;

children.text: sambandhe bhojane caiva dāne yajñe tathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: In matters of marriage alliance, dining, gifts, sacrifice,

children.text: vidvadbhiḥ śrāddhakāle ca varjjyā ete punaḥ punaḥ // Valc_1.37 //
children.translated_text: and at the time of <s>śrāddha</s> (ancestral rites), these are to be avoided again and again by the learned. // Valc_1.37 //
Thus the names and other details of the <s>Pratigrāhins</s>.
Now, the account of the marriages of the sons of the <s>Pratigrāhins</s>.
By <s>Vaśiṣṭha</s>, the daughter of <s>Gaṇa</s> [was married]; by <s>Ṭoṭa</s>, the daughters of <s>Śakuni</s>;
by <s>Dāyika</s>, the daughter of <s>Hāḍa</s>; <s>Kubera</s> became the husband of <s>Hāsya</s>'s daughter. // Valc_1.38 //
having become the husband of <s>Viṭhu</s>'s daughter, <s>Caṭṭaja</s>, the ornament of his family —
from marrying the sons of <s>Pratigrāhins</s>, these six are known as <s>Vaṃśajas</s> (those of lineage). // Valc_1.39 //
By <s>Cakrapāṇi</s> also, a daughter was taken, out of greed for wealth;

children.text: śrotriyāya sutāṃ dattvā kulīno vaṃśajaḥ punaḥ // Valc_1.40 //
children.translated_text: Having given a daughter to a <s>Śrotriya</s>, a <s>Kulīna</s> [becomes] a <s>Vaṃśaja</s> again. // Valc_1.40 //
Having obtained a village from <s>Vallāla</s>, the <s>Kauṇḍilya</s> was thus established;

children.text: yavagrāmī kaḍāro ca kauṇḍilyo vaiduḍīstathā // Valc_1.41 //
children.translated_text: <s>Yavagrāmī</s>, <s>Kaḍāra</s>, <s>Kauṇḍilya</s>, and <s>Vaiduḍī</s> likewise. // Valc_1.41 //
Thus the account of the marriages of the sons of the <s>Pratigrāhins</s>.
Now, the account of the village-names and other details of the five-<s>gotra</s> [families].
Now, the village-names of the lineage-bearers of <s>Bhaṭṭanārāyaṇa</s> of the <s>Śāṇḍilya</s> <s>gotra</s>:

children.text: ādau vandyo varāhaḥ syāt rāmo gaḍgaḍistathā /
children.translated_text: First <s>Vandya</s>, then <s>Varāha</s>, <s>Rāma</s>, and <s>Gaḍgaḍi</s>,

children.text: nṛpaḥ syāt keśaraścaiva nānaḥ kusumakaulikaḥ // Valc_1.42 //
children.translated_text: <s>Nṛpa</s>, <s>Keśara</s>, <s>Nāna</s>, and <s>Kusumakaulika</s>. // Valc_1.42 //
<s>Vāṭu</s>, then <s>Pārihāla</s>, <s>Kulabhi</s> by name <s>Rguī</s>;

children.text: gaṇo ghoṣalitāṃ prāptaḥ seyuḥ śāṇḍīśvarīstathā // Valc_1.43 //
children.translated_text: <s>Gaṇa</s> reached <s>Ghoṣalitā</s>; <s>Seyu</s> [and] <s>Śāṇḍīśvarī</s> likewise. // Valc_1.43 //
<s>Vuḍomā</s> and <s>Caraka</s>, <s>Vaṭavyāla</s> and <s>Vikarttana</s>,
<s>Vasurāyi</s> and <s>Nīla</s>, <s>Kaḍyāla</s> and <s>Madhusūdana</s>. // Valc_1.44 //

children.text: kuśī ca koyanāmā ca kulisā caiva vāsukaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Kuśī</s> and one named <s>Koya</s>, <s>Kulisā</s> and <s>Vāsuka</s>,

children.text: ākāśo mādhavo dīrghagrāmī caiva mahāmatiḥ // Valc_1.45 //
children.translated_text: <s>Ākāśa</s>, <s>Mādhava</s>, <s>Dīrghagrāmī</s>, and <s>Mahāmati</s>. // Valc_1.45 //
These sixteen of the <s>Śāṇḍilya</s> [gotra] have been declared, honored by the king.
Next, the lineage of <s>Dakṣa</s> of the <s>Kāśyapa</s> <s>gotra</s> is stated. // Valc_1.46 //
Now, the village-names of the lineage-bearers of <s>Dakṣa</s> of the <s>Kāśyapa</s> <s>gotra</s>:
<s>Dhīra</s> was [of] <s>Guḍīgrāmī</s>; <s>Nīra</s> was <s>Āmarūlika</s>;
<s>Bhūriṣṭāla</s> and <s>Śubha</s>, and <s>Śambhu</s> was <s>Tailavāṭika</s>. // Valc_1.47 //
<s>Kautuka</s> was <s>Pītamuṇḍī</s>; <s>Caṭṭagrāmī</s> [was] <s>Sulocana</s>;
<s>Palaśāyī</s> [was] called <s>Pālu</s>; <s>Haḍ</s> [was] known as <s>Kāka</s>. // Valc_1.48 //
<s>Poḍāri</s>, designated <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>; <s>Pāladhī</s>, named <s>Rāma</s>;
one named <s>Jana</s> [was] <s>Koyāri</s>; <s>Parkkaṭi</s> [was] <s>Vanamālika</s>. // Valc_1.49 //
<s>Simalāyī</s> was <s>Śrīhari</s>; <s>Jaṭa</s> was <s>Pūṣalika</s>;
<s>Bhaṭṭagrāmī</s> [was] <s>Śaśidhara</s>; <s>Mūlagrāmī</s> was <s>Keśava</s>.

children.text: ete ṣoḍaśa bhūdevāḥ jñeyāḥ kāśyapasaṃjñakāḥ // Valc_1.50 //
children.translated_text: These sixteen Brahmins are to be known as those of the <s>Kāśyapa</s> [gotra]. // Valc_1.50 //
Now, the village-names of the lineage-bearers of <s>Śrīharṣa</s> of the <s>Bhāradvāja</s> <s>gotra</s>:
<s>Dhāṁdu</s> by name was <s>Mukhaiṭi</s>; <s>Jana</s> was <s>Dīnasāyika</s>;

children.text: nānaḥ sāhariko jñeyo rāyī ca rāmanāmakaḥ // Valc_1.51 //
children.translated_text: <s>Nāna</s> should be known as <s>Sāharika</s>; and <s>Rāyī</s> was named <s>Rāma</s>. // Valc_1.51 //
These are the sons of <s>Śrīharṣa</s>, born of the <s>Bhāradvāja</s> lineage;
these four foremost ones are known in all lands. // Valc_1.52 //
Now, the village-names of the lineage-bearers of <s>Vedagarbha</s> of the <s>Sāvarṇa</s> <s>gotra</s>:
<s>Gāṅgulī</s>, one named <s>Hala</s>, <s>Kunda</s>, and <s>Rājyadhara</s>,

children.text: vaśiṣṭhaḥ siddhalo jñeyo dāyī ca madano bhavat // Valc_1.53 //
children.translated_text: <s>Vaśiṣṭha</s> and <s>Siddhala</s> are to be known; <s>Dāyī</s> and <s>Madana</s>. // Valc_1.53 //
<s>Viśvarūpa</s> and <s>Nandī</s>, <s>Vāligrāmī</s> and <s>Kumāraka</s>;

children.text: yogī siyāriko jñeyaḥ puṃsiko rāmanāmakaḥ // Valc_1.54 //
children.translated_text: <s>Yogī</s> and <s>Siyārika</s> are to be known; <s>Puṃsika</s>, named <s>Rāma</s>. // Valc_1.54 //
<s>Dakṣa</s>, designated <s>Sākaṭa</s>; <s>Pārī</s> and <s>Madhusūdana</s>;
<s>Ghaṇṭāgrāmī</s> and <s>Mādhava</s>; and <s>Nāyārī</s> and <s>Guṇākara</s>.

children.text: ete putrā mahāprājñāḥ sāvarṇā dvādaśa smṛtāḥ // Valc_1.55 //
children.translated_text: These twelve sons of great wisdom are remembered as being of the <s>Sāvarṇa</s> [gotra]. // Valc_1.55 //
Now, the village-names of the lineage-bearers of <s>Chāndaḍa</s> of the <s>Vātsya</s> <s>gotra</s>:

children.text: ravirmahintā surabhiśca ghoṣaḥ kaviḥ pṛthivyāṃ khalu śimbalālaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Ravi</s>, <s>Mahintā</s>, <s>Surabhi</s>, <s>Ghoṣa</s>, <s>Kavi</s>, and on earth <s>Śimbalāla</s>,

children.text: mahāyaśā vāpulikaśca piplī dhīraśca pūtirnanu śaṅkarākhyaḥ // Valc_1.56 //
children.translated_text: <s>Mahāyaśā</s> and <s>Vāpulika</s> and <s>Piplī</s>, <s>Dhīra</s>, and indeed <s>Pūti</s> called <s>Śaṅkara</s>. // Valc_1.56 //

children.text: śrīśrīdharobhūt khalu kāñjivillī nārāyaṇo nāma ca kāñjiyārī /
children.translated_text: <s>Śrīdhara</s> was indeed <s>Kāñjivillī</s>; <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> by name was <s>Kāñjiyārī</s>;

children.text: cautkhaṇḍiko nāma guṇākaraḥ syāt mano dīghālo bhuvi rudratulyaḥ // Valc_1.57 //
children.translated_text: one named <s>Cautkhaṇḍika</s> was <s>Guṇākara</s>; <s>Mana</s> and <s>Dīghāla</s>, on earth, [were] equal to <s>Rudra</s>. // Valc_1.57 //
<s>Viśvambhara</s> was indeed <s>Pūrvagrāmī</s>; and the <s>Vātsyas</s> [settled in] those dwelling-places.
Now, the listing of the secondary <s>Kulīnas</s> (those of noble family).

children.text: dīrghāṅgī pāriḥ kulabhī poḍārī rāiḥ keśarī /
children.translated_text: <s>Dīrghāṅgī</s>, <s>Pāri</s>, <s>Kulabhī</s>, <s>Poḍārī</s>, <s>Rāi</s>, <s>Keśarī</s>,
<s>Ghaṇṭā</s>, <s>Ḍiṇḍi</s>, <s>Pītamuṇḍī</s>, <s>Mahintā</s>, <s>Guḍ</s>, <s>Pippalī</s>,
<s>Haḍ</s> and <s>Gaḍgaḍi</s> — these are declared as the secondary [Kulīnas].

children.text: ataḥparaṃ viśeṣaṃ yadatraiva varṇyate mayā // Valc_1.58 //
children.translated_text: Hereafter, the distinctions in this matter are described by me. // Valc_1.58 //
Once, King <s>Vallāla</s>, for the purpose of establishing the <s>kaulīnya</s> (nobility) system,
summoned the Brahmins for the ceremony of ascending the assembly. // Valc_1.59 //
Having completed their daily rituals, on that appointed day,
all the Brahmins came to the assembly in the presence of the king. // Valc_1.60 //
Some [came] within one <s>prahara</s> (three-hour period), some within one and a half <s>praharas</s>;
some went to the king's presence at two and a half <s>praharas</s>. // Valc_1.61 //
Then the wise king, having examined the conduct of the twice-born,
gave to them joyfully, according to the fitness of their <s>kaulīnya</s> and other [qualities], in that assembly. // Valc_1.62 //
Those twice-born who came to the assembly after two and a half <s>praharas</s> had passed —

children.text: te samparṇūdharmma-niṣṭhāḥ kaulīnyaṃ lebhire dvijāḥ // Valc_1.63 //
children.translated_text: they, being fully devoted to <s>dharma</s>, obtained [the rank of] <s>Kaulīnya</s> (nobility). // Valc_1.63 //
Those who arrived at one and a half <s>praharas</s> are declared as <s>Śrotriyas</s>.
those who passed beyond their allotted watches became secondary <s>kulīnas</s> (lineage-holders). // Valc_1.64 //
In time, they were settled among the pure original <s>śrotriyas</s> (learned Brahmins);
they were known as secondary, bearing the designation of <s>kaṣṭa-śrotriya</s> (inferior śrotriya). // Valc_1.65 //

children.text: yathā gauṇāstathā kaṣṭā heyā eva samaṃ sadā /
children.translated_text: Just as the secondary [lineages] are to be avoided, so too are the <s>kaṣṭa</s> [lineages] — always equally so;
thus has been stated the determination of lineage among the <s>Rāḍhīya</s> Brahmins. // Valc_1.66 //
Thus the account of the attainment of <s>kaulīnya</s> (noble lineage status) and other [distinctions] among the <s>Rāḍhīya</s> Brahmins.
Now the account of the <s>Varendra</s> lineages.
In the <s>Kāśyapa</s> [<s>gotra</s>], eighteen are to be known; in the <s>Śāṇḍilya</s> [<s>gotras</s>], fourteen;
twenty-four of the <s>Vātsyas</s>; likewise in the <s>Bharadvāja</s> [<s>gotra</s>]. // Valc_1.67 //
In the <s>Sāvarṇa</s> [<s>gotra</s>], twenty are to be known — thus the five <s>gotras</s> have been stated;

children.text: teṣāṃ grāmī savistāraṃ kathyate ca yathākramam // Valc_1.68 //
children.translated_text: their village-names are now related in full detail, in proper order. // Valc_1.68 //
Now the village-names of the lineage-bearers of the <s>Kāśyapa gotra</s> of <s>Kṛpānidhi</s>:
<s>Karañja</s>, <s>Bhāduḍī</s>, <s>Maitra</s>, <s>Bāla</s>, <s>Yaṣṭika</s>, <s>Kerala</s>,
<s>Madhugrāmī</s>, <s>Balīhārī</s>, <s>Moyālī</s>, <s>Bījakuñjaka</s>, // Valc_1.69 //
<s>Koṭi</s>, <s>Sarvagrāmakoṭi</s>, <s>Pareśa</s>, and <s>Dhosaka</s>,
<s>Bhadrayāmī</s>, <s>Āśrukoṭi</s>, and the renowned <s>Śaragrāmī</s>,
<s>Velagrāmī</s>, <s>Camagrāma</s> — these are the lineage-holders of <s>Kṛpānidhi</s>. // Valc_1.70 //
Now the village-names of the lineage-bearers of the <s>Śāṇḍilya gotra</s> of <s>Dāmodara</s>:
<s>Rudravāgcī</s>, <s>Sādhuvāgcī</s>, <s>Lāhiḍī</s>, <s>Campaṭi</s> likewise,

children.text: nandanāvāṭī kālindī caṭṭagrāmī ca pūṣaṇaḥ // Valc_1.71 //
children.translated_text: <s>Nandanāvāṭī</s>, <s>Kālindī</s>, <s>Caṭṭagrāmī</s>, and <s>Pūṣaṇa</s>, // Valc_1.71 //
<s>Śihari</s>, <s>Viśī</s>, <s>Matsyāśī</s>, <s>Veluḍī</s>, and [one] named <s>Campa</s>,
<s>Suvarṇatoṭa</s> — these are the lineage-holders of <s>Dāmodara</s> in the <s>Śāṇḍilya</s> [gotra]. // Valc_1.72 //
Now the village-names of the lineage-bearers of the <s>Vātsya gotra</s> of <s>Dharādhara</s>:

children.text: saṃyāminī bhīmakālī bhaṭṭaśālī ca kuḍmuḍiḥ // Valc_1.73 //
children.translated_text: <s>Saṃyāminī</s>, <s>Bhīmakālī</s>, <s>Bhaṭṭaśālī</s>, and <s>Kuḍmuḍi</s>, // Valc_1.73 //
<s>Bhāḍiyāla</s>, <s>Kāmakālī</s>, <s>Vātsyagrāmī</s>, and <s>Lakṣaka</s>,
<s>Voḍgrāmī</s>, <s>Jāmarūkhī</s>, <s>Kālīgrāmī</s>, <s>Kalīhara</s>, // Valc_1.74 //

children.text: śītalī dhosalī caiva tāluḍī kukkuṭī tathā /
children.translated_text: <s>Śītalī</s>, <s>Dhosalī</s> as well, <s>Tāluḍī</s>, <s>Kukkuṭī</s> also,

children.text: nidrālī cākṣuṣagrāmī deuli siharī tathā // Valc_1.75 //
children.translated_text: <s>Nidrālī</s>, <s>Ākṣuṣagrāmī</s>, <s>Deulī</s>, <s>Siharī</s> likewise, // Valc_1.75 //
<s>Prauṇḍrīkākṣi</s>, <s>Śrutavaṭī</s>, and <s>Caturāndī</s> as remembered,
<s>Kālindī</s> — these are the lineage-holders of <s>Dharādhara</s> in the <s>Vātsya gotra</s>. // Valc_1.76 //
Now the village-names of the lineage-bearers of the <s>Bharadvāja gotra</s> of <s>Gautama</s>:

children.text: bhādaḍo lāḍḍela-jhāmā jhāmālī jhampaṭī ca vā /
children.translated_text: <s>Bhādaḍa</s>, <s>Lāḍḍela</s>, <s>Jhāmā</s>, <s>Jhāmālī</s>, <s>Jhampaṭī</s> or likewise,
<s>Urttivāhī</s>, <s>Ugrarekhī</s>, <s>Ākhu</s>, <s>Ratnābalī</s>, <s>Khani</s>, // Valc_1.77 //
<s>Gosvāśirātha</s>, <s>Pisvīni</s>, <s>Ceṅgā</s>, <s>Ākhuri</s>, <s>Pippalī</s>,
<s>Viśālā</s>, <s>Kāñcanagrāmī</s>, <s>Asṛk</s>, <s>Śākoṭaka</s> likewise, // Valc_1.78 //
<s>Kṣetragrāmī</s>, <s>Rājagrāmī</s>, <s>Nandīgrāmī</s>, and <s>Jadhyala</s>,
<s>Pukti</s>, <s>Vṛhatī</s> — among the <s>Bharadvāja gotras</s>, [descended] from <s>Gautama</s>. // Valc_1.79 //
Now the village-names of the lineage-bearers of the <s>Sāvarṇa gotra</s> of <s>Parāśara</s>:
<s>Siṃhaḍālaka</s>, <s>Unduḍī</s>, <s>Śṛṅgī</s>, <s>Pākaḍī</s>, <s>Ledhuḍī</s>,

children.text: dhundhuḍī tātoyā setuḥ kapālī lomapeṭarau // Valc_1.80 //
children.translated_text: <s>Dhundhuḍī</s>, <s>Tātoyā</s>, <s>Setu</s>, <s>Kapālī</s>, <s>Lomapeṭara</s>, // Valc_1.80 //
<s>Pañcavaṭī</s>, <s>Khaṇḍavaṭī</s>, <s>Nikaḍi</s>, and <s>Samudraka</s>,

children.text: puṇḍariko yaśogrāmī ketugrāmī ca viśrutaḥ // Valc_1.81 //
children.translated_text: <s>Puṇḍarīka</s>, <s>Yaśogrāmī</s>, and the renowned <s>Ketugrāmī</s>, // Valc_1.81 //
<s>Puṣpapa</s> and <s>Bhāduṣī</s> as well — these are the <s>Varendra</s> village-names;

children.text: munikalpā amī jātā sāvarṇeṣu parāśarāt // Valc_1.82 //
children.translated_text: these, comparable to sages, were born in the <s>Sāvarṇa</s> [gotra] from <s>Parāśara</s>. // Valc_1.82 //
Now the reason for the <s>Vaidikas</s> (Vedic Brahmins) being devoid of <s>kaulīnya</s> (noble lineage) and the like:
There were Vedic Brahmins who sided with the merchants;
therefore, in anger, the king did not invite them to the assembly. // Valc_1.83 //
Those ascetically wealthy Brahmins, knowers of <s>Brahman</s>, did not desire

children.text: brāhmaṇāḥ brahmavidvāṃso vaidikā iti kecana // Valc_1.84 //
children.translated_text: the grant given by the king — some [known as] <s>Vaidikas</s> (Vedic). // Valc_1.84 //
Thus the account of the <s>Vaidikas</s>' lack of <s>kaulīnya</s> (noble lineage) and the like.
Now the names and <s>gotras</s> of the <s>Kāyasthas</s> (scribal caste) who came from <s>Kānyakubja</s> (Kanauj):
Born in the <s>Kāśyapa gotra</s>, [there was one] named <s>Dakṣa</s>, of great intellect;

children.text: tasya dāso gautamasya gotre daśaratho vasuḥ // Valc_1.85 //
children.translated_text: his servant was <s>Daśaratha</s>, of the <s>Gautama gotra</s>, [and] <s>Vasu</s>. // Valc_1.85 //
Born in the <s>Śāṇḍilya gotra</s>, [there was] <s>Bhaṭṭanārāyaṇa</s>, the scribe;

children.text: tasya saukālino dāso ghoṣajo makarandakaḥ // Valc_1.86 //
children.translated_text: his servant was <s>Saukālina</s>, and <s>Ghoṣaja Makarandaka</s>. // Valc_1.86 //
Renowned among the <s>Bharadvājas</s> was <s>Śrīharṣa</s>, the foremost among sages;

children.text: dāsastasya virāṭākhyaḥ guhakaḥ kāśyapaḥ smṛtaḥ // Valc_1.87 //
children.translated_text: his servant was <s>Virāṭa</s> by name, and <s>Guhaka</s> of the <s>Kāśyapa</s> [gotra] is remembered. // Valc_1.87 //
Designated as being of the <s>Sāvarṇa gotra</s> was <s>Vedagarbha</s>, rich in austerities;
his servant was <s>Mitravaṃśa</s>, of the <s>Viśvāmitra gotra</s>;
the one known as <s>Kālidāsa</s>, born of a <s>Śūdra</s> lineage. // Valc_1.88 //
Born among the <s>Vātsya gotras</s>, [one was] designated as <s>Chāndaḍa</s>;
of the <s>Maudgalya gotra</s>, [there was one] named <s>Datta Puruṣottama</s>;
for the protection of these [families], he came to the <s>Gauḍa</s> (Bengal) region. // Valc_1.89 //

children.text: ye ghoṣavasumitrāstu kulīnāḥ sarvva eva te /
children.translated_text: Those who are <s>Ghoṣa</s>, <s>Vasu</s>, and <s>Mitra</s> — all of them are <s>kulīnas</s> (of noble lineage);
<s>Deva</s>, <s>Datta</s>, <s>Senasiṃha</s>, <s>Pālita</s>, <s>Kara</s>, <s>Guha</s>,
and <s>Dāsa</s> — these eight are middle-ranked; then seventy-two are <s>gharas</s> (householders). // Valc_1.90 //
Eighty <s>maulikas</s> (chief ones) — approved by king <s>Vallālasena</s>;

children.text: dvisaptatirgharā ye te kāyastheṣvadhamāḥ smṛtāḥ // Valc_1.91 //
children.translated_text: those seventy-two <s>gharas</s> are considered the lowest among the <s>Kāyasthas</s>. // Valc_1.91 //
Now the praise of virtuous <s>Kāyasthas</s>:

children.text: śūdrāstu ye dānaparā bhavanti vratānvitā vipraparāyaṇāśca /
children.translated_text: Those <s>Śūdras</s> who are devoted to charity, who observe vows, and who are dedicated to Brahmins —

children.text: annaṃ hi teṣāṃ satataṃ subhojyaṃ bhavet dvijair dṛṣṭam idaṃ purātanaiḥ // Valc_1.92 //
children.translated_text: the food of such ones is always fit to be eaten; this was seen by the ancient twice-born. // Valc_1.92 //
Thus is completed the first section (<s>Pūrvakhaṇḍa</s>) in the <s>Vallālacarita</s> composed by <s>Ānandabhaṭṭa</s>.

<s>Vallālacaritam</s>
Latter Section (<s>Uttarakhaṇḍa</s>)
Now the first chapter:
The <s>Vallālacarita</s>, the first section, has been narrated by me;
now hear — in the latter section, it is told in detail. // Valc_2,1.1 //
The renowned king named <s>Vallāla</s>, bearer of the <s>Sena</s> dynasty,
formerly enjoyed this earth, his rule undiminished in power. // Valc_2,1.2 //
Though the lord was still in his youth, there was discernment in him;

children.text: nāhāri brāhmaṇī kanyā kadācidapi bhūbhṛtā // Valc_2,1.3
children.translated_text: never did the king take a Brahmin maiden [in marriage]. // Valc_2,1.3 //
Though licentious and proud, he was a servant of his beloved;
never did the king become a paramour of other men's wives. // Valc_2,1.4 //
A <s>Caṇḍāla</s> (outcaste) girl of twelve years was enjoyed by the king,
and an actress-girl too — for the purpose of [tantric] accomplishment, following a heterodox doctrine. // Valc_2,1.5 //
Until the king was instructed by the revered <s>Bhaṭṭa</s> (learned Brahmin),

children.text: tāvat sa kṛtavān karmma tattat sajjanagarhitam // Valc_2,1.6 //
children.translated_text: until then he performed various deeds censured by good people. // Valc_2,1.6 //
Then, following the <s>Bhaṭṭa</s>'s vows, with purified mind,

children.text: kiṃ kiṃ nānuṣṭhitaṃ karmma brāhmaṇānāṃ priyaṅkaram // Valc_2,1.7 //
children.translated_text: what deed pleasing to Brahmins did he not perform? // Valc_2,1.7 //
<s>Vaṅga</s>, <s>Bāgaḍa</s> (Bāgḍī), <s>Varendra</s>, <s>Rāḍhā</s>, and <s>Mithilā</s> also —
his was this vast kingdom of five regions. // Valc_2,1.8 //

children.text: vasatisma nṛpaḥ śrīmān purā gauḍe purottame /
children.translated_text: The glorious king formerly resided in <s>Gauḍa</s> (Bengal), the best of cities,

children.text: kadācidvā yathākāmaṃ nagare vikrame pure // Valc_2,1.9 //
children.translated_text: or sometimes at will in the city of <s>Vikramapura</s>. // Valc_2,1.9 //
Sometimes in <s>Svarṇagrāma</s> (Gold Village), in an exceedingly beautiful palace,
enjoying himself with royal splendors, like the lord of the three heavens (<s>Indra</s>) in heaven. // Valc_2,1.10 //
Learned in the recreational arts and [skilled] on horseback,

children.text: śastrāsteṣu paraṃ dakṣo dāne karṇa ivāparaḥ // Valc_2,1.11 //
children.translated_text: supremely adept in weapons and missiles, and in generosity, like another <s>Karṇa</s>. // Valc_2,1.11 //
Thus, in the <s>Vallālacarita</s> composed by <s>Ānandabhaṭṭa</s>, [ends] the first chapter named 'The Introduction of <s>Vallāla</s>.'
Now the second chapter:
The king, desiring to conquer the lord of <s>Purodantapura</s>,
obtained one crore (<s>koṭi</s>) from the wealthy <s>Vallabhānanda</s>, by kindling [his generosity]. // Valc_2,2.1 //

children.text: vāraṃ vāraṃ jito rājā yato maṇipurāhave /
children.translated_text: Since the king was defeated again and again in the battle of <s>Maṇipura</s>,
he was determined to undertake a terrible military expedition. // Valc_2,2.2 //
Even though <s>Vallabha</s> was unwilling to give, seeing the breach of agreement,

children.text: preṣayāmāsa dūtaṃ sa vaṇijāya mahātmane // Valc_2,2.3 //
children.translated_text: [the king] dispatched a messenger to the great-souled merchant. // Valc_2,2.3 //
That messenger approached <s>Vallabha</s>, who was stationed at <s>Saṅkakoṭa</s>,
and communicated the royal decree of King <s>Vallāla</s>. // Valc_2,2.4 //
<s>Vallāla</s> said:

children.text: yathāsmābhi rhi karttavyaṃ saṃyānaṃ prati kīkaṭam /
children.translated_text: Since we must undertake a military march against <s>Kīkaṭa</s> (Magadha),
making great preparations, with forces equipped with the six divisions, // Valc_2,2.5 //
therefore let <s>Vallabhacandra</s>, upon receiving the life-giving letter,

children.text: preṣayan tu sārddhakoṭiṃ suvarṇamiti māciram // Valc_2,2.6 //
children.translated_text: promptly send one and a half crore in gold. // Valc_2,2.6 //
<s>Vallabha</s> said:
The king, being an unlimited spender, has imposed a <s>kālikā</s> (emergency levy) upon me at once;

children.text: kiṃ brūmo nṛpatiṃ naivaṃ mayā dṛṣṭaḥ satāṃ vidhiḥ // Valc_2,2.7 //
children.translated_text: what shall I say — I have never seen such a practice among the virtuous from a king. // Valc_2,2.7 //
Why indeed this zeal for war? The protection of what has been obtained,
of the kingdom itself, is the proper course — this war is without cause. // Valc_2,2.8 //
Let the disposition of invading villages be abandoned, for the welfare of the subjects;
war causes the destruction of subjects, is unrighteous, and leads to hell. // Valc_2,2.9 //
A king who acts by whim does not see the <s>rājadharma</s> (royal duty);

children.text: arakṣaṇe mahaddoṣaḥ kiṃ guṇo rāṣṭravarddhanaiḥ // Valc_2,2.10 //
children.translated_text: in failing to protect, there is great fault — what use are those who merely expand the kingdom? // Valc_2,2.10 //
Whether a <s>Kṣatriya</s> devoted to the Lord, or a pestle [serving as] a bow —

children.text: na ko 'pi puruṣaḥ karttuṃ kadācidbhavati prabhuḥ // Valc_2,2.11 //
children.translated_text: no man is ever master [enough] to accomplish [everything by force alone]. // Valc_2,2.11 //
A king who, without protecting his subjects, merely takes tribute,
obtains great infamy and indeed goes to hell. // Valc_2,2.12 //
Thus say the treasury officials — what is the use of debating statecraft?

children.text: rājanīti rhi vijñeyaṃ śatrūṇāṃ parimardanam // Valc_2,2.13 //
children.translated_text: Statecraft, indeed, should be understood as the crushing of enemies. // Valc_2,2.13 //
Or rather, since people like us are afflicted by wars,

children.text: ulapā iva sāmānyā bravīmi tena hetunā // Valc_2,2.14 //
children.translated_text: [we who are] like ordinary grass — I speak for this reason. // Valc_2,2.14 //
If the king would give [protection] accompanied by a tax-collection [arrangement],

children.text: ādhitve harikelīyaṃ ṛṇaṃ dātuṃ tadotsahe // Valc_2,2.15 //
children.translated_text: I would be willing to pay the debt owed from <s>Harikelī</s> (coconut trade). // Valc_2,2.15 //

children.text: tasya tadbhāṣitaṃ sarvvaṃ sa dūtaḥ śrāntavāhanaḥ /
children.translated_text: All those words of his, that messenger, with his vehicle exhausted,
having come to the city of <s>Vikrama</s>, reported to <s>Vallāla</s>. // Valc_2,2.16 //
Having heard this message, the king <s>Vallāla</s>,

children.text: manyunā sa prajajvāla kuṭaṅko vahninā yathā // Valc_2,2.17 //
children.translated_text: blazed with fury like a furnace with fire. // Valc_2,2.17 //
Then from his face, reddened with anger, flowed torrents of sweat,
like moisture dripping from firewood being burned by the contact of fire. // Valc_2,2.18 //
Enraged at <s>Vallabha</s>, and also at the innocent merchants,

children.text: kruddho bhūtvā sa vallālaḥ cakāra kadanaṃ bhṛśam // Valc_2,2.19 //
children.translated_text: having become furious, <s>Vallāla</s> wrought terrible havoc. // Valc_2,2.19 //
Even under the pretext of [collecting] customs duties, he forcibly seized

children.text: vyavahāre dhṛtaṃ vastu keṣāñcit krośatāmapi // Valc_2,2.20 //
children.translated_text: the goods held in trade from certain [merchants], even as they cried out. // Valc_2,2.20 //
Though marriage with one of unequal <s>varṇa</s> (caste) is forbidden even in the <s>Kali</s> age,

children.text: govindāḍhyasya kanyāṃ sa jahāra vaṇijo balāt // Valc_2,2.21 //
children.translated_text: the king forcibly seized the daughter of the merchant <s>Govindāḍhya</s>. // Valc_2,2.21 //
<s>Nahardeva</s> too, following the example of the <s>Sauvarṇas</s> (gold-merchants),

children.text: kulavṛddhaiḥ sahāgatya nāpi pratyagrahīcca tam // Valc_2,2.22 //
children.translated_text: came together with the clan elders but did not accept him [the king's demands]. // Valc_2,2.22 //

children.text: tataḥ sa mantrayan rājā gūḍhṃ cāṭuviṭaiḥ saha /
children.translated_text: Then the king, secretly plotting together with flatterers and rogues,
persecuted the merchants and said this to the messenger: // Valc_2,2.22 //
<s>Vallāla</s> said:
The <s>Suvarṇa</s> (gold-dealing) merchants in the kingdom are ill-mannered and proud of their wealth;

children.text: brāhmaṇān te tūlayanti brahmakṣatrañca māmapi // Valc_2,2.23 //
children.translated_text: they disregard the Brahmins, the warrior class, and even me! // Valc_2,2.23 //
And the one named <s>Vallabhānanda</s>, the chief among the merchant community,
is ill-mannered, boastful of his birth, and especially deceitful. // Valc_2,2.24 //
Having falsely attributed these and very many other faults to the merchants,

children.text: vallabhāya saṅkakoṭe rājā dūtaṃ vyasarjayat // Valc_2,2.25 //
children.translated_text: the king dispatched a messenger to <s>Vallabha</s> at <s>Saṅkakoṭa</s>. // Valc_2,2.25 //

children.text: āsedhaṃ vipulaṃ cakre bhayaṃ maitraṃ ca darśayan /
children.translated_text: He imposed extensive restrictions, displaying both fear and friendliness,

children.text: yena kena prakāreṇa taṃ vaśīkaraṇecchayā // Valc_2,2.26 //
children.translated_text: by whatever means, with the desire to bring him under control. // Valc_2,2.26 //
He then collected taxes unjustly at double the [usual] rate,
and repeatedly extorted bride-price under the pretext of tolls. // 2.27 //
Thus, in the <s>Vallālacarita</s> composed by <s>Ānandabhaṭṭa</s>, ends the second chapter named 'The Oppression of the Merchants.'
Now the third chapter.
One day, mounting a swift horse, the king, by chance,
set out toward the beautiful forest of <s>Dhavaleśvarī</s>. // 3.1 //
Wandering along charming banks, forests, and sandy shores,
he beheld a woman strolling along the riverbank. // 3.2 //
She had round, budding, firm, and closely-set breasts,
which the beautiful-eyed one was covering shyly with the edge of her garment. // 3.3 //
With lovely hair, pure teeth, a young woman with a lotus-like face,
slender-limbed, of exceedingly soft limbs, with a fine nose and a gentle smile, // 3.4 //
endowed with broad, abundant hips, with beautiful cheeks, captivating —

children.text: sa hitāmekayā sakhyā sthalajāmiva padminīm // Valc_2,3.5 //
children.translated_text: accompanied by a single friend, like a land-lotus. // 3.5 //
From the playful lotus-face of that supremely beautiful woman,
the bee-like eyes of the king drank the nectar of her loveliness. // 3.6 //
Pierced in every limb by her maddening sidelong glance, the king,

children.text: tāṃ vilokya yayau tūrṇaṃ manmathasya vidheyatām // Valc_2,3.7 //
children.translated_text: upon seeing her, quickly fell under the sway of <s>Manmatha</s> (Love). // 3.7 //
Approaching that beautiful-hipped, lotus-eyed woman,
gazing at her standing there without blinking, he spoke these words: // 3.8 //
'With your eyes you have surpassed the blue lotus, with your face the [golden] lotus,
with your teeth the <s>kunda</s> flower, with your lips the ripe <s>bimba</s> fruit;
with your body you have put to shame the golden <s>campaka</s> and plantain —
who are you, like a forest goddess on the bank of this river in the forest? // 3.9 //
The king said:
'I, whose lotus-feet are served by hosts of feudatory lords,
who am the cause of widowhood for the beautiful wives of enemies,
King <s>Vallālasena</s>, O jasmine-toothed one,
have come under your sway — cast your glance upon me!' // 3.10 //
Hearing that, she, her passion aroused but concealing her feelings,
her face slightly downcast, spoke to the king in a soft voice: // 3.11 //
The maiden said:
'Do not speak thus, O lord of the earth, to me, a maiden;

children.text: vaṃśaḥ kva te vidhubhavaḥ kvaca sambhavo me // Valc_2,3.12 //
children.translated_text: where is your lineage — descended from the moon — and where is my birth? // 3.12 //
'I am known in the world as the daughter of a leather-worker;
I, being of low birth, am not worthy of being married by you.' // 3.13 //
The king said:
'Why do you delude me, O girl, by calling yourself a leather-worker's daughter?

children.text: carmmāryyā īdṛśaṃ rūpaṃ kiṃ syāt bhuvanamohanam // Valc_2,3.14 //
children.translated_text: Would such a world-enchanting beauty belong to a leather-worker's family? // 3.14 //

children.text: carmmārasya nāsi kanyā pālakaḥ sa tu kevalam /
children.translated_text: 'You are not the daughter of a leather-worker — he is merely your guardian;

children.text: rājakanyāsi bhadre tvaṃ dhruvameva na saṃśayaḥ // Valc_2,3.15 //
children.translated_text: you are a princess, O blessed one — that is certain, without doubt. // 3.15 //

children.text: ko vā kāpuruṣo loke bhavedīdṛk varānane /
children.translated_text: 'What wretched man in the world, O beautiful-faced one,

children.text: yastvāṃ nidhimiva prāpyāmūlyaṃ karagataṃ tyajet // Valc_2,3.16 //
children.translated_text: would abandon you, a priceless treasure that has come into his hands? // 3.16 //
'Whether you are of noble birth or low birth, you alone are dear to my heart;

children.text: āyāhi tvaṃ mayā sārddhaṃ tvāṃ nayāmi nijaṃ puram // Valc_2,3.17 //
children.translated_text: come with me — I shall take you to my own city.' // 3.17 //
Hearing those words of the king, she, with averted eyes,

children.text: sā sakhīṃ nodayāmāsa vaktuṃ tatrocitaṃ tadā // Valc_2,3.18 //
children.translated_text: prompted her friend to speak what was appropriate at that moment: // 3.18 //
The friend said:
'If you have firmly resolved to take her hand in marriage by proper rite,

children.text: tadaināṃ naya te sārddhameṣātmānaṃ dadāti te // Valc_2,3.19 //
children.translated_text: then take her with you — she gives herself to you.' // 3.19 //
The king said:
'By the <s>Gāndharva</s> rite of marriage, this woman who has chosen her own husband is obtained by me;

children.text: patitvena bhavāmyasyā iyaṃ me jīviteśvarī // Valc_2,3.20 //
children.translated_text: I become her husband, and she is the mistress of my life.' // 3.20 //

children.text: ityuktvā korikanyāṃ sa punareva jagāda tām /
children.translated_text: Having said this, he addressed the leather-worker's daughter once again,
his face blooming with the fullness of supreme bliss: // 3.21 //
The king said:

children.text: cala mama sākaṃ bhava mama bhāryyā svārohedaṃ varayānam /
children.translated_text: 'Come with me, become my wife; mount this excellent vehicle;

children.text: avarodhe svāminī ca bhava mama caivāntaḥpurāṇām // Valc_2,3.22 //
children.translated_text: and be the mistress of my royal harem, the sovereign of my inner chambers.' // 3.22 //
Having spoken thus, smiling, he took hold of her, trembling,

children.text: sasakhīṃ yāpya yānena nināya vikramaṃ puram // Valc_2,3.23 //
children.translated_text: and together with her friend, conveying them in a carriage, he brought them to the city of <s>Vikrama</s>. // 3.23 //

children.text: bubhuje kāmato rājā rājakṛtye hatādaraḥ // Valc_2,3.24 //
children.translated_text: the king enjoyed her at will, heedless of royal duties. // 3.24 //
Then, having installed that woman of faultless limbs in his own palace,
Exceedingly pampered by the king, that leather-worker's girl
enjoyed the breeze of waving <s>cāmaras</s> (fly-whisks) in the midst of the harem. // 3.25 //

children.text: śuddhāntagatayā sārddhaṃ viharan sa tayā sukham /
children.translated_text: Sporting happily with her, who had entered the inner chambers,
the king did not even notice the great passage of time. // 3.26 //
Thus, in the <s>Vallālacarita</s> composed by <s>Ānandabhaṭṭa</s>, ends the third chapter named 'The Meeting with the Beautiful Woman.'
The Fourth Chapter.
Then, after some time, eager for the gem of amorous sport,
the king entered the inner chambers one day at the onset of night. // 4.1 //
Entering the bedchamber, he saw his beloved lying on the ground,
her delicate body like a creeper torn from its roots. // 4.2 //
Her face covered with her garment, weeping — that lotus-eyed one,
who did not deserve such sorrow, dearer to him than his own life. // 4.3 //
Seeing her, her appearance haggard, rolling on the floor,

children.text: jughūrṇa mastakaṃ tasya netrābhyāṃ dadṛśe tamaḥ // Valc_2,4.4 //
children.translated_text: his head reeled and darkness appeared before his eyes. // 4.4 //
The king, astonished, wiped the water born from her eyes
and, deeply agitated, spoke these words in fear: // 4.5 //
The king said:
'What is this, O doe-eyed one — water flowing from your eyes?

children.text: avāṅmukhī kimarthaṃ tvaṃ bhūmāveva viluṇṭhase // Valc_2,4.6 //
children.translated_text: Why do you lie face-down, rolling on the ground? // 4.6 //
'I have not done anything displeasing to you, O beautiful one;

children.text: krandanena duḥkhayase kathaṃ māṃ tanumadhyame // Valc_2,4.7 //
children.translated_text: why do you cause me pain with this weeping, O slender-waisted one? // 4.7 //
'Why, O one of radiant smile, do you not accept
the saffron-dyed garment, the golden locket, O lovely-hipped one with gem-studded breasts? // 4.8 //
'Your hair has not been arranged, O fair-browed one, with fragrant jasmine garlands;

children.text: kucayoścandralekheva patrāṅkā ca na kāritā // Valc_2,4.9 //
children.translated_text: nor have decorative leaf-marks been painted on your breasts, like a crescent moon. // 4.9 //
'Your finest garment, which once shone from the contact of your hips,

children.text: śobhitaṃ nādhunā bhūmau patitaṃ tadvirājate // Valc_2,4.10 //
children.translated_text: now lies fallen on the ground and no longer gleams. // 4.10 //

children.text: maktāvalī bhrājate na cyutā tava kucadvayāt /
children.translated_text: 'Your pearl necklace does not sparkle, having slipped from your pair of breasts;
the neck ornament has fallen from your throat and has become a non-ornament. // 4.11 //
'With your face whose smile surpasses the beauty of the moonlight of the full moon,

children.text: kiṃ no vadasi vaktena kuśeśayasugandhinā // Valc_2,4.12 //
children.translated_text: fragrant as a lotus — why do you not speak to me? // 4.12 //
'In every way, O lotus-petal-eyed one, I am obedient to your words;

children.text: pratīkṣante tavādeśaṃ majjanāśca sadā priye // Valc_2,4.13 //
children.translated_text: my subjects too always await your command, O beloved. // 4.13 //
'Why do you not command me as before, O one who speaks with a smiling preamble?

children.text: prapannaṃ prapade prāptaṃ dāsaṃ himakarānane // Valc_2,4.14 //
children.translated_text: I have come to your feet, a surrendered one, a servant, O moon-faced one. // 4.14 //

children.text: tvattvaḥ priyatarā nānyā varttate mama sundari /
children.translated_text: 'There is no woman dearer to me than you, O beautiful one;

children.text: tvaṃ hi me jīvanaṃ prāṇāḥ tvaṃ hi me paramā gatiḥ // Valc_2,4.15 //
children.translated_text: you are my life, my vital breath; you are my supreme refuge. // 4.15 //
'Revive me with words that are nectar to the ears, O one of beautiful smiles;
me, a <s>Kāyastha</s> and yet no <s>Kāyastha</s> [i.e., one who possesses a body yet is as good as dead] — seemingly alive yet dead. // 4.16 //
'I shall give a hundred thousand [coins] to the slave-girl who inspires trust in you, O trustworthy one;

children.text: ratnālaṅkārabhāraṃ vā yatte manasi varttate // Valc_2,4.17 //
children.translated_text: or a load of jeweled ornaments — whatever is in your mind. // 4.17 //
'I would even abandon <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> [my kingdom] for your sake, O beautiful-faced one;

children.text: gāṅgeyaṃ sāgaraṃ bāle praviśeyam hutāśanam // Valc_2,4.18 //
children.translated_text: I would dive into the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, the ocean, or even enter fire, O maiden. // 4.18 //
'What is the reason for your distress, O mistress of my life? Tell me;

children.text: tatpriyaṃ prākariṣyāmi śape te lalitāṅghriṇā // Valc_2,4.19 //
children.translated_text: I shall do what pleases you — I swear by your graceful feet. // 4.19 //

children.text: nirīkṣase kiṃ na subhru preṣya māṃ tava sundari /
children.translated_text: 'Why do you not look at me, O fair-browed one? I am your servant, O beautiful one;
by whom have you been slighted? Who dares to be a moth before the fire? // 4.20 //
'What rich man should be made poor? What powerful man be reduced to powerlessness?

children.text: ko vaddho mucyatāmadya ko 'vadhyo vā nihanyatām // Valc_2,4.21 //
children.translated_text: What prisoner should be released today? Who, though inviolable, should be slain?' // 4.21 //
Having heard these words of his, who was under the sway of love,

children.text: sābhimānavatī rājñaḥ sthitā natamukhī tadā // Valc_2,4.22 //
children.translated_text: she, full of wounded pride, stood before the king with bowed face. // 4.22 //
The beautiful woman, her face turned aside, her gaze slightly averted,

children.text: sakṛdvilokya nṛpatiṃ tasthau natamukhī punaḥ // Valc_2,4.23 //
children.translated_text: glanced once at the king and again stood with lowered face. // 4.23 //
With breasts heaving firm from sighs, with quivering <s>bimba</s>-like lips, then,
wiping her tears with the edge of her garment, she spoke in a faltering voice: // 4.24 //
<s>Padmākṣī</s> (Lotus-eyed) said:

children.text: yadi te matpriyaṃ kāryyaṃ māṃ preṣaya piturgṛham /
children.translated_text: 'If you wish to do what is dear to me, send me to my father's house —
me, who deserves suffering, a sorrowful woman, a wanderer in the wilderness. // 4.25 //
'Forget me, the enjoyable, the wretched one, and even my very name;

children.text: rājyaṃ bhuṅkṣva mahārāja māṃ vihāya sukhaṃ sadā // Valc_2,4.26 //
children.translated_text: enjoy your kingdom, O great king, always in happiness without me. // 4.26 //
'You have obtained great suffering on my account, O king;
in every region, O beloved, you bear disgrace because of me. // 4.27 //
'The nature of kings, princes, wise men of noble birth —

children.text: purā nājñāsiṣaṃ nātha prakṛtiṃ vanacāriṇī // Valc_2,4.28 //
children.translated_text: I did not know before, O lord, being a forest-dweller. // 4.28 //
'Today, having come to know the ways of the world, O king —

children.text: jīveyaṃ yadi paśyeyaṃ tadā kiṃ kiṃ na kilbiṣam // Valc_2,4.29 //
children.translated_text: if I were to live and witness [it all], then what sin would there not be? // 4.29 //
'I have no need for wealth or for ornaments and the like;
falling into the <s>Dhavaleśvarī</s> [river], I would surely drown. // 4.30 //
As she lamented thus, King <s>Vallāla</s>, the protector of the earth,
as if drawing her into his breast, spoke to her again: // 4.31 //
The king said:

children.text: śiro me ghūrṇate jāye vadanañca viśuṣyati /
children.translated_text: 'My head reels, my mouth goes dry, O wife;

children.text: kimu tatkāraṇaṃ yasmāt tvamevaṃ bhṛśamākulā // Valc_2,4.32 //
children.translated_text: what is the cause, that you are so exceedingly distressed? // 4.32 //

children.text: tvaṃ hi me jīvanaṃ patni tvaṃ hi me paramaṃ tapaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'You are my life, O wife; you are my supreme austerity;

children.text: tvameva me rājadharmmaḥ prāṇānāmīśvarī ca me // Valc_2,4.33 //
children.translated_text: you are my royal duty; you are the sovereign of my very breath. // 4.33 //

children.text: tvayā hīnaṃ na kāṅkṣeyaṃ kāñcīśatvamapi priye /
children.translated_text: 'Deprived of you, I would not desire even sovereignty over <s>Kāñcī</s>, O beloved;

children.text: tvayā saha viśālākṣi vane vāso varaṃ mama // Valc_2,4.34 //
children.translated_text: with you, O wide-eyed one, dwelling in the forest is better for me. // 4.34 //

children.text: prāṇā api mayā śakyāstyaktuṃ na tvāṃ kadācana /
children.translated_text: 'I could give up even my life-breath, but never you;

children.text: śaknuyāmasitāpāṅgi kalaṅkeṣu ca kā kathā // Valc_2,4.35 //
children.translated_text: I am able [to bear anything], O dark-eyed one — what need to speak of mere calumnies? // 4.35 //
'O great queen, why do you not show compassion to your husband, who has fallen at your feet?
I adjure you by my very life — speak, O beauty of the three worlds! // 4.36 //

children.text: tvameva mahiṣī rājñi bharttāhaṃ te mahāguruḥ /
children.translated_text: 'You are indeed the chief queen, O sovereign; I am your husband, your greatest authority;
tell me the feeling in your heart — here I stand with palms joined. // 4.37 //

children.text: patāmi tvatpadau mūrddhnā kasmānna dayase patim /
children.translated_text: 'I fall at your feet with my head — why do you not show mercy to your husband,
who is devoted to you, unattached to others? Be gracious, O lotus-eyed one! // 4.38 //
As the king was speaking thus, that lotus-eyed woman
spoke harsh words, sighing again and again: // 4.39 //
The queen said:

children.text: avaktavyamapi svāmin tvāṃ vadāmi śṛṇa prabho /
children.translated_text: 'What should not be spoken, O lord, I shall tell you — hear me, O master;

children.text: ākarṇya ca prāṇanātha yatkarttavyaṃ tadācara // Valc_2,4.40 //
children.translated_text: and having heard, O lord of my life, do what must be done. // 4.40 //

children.text: bharttā hi rakṣakaḥ strīṇāṃ yuvatīnāṃ viśeṣataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'A husband is indeed the protector of women, of young women especially;

children.text: bharttāraṃ yadi no vacmi kaṃ vadāmi sayauvanā // Valc_2,4.41 //
children.translated_text: if I do not tell my husband, whom shall I tell, being in my youth? // 4.41 //
'A husband is the refuge of women, a husband is the supreme deity;

children.text: brāhmaṇasya mukhāt pitrālaye deva mayā śrutam // Valc_2,4.42 //
children.translated_text: from the mouth of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, at my father's home, O lord, I have heard: // 4.42 //
'"Devotion to one's husband is the highest <s>dharma</s> that women possess" —
I would never transgress you, even in my mind. // 4.43 //
'I am not like a common woman, devoid of devotion to her husband;
establishing you on the lotus-throne of my heart, I always worship you. // 4.44 //
By whom I am always honored with prostrations and devotion —
by him, that wretch of low conduct and wrong ways, I have been dishonored. // <s>Valc</s> 2,4.45 //

children.text: dhik taṃ sa kilviṣācāraḥ kāmāndho vyatthitendriyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Shame upon him! That sinner of wicked conduct, blinded by lust, with uncontrolled senses,

children.text: mātaraṃ yaḥ kāmayate durātmā māṃ pativratām // Valc_2,4.46 //
children.translated_text: that evil-souled one who lusts after his own mother, me, a devoted wife! // <s>Valc</s> 2,4.46 //
Today, O lord, I went to the bathing chamber;
seeing me alone, that one followed me, grinning. // <s>Valc</s> 2,4.47 //

children.text: bhītayā yanmayāhūtā sakhī tatra drutaṃ gatā /
children.translated_text: Because I, in fear, called a companion who quickly came there,

children.text: tato duṣṭātmanā nātha na tena malinīkṛtā // Valc_2,4.48 //
children.translated_text: therefore, O lord, I was not defiled by that evil-souled one. // <s>Valc</s> 2,4.48 //

children.text: dharmeṇa rakṣitā sāhaṃ tvām vadāmi yathāyatham /
children.translated_text: Protected by <s>dharma</s>, I tell you exactly as it happened;

children.text: kampante mama gātrāṇi smṛtvā tasya kuceṣṭitam // Valc_2,4.49 //
children.translated_text: my limbs tremble when I recall his wicked behavior. // <s>Valc</s> 2,4.49 //
I am terrified of that one of despicable conduct; I, being unprotected,
shall perish like an army without a commander that has gone to the battlefield. // <s>Valc</s> 2,4.50 //
Having spoken these terrible words, the cruel wife of <s>Vallāla</s>
fell silent, shedding tears upon her husband's chest. // <s>Valc</s> 2,4.51 //
Hearing those words fallen from the lotus-face of his beloved,
the king blazed with anger, like a mountain ablaze with a forest fire. // <s>Valc</s> 2,4.52 //
Then, as the enraged king's face resembled that of a barbarian,
his pair of eyes reddened, his entire body trembling. // <s>Valc</s> 2,4.53 //
<s>Vallāla</s>, promising punishment of his son,

children.text: putre daṇḍaṃ pratijñāya sāntvayāmāsa viklavām // Valc_2,4.54 //
children.translated_text: then consoled his distressed wife, she of elephant-like thighs. // <s>Valc</s> 2,4.54 //
Brooding upon his son's misconduct, the king, agitated with anger upon his bed,
somehow passed that night awake. // <s>Valc</s> 2,4.55 //
Thus ends the fourth chapter, named 'The Appeasement of the Beloved,' in the <s>Vallālacarita</s> composed by <s>Ānandabhaṭṭa</s>.
Now begins the fifth chapter.
Rising at dawn, the king, greatly summoning his wrath,
secretly ordered assassins to kill his dear son. // <s>Valc</s> 2,5.1 //
Hearing the order for his own execution, the wretched <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> then

children.text: vyākulo mantrayāmāsa kāntayā saha nirjjane // Valc_2,5.2 //
children.translated_text: in great distress consulted with his wife in private. // <s>Valc</s> 2,5.2 //
As the night deepened, having privately bid farewell to his wife,
he boarded a secret boat and fled in great fear. // <s>Valc</s> 2,5.3 //
When dawn broke, learning of his flight,
the king went to the fortress, his eyes wide with anxiety. // <s>Valc</s> 2,5.4 //
Entering the palace there, the king upon the wall
saw a verse inscribed by his daughter-in-law and read it himself: // <s>Valc</s> 2,5.5 //
"Rain falls unceasingly, peacocks dance with joy;

children.text: adya kāntaḥ kṛtānto vā duḥkhasyāntaṃ kariṣyati // Valc_2,5.6 //
children.translated_text: today either my beloved or Death will put an end to my sorrow." // <s>Valc</s> 2,5.6 //
Having read this verse, King <s>Vallāla</s>, the lord of the earth,
his heart wavering with affection for his son, summoned the fishermen. // <s>Valc</s> 2,5.7 //
To them who had arrived, the king said: "Listen, O you who live by boating!

children.text: matpriyaṃ yadi karttavyaṃ śrayatāṃ vacanaṃ mama // Valc_2,5.8 //
children.translated_text: If you would do what pleases me, heed my words: // <s>Valc</s> 2,5.8 //
My son <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, bearing marks of anger, has departed from here;
I shall give you whatever you desire — search for him and bring him back at once!" // <s>Valc</s> 2,5.9 //
The boatmen said:
"Whether on a mountain, in a cave, in a fortress, in a wilderness, on the lord of waters,
or in the netherworld — we shall bring him back without delay wherever he may be!" // <s>Valc</s> 2,5.10 //
Having spoken thus and saluted the king, the boatmen joyfully

children.text: ānetuṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ jagmuḥ kṛtvā kolāhalaṃ bhṛśam // Valc_2,5.11 //
children.translated_text: set out to bring back <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, raising a great clamor. // <s>Valc</s> 2,5.11 //
Driving a large vessel swiftly with seventy-two oars,
the fisherfolk brought <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> back in two days. // <s>Valc</s> 2,5.12 //
Then the king, his face bright with satisfaction, gave them
loads of wealth, gems, and garments, as well as farming land for their livelihood. // <s>Valc</s> 2,5.13 //
Thus ends the fifth chapter, named 'The Bringing Back of <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>,' in the <s>Vallālacarita</s> composed by <s>Ānandabhaṭṭa</s>.
Now begins the sixth chapter.

children.text: athāsti śaivaiḥ sakalaiśca śāktaiḥ sauraistathā vaiṣṇavagāṇapatyaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Now there is one always venerated by all <s>Śaivas</s>, <s>Śāktas</s>, <s>Sauras</s>, <s>Vaiṣṇavas</s>, and followers of <s>Gaṇapati</s>,
by female and male lay devotees, and by ascetics with staffs, by mendicant monks and nuns: // <s>Valc</s> 2,6.1 //

children.text: vipraiśca kṣetraiḥ varigajaiśca śūdraiḥ sannyāsibhi rmānuṣamānuṣībhiḥ /
children.translated_text: by <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, <s>Vaiśyas</s> with their elephants, and <s>Śūdras</s>, by renunciants, by men and women —

children.text: sarvvaiśca pūjyo varadaḥ prasiddha u mādhavograḥ kila devadevaḥ // Valc_2,6.2 //
children.translated_text: worshiped by all, the boon-granting, renowned, fierce <s>Mādhava</s> (<s>Ugramādhava</s>), the God of Gods. // <s>Valc</s> 2,6.2 //

children.text: gatāḥ sma pūjituṃ devaṃ mānavā ugramādhavam // Valc_2,6.3 /
children.translated_text: people went to worship the lord <s>Ugramādhava</s>. // <s>Valc</s> 2,6.3 //
<s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, all <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, <s>Vaiśyas</s>, and other human beings,
good <s>Śūdras</s> and other <s>Śūdras</s> all came to the great shrine. // <s>Valc</s> 2,6.4 //
Some gathered flowers, others incense and lamps;

children.text: kecit gandhañca naivedyān kecit vyajanacāmarān // Valc_2,6.5 //
children.translated_text: some brought sandalwood paste and food offerings, and some fans and <s>cāmaras</s> (fly-whisks). // <s>Valc</s> 2,6.5 //
Now, to worship the primordial great <s>liṅga</s> in the eastern region of <s>Gauḍa</s>,
Some brought parasols, gems, garlands, and garments;

children.text: ityādīni samāgṛhya te dravyāṇi samāgatāḥ // Valc_2,6.6 //
children.translated_text: having gathered such articles, they all arrived. // <s>Valc</s> 2,6.6 //
The people worshiped the Self-born One with seasonal flowers such as oleanders
and with incenses of sandalwood and the like. // <s>Valc</s> 2,6.7 //
With pure waters from sacred pilgrimage sites, tinted with saffron,
they bathed <s>Śaṅkara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) with cool and fragrant ablutions. // <s>Valc</s> 2,6.8 //
Some offered ghee lamps and others oil lamps;
they gave milk-offerings (<s>kṣīrārghya</s>) and <s>pādya</s> (foot-water) with pure water. // <s>Valc</s> 2,6.9 //
With cow's milk, cow's ghee, honey, saffron, camphor,
<s>pañcāmṛta</s> (five nectars), saffron threads, jaggery, and sugar — // <s>Valc</s> 2,6.10 //
with sandalwood, fragrant substances, and the five perfumes, others joyfully
anointed <s>Śaṅkara</s>, the people being devoted with devotion. // <s>Valc</s> 2,6.11 //
They joyfully offered the finest food prepared with rice, sweets,
<s>laḍḍukas</s> (sweets), <s>piṣṭakas</s> (cakes), and various other food offerings. // <s>Valc</s> 2,6.12 //
They set up banners and fluttering silk streamers;

children.text: nanṛtuśca jaguḥ kecit kecit ghaṇṭāmavīvadan // Valc_2,6.13 //
children.translated_text: some danced, some sang, and some rang bells. // <s>Valc</s> 2,6.13 //

children.text: suvarṇaṃ rajataṃ tāmraṃ daduḥ kecit svayambhuve /
children.translated_text: Some gave gold, silver, and copper to the Self-born One;

children.text: daduśca pañcaratnāni saha lājākṣatai rnarāḥ // Valc_2,6.14 //
children.translated_text: the people also gave the five gems along with parched rice and unbroken grains. // <s>Valc</s> 2,6.14 //
They also gave betel for the hands, mouth-freshening substances,
and placed <s>dūrvā</s> grass, flowers, and unbroken grains upon the deity's head. // <s>Valc</s> 2,6.15 //
Thus, with the five-fold worship (<s>pañcopacāra</s>), the people headed by <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>
worshiped <s>Śiva</s>, performed <s>japa</s> (chanting), and performed circumambulation. // <s>Valc</s> 2,6.16 //
With dances, songs, great festivities, and musical instruments of sweet sound,
with 'hāṃ' and 'huṃ' exclamations and exultations, they carried <s>Ugramādhava</s> in procession. // <s>Valc</s> 2,6.17 //
Some with the fivefold prostration, others with the eightfold prostration,
bowed down and offered hymns of praise with sweet voices. // <s>Valc</s> 2,6.18 //
With <s>bhallakas</s> (a type of drum), <s>jhallarīs</s> (cymbals), <s>mṛdaṅgas</s>, and <s>mardala</s> drums,
with flutes and stringed instruments, some worshiped the Self-born One. // <s>Valc</s> 2,6.19 //
With auspicious victory-songs, <s>dhāraṇīs</s> (protective chants), and hymns,
mendicant monks and nuns worshiped <s>Śaṅkara</s> with songs in the vernacular. // <s>Valc</s> 2,6.20 //
<s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, the best among Vedic scholars, with melodious <s>Veda</s> recitations;
<s>Kṣatriyas</s> with gold, gems, and great parasols; // <s>Valc</s> 2,6.21 //
merchants with golden crest-jewels and <s>bilva</s>-leaf offerings;
and <s>Śūdras</s> worshiped with various ritual fruits and offerings. // <s>Valc</s> 2,6.22 //

children.text: athānye āgatā ye ca jātayo rajakādayaḥ /
children.translated_text: And others who came — those of castes such as washermen and the like —

children.text: te sarvve dūrataḥ sthitvā praṇemuśca punaḥ punaḥ // Valc_2,6.23 //
children.translated_text: they all stood at a distance and bowed down again and again. // <s>Valc</s> 2,6.23 //
Thus ends the sixth chapter, named 'The Worship of <s>Ugramādhava</s>,' in the <s>Vallālacarita</s> composed by <s>Ānandabhaṭṭa</s>.
Now begins the seventh chapter.
Once upon a time, the lotus-eyed <s>Padmākṣī</s>, the beloved of <s>Vallāla</s>,
came to that great shrine to worship <s>Śaṅkara</s>. // <s>Valc</s> 2,7.1 //
Having brought many articles of gold and silver,
a parasol for the deity, ear-ornaments for the goddess, // <s>Valc</s> 2,7.2 //
a pendant, a bracelet, a crown, a neck-ornament,
an armlet, a wristlet, a precious girdle, anklets, and the like — // <s>Valc</s> 2,7.3 //

children.text: vastrāṇi ca mahārhāṇi patākāśca dhvajāni ca /
children.translated_text: precious garments, banners, and flags,
sacred threads, sandal paste, and various accessories — // <s>Valc</s> 2,7.4 //

children.text: arcayāmāsa devaṃ sā devīṃ ca sa purohitaḥ /
children.translated_text: she, along with the family priest, worshiped the deity and the goddess

children.text: naivedye stairalaṅkāraicchatreṇa ca paraṃ mudā // Valc_2,7.5 //
children.translated_text: with food offerings, those ornaments, and a parasol, with supreme delight. // <s>Valc</s> 2,7.5 //

children.text: pūjayitvā gatā devī sāruhya hayanaṃ varam /
children.translated_text: Having completed the worship, the queen departed, mounting a fine palanquin;
the family priest remained there, hoping for a share of the donated articles. // <s>Valc</s> 2,7.6 //

children.text: sa mahāntam dharmmagiriṃ valadeva uvāca ha /
children.translated_text: He, <s>Valadeva</s>, said to the great <s>Dharmagiri</s>, the lord of the shrine:

children.text: bhadanta dehi me bhāgam matprāpyamacireṇa bhoḥ // Valc_2,7.7 //
children.translated_text: "Venerable sir, give me my share — what is due to me — without delay!" // <s>Valc</s> 2,7.7 //

children.text: tacchratvā tadvacaḥ sthānādhipaḥ sa pratyuvāca tam /
children.translated_text: Hearing his words, the lord of the shrine replied to him:

children.text: adadāma na kasmaicit bhāgameva kadācana // Valc_2,7.8 //
children.translated_text: "We never give a share to anyone, ever. // <s>Valc</s> 2,7.8 //

children.text: ato na dadyāṃ bhavate gaccha gaccha gṛhaṃ vraja /
children.translated_text: Therefore I shall not give to you — go, go, go home!"
Thus between the two there was an exchange of harsh words for some time. // <s>Valc</s> 2,7.9 //
<s>Valadeva</s>, becoming enraged, then cursed the temple-lord:

children.text: nipatadhvamare mūḍha na te bhadraṃ bhaviṣyati // Valc_2,7.10 //
children.translated_text: "May ruin fall upon you, O fool! Nothing good shall befall you!" // <s>Valc</s> 2,7.10 //
Hearing this, the temple-lord, his face contorted with fury like a barbarian's,
struck <s>Valadeva</s> on the cheek with a slap. // <s>Valc</s> 2,7.11 //
He commanded his sturdy disciples: "Remove this man!"
Those men then carried out their master's command,
and <s>Valadeva</s> went running to the presence of the king. // <s>Valc</s> 2,7.12 //
He narrated the entire incident from beginning to end to the king;
the courtiers and <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> also confirmed his account. // <s>Valc</s> 2,7.13 //
They declared that the words of <s>Valadeva</s> were justified and that the temple-lord should be punished.
Having thus ascertained the insult to his priest,

children.text: manyunā sa prajajvāla vahninā paṭalaṃ yathā // Valc_2,7.14 //
children.translated_text: the king blazed with fury, like a forest set ablaze by fire. // <s>Valc</s> 2,7.14 //
"Let <s>Dharmagiri</s> be banished from my territories, along with his entire community!"
— thus the king commanded <s>Rudranāga</s>, the chief of punishment. // <s>Valc</s> 2,7.15 //
That lion among kings, a treasury of virtues and sole kinsman of his people — true was the word of the best of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> to the Creator —

children.text: cakāra rāṣṭrāt sa vahiṣkṛtaṃ taṃ gaṇena sārddhaṃ kila rājasiṃhaḥ // Valc_2,7.16 //
children.translated_text: he had him banished from the kingdom along with his entire community. // <s>Valc</s> 2,7.16 //

children.text: ityānandabhaṭṭaprokte vallālacarite devalānāṃ nirvvāsanaṃ nāma saptamo 'dhyāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus ends the seventh chapter, named 'The Banishment of the Temple-keepers,' in the <s>Vallālacarita</s> composed by <s>Ānandabhaṭṭa</s>.

]
Now begins the eighth chapter.
<s>Oṃ</s> — Salutation to <s>Śiva</s>!
Having saluted <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, and <s>Nara</s> also, the best of men,
and the goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s>, and <s>Vyāsa</s>, then one should proclaim victory. // <s>Valc</s> 2,8.1 //
<s>Oṃ</s> — Salutation to the blessed <s>Vāsudeva</s>!
Salutation to <s>Siṃhagiri</s>, the lord, of wondrous power,

children.text: vallālabhūpati rninye mārge yena sanātane // Valc_2,8.2 //
children.translated_text: by whom King <s>Vallāla</s> was led upon the eternal path. // <s>Valc</s> 2,8.2 //
Now, the illustrious <s>Vallālasena</s>, long ago, in the foremost city of <s>Gauḍa</s>,
sat in comfort in an assembly-hall blazing with the splendor of various gems. // <s>Valc</s> 2,8.3 //
With dark, curling locks of hair and waving ringlets,
their lotus-faces being drunk in by the bee-like eyes of the people in the assembly, // <s>Valc</s> 2,8.4 //
their breasts covered by bodices, their bangles and bracelets jingling,
beautifully clothed, lovely in every limb, with reddened lips, // <s>Valc</s> 2,8.5 //
revealing the roots of their arms, with dancing hands, as it were — the women
served the king there with the breezes of waving fly-whisks. // <s>Valc</s> 2,8.6 //
Nobles, princes, eloquent courtiers, and others,

children.text: upāsate sma vallālaṃ brāhmaṇāśca mahaujasaḥ // Valc_2,8.7 //
children.translated_text: as well as <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> of great splendor, attended upon <s>Vallāla</s>. (Valc 2.8.7)
Dancing girls with deer-like eyes, with songs, <s>hallīṣa</s> (group dances), and <s>lāsya</s> (graceful dances),
and <s>bhrukuṃśas</s> (jesters) and musicians skilled in instruments delighted him with their music. (Valc 2.8.8)
Once, a knower of the <s>Vedas</s>, <s>Vedāṅgas</s>, <s>Upaniṣads</s>, and <s>Dharmaśāstra</s>,
a master of the <s>Itihāsas</s> and <s>Purāṇas</s>, saluted by the world, (Valc 2.8.9)
wise, skilled in statecraft, eloquent, the great king's preceptor, a sage,
a lord among <s>yogīs</s>, of great wisdom, proficient in all <s>śāstras</s>, (Valc 2.8.10)
the <s>Bhaṭṭa</s> named <s>Siṃhagiri</s>, surrounded by his disciples at that time,

children.text: udbhāsayan diśaḥ sarvvāḥ śriyā paramayā jvalan // Valc_2,8.11 //
children.translated_text: illuminating all directions, blazing with supreme glory, (Valc 2.8.11)
swift as thought, desiring to see King <s>Vallāla</s> seated in the assembly hall,
wandering from the region of the <s>Badarikāśrama</s>, came to that assembly. (Valc 2.8.12)
Seeing the sage who was blessing him with benedictions of victory, the king

children.text: pratyutpatyāsanāt tūrṇaṃ babande caraṇau muneḥ // Valc_2,8.13 //
children.translated_text: quickly rose from his seat and grasped the feet of the sage. (Valc 2.8.13)

children.text: dattvāsanaṃ tatastasmai bhaktyā prītyā ca pārthivaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, having offered a seat to him, the king with devotion and affection

children.text: dhanaiḥ ratnai ryathākāmaiḥ pūjayāmāsa yatnataḥ // Valc_2,8.14 //
children.translated_text: worshipped him diligently with wealth and gems as desired. (Valc 2.8.14)
The sage, honored by King <s>Vallāla</s>, was pleased at heart then,
and inquired of the lord of men about his welfare and prosperity. (Valc 2.8.15)
Having met <s>Valadeva</s>, the best of sages, smiling,

children.text: pratipūjya yathānyāyaṃ papraccha kuśalaṃ tadā // Valc_2,8.16 //
children.translated_text: honoring him according to proper custom, then asked about his well-being. (Valc 2.8.16)
That king, joyful in mind, spoke to the sage <s>Bhaṭṭa Siṃhagiri</s>,
with supreme delight, to the ascetic radiant with splendor. (Valc 2.8.17)

children.text: adya me saphalaṃ janma mahadgṛñca pavitritam /
children.translated_text: "Today my birth is fruitful and my great house is purified;
by your arrival alone, the night has become auspicious dawn." (Valc 2.8.18)
Then, perceiving that sage of firm vows to be rested,
the lord of the earth, seated near him who was comfortably seated, spoke: (Valc 2.8.19)
The king said:
"O venerable one, you are a knower of all <s>śāstras</s>, omniscient, a knower of all truths;
there is nothing unknown to you — please tell me out of compassion. (Valc 2.8.20)
Tell me, O sage, about the origin of the four <s>varṇas</s>, the auspicious <s>gotras</s>, lineages, and the rest,

children.text: varṇānāṃ śaṅkarotpattiṃ kathayasva ca me mune // Valc_2,8.21 //
children.translated_text: and also about the mixed origins of the <s>varṇas</s>." (Valc 2.8.21)
Hearing these words of the king, with a face brightened by satisfaction,
the greatly radiant son of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> replied: (Valc 2.8.22)
<s>Siṃhagiri</s> said:
"O king, just as the treasure-house of austerities, <s>Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana</s>, spoke

children.text: kṛṣṇadvaipāyaragaḥ prāha tathādya kathayāmi te // Valc_2,8.23 //
children.translated_text: to the eager <s>Rājarṣis</s> (royal sages), so I shall tell you today. (Valc 2.8.23)
In the sacred <s>Badarikāśrama</s>, in the abode of <s>Devadāru</s> (deodar) forest,
teeming with various birds and animals, the dwelling of peace and beauty, (Valc 2.8.24)
the <s>Rājarṣis</s> (royal sages), having bowed before the great sage <s>Vyāsa</s>,
the long-lived one, knower of the three times, to whom oblations had been offered, approached him respectfully. (Valc 2.8.25)
The <s>Rājarṣis</s> (royal sages) said:
'We have gone to <s>Naimiṣāraṇya</s> and also to the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>,

children.text: bhavān na ca śuko dṛṣṭaḥ sauti vāṃ śaunakādayaḥ // Valc_2,8.26 //
children.translated_text: but neither you, nor <s>Śuka</s>, nor <s>Sauti</s>, nor <s>Śaunaka</s> and others were seen. (Valc 2.8.26)
By good fortune, O venerable one, you are seen today after a long time on this mountain,
like <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> to the devotees who had been searching for a long time. (Valc 2.8.27)
The <s>Vedas</s> were divided by you formerly, O son of <s>Satyavatī</s>,
and the <s>Itihāsas</s> and <s>Purāṇas</s> were narrated out of compassion. (Valc 2.8.28)
The <s>Dharmaśāstra</s> was also narrated; now the <s>Kali</s> age prevails,

children.text: kṛṣṇo 'pi palitaiḥ keśaiḥ śuklatāṃ gatavānasi // Valc_2,8.29 //
children.translated_text: and even <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, with whitened hair, has turned grey. (Valc 2.8.29)
Therefore, today, O <s>Brahman</s>, O great sage, tell us yourself

children.text: purāṇaṃ dharmmatatvajña hyanugrāhyā vayaṃ tava // Valc_2,8.30 //
children.translated_text: a <s>Purāṇa</s>, O knower of the essence of <s>Dharma</s>, for we are worthy of your grace. (Valc 2.8.30)
We shall not leave you without the narration of a <s>Purāṇa</s>;

children.text: baddho 'sti padayo rbhaktidāmabhi stvavaśo bhavān // Valc_2,8.31 //
children.translated_text: you are bound at the feet by the ropes of devotion, and are under our power.' (Valc 2.8.31)

children.text: iti teṣāṃ vacaḥ śrutvā sa kiñcit prahasanniva /
children.translated_text: Hearing their words, he, slightly smiling,

children.text: uvāca vāgvidāṃ śreṣṭhaḥ śrūyatāṃ kathayāmi vaḥ // Valc_2,8.32 //
children.translated_text: the best among the eloquent, said: 'Listen, I shall narrate to you.' (Valc 2.8.32)
Thus ends the eighth chapter in the <s>Vyāsapurāṇa</s> of the <s>Vallālacarita</s>.
Now begins the ninth chapter.
<s>Vyāsa</s> said:
The <s>Puruṣa</s> (Cosmic Being) with a thousand heads, a thousand eyes, and a thousand feet,

children.text: sa bhūmiṃ viśvato vṛttvā atyatiṣṭhadaśāṅgulam // Valc_2,9.1 //
children.translated_text: having pervaded the earth on all sides, stood ten fingers' breadth beyond it. (Valc 2.9.1)
From him <s>Virāṭ</s> (the Cosmic Form) was born; from <s>Virāṭ</s> came the supreme <s>Puruṣa</s>;
then from his forehead, as he meditated, <s>Rudra</s> was born. (Valc 2.9.2)
The moon was born from his mind, the sun was born from his eyes,
<s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s> from his mouth, and <s>Vāyu</s> was born from his breath. (Valc 2.9.3)
<s>Marīci</s>, <s>Atri</s>, <s>Aṅgirasa</s>, <s>Pulastya</s>, <s>Pulaha</s>, <s>Kratu</s>,
and <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> — the greatly radiant one created these seven mind-born ones. (Valc 2.9.4)
For the increase of the worlds, from his mouth, arms, thighs, and feet,

children.text: brāhmaṇaṃ kṣatriyaṃ vaiśyaṃ śūdrañca niravarttayat // Valc_2,9.5 //
children.translated_text: he brought forth the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>Kṣatriya</s>, <s>Vaiśya</s>, and <s>Śūdra</s>. (Valc 2.9.5)

children.text: sṛjyamāmāḥ prajā naiva vivarddhante yadā yadā /
children.translated_text: When the beings that were being created did not multiply,
having divided his own body in two, with one half he became male,

children.text: arddhena nārī tasyāṃ sa sasṛje vividhāḥ prajāḥ // Valc_2,9.6 //
children.translated_text: and with the other half female — in her he created various progeny. (Valc 2.9.6)
Of him who pervades and abides in heaven and earth by his greatness,

children.text: pitḥṇāntu gaṇāḥ sapta purāṇe kathitā mayā // Valc_2,9.7 //
children.translated_text: seven groups of <s>Pitṛs</s> (ancestors) have been described by me in the <s>Purāṇa</s>. (Valc 2.9.7)
The <s>Vairājas</s>, <s>Agniṣvāttas</s>, and likewise those known as <s>Barhiṣads</s>,
the <s>Sukālas</s>, <s>Haviṣmantas</s>, <s>Susvadhās</s>, and <s>Somapās</s>. (Valc 2.9.8)
Of these, the first three, O kings, are known as the formless <s>Pitṛs</s> (ancestors),

children.text: sakālādyāśca catvāraḥ saptaivaite gaṇāḥ smṛtāḥ // Valc_2,9.9 //
children.translated_text: and the four beginning with <s>Sukāla</s> — these seven are known as the groups. (Valc 2.9.9)
The <s>Somasads</s> are the sons of <s>Virāṭ</s>; the <s>Agniṣvāttas</s> are born of <s>Marīci</s>;
the <s>Barhiṣads</s> are of <s>Pulastya</s>'s lineage; the <s>Sukālas</s> are born of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>;

children.text: susvadhāḥ pulahājjātāḥ somapāstu kaveḥ sutāḥ // Valc_2,9.10 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Susvadhās</s> are born from <s>Pulaha</s>, and the <s>Somapās</s> are the sons of <s>Kavi</s>. (Valc 2.9.10)
The <s>Sukālas</s>, <s>Haviṣyantas</s>, <s>Susvadhās</s>, and <s>Somapās</s> —
<s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, <s>Vaiśyas</s>, and <s>Śūdras</s> propitiate them seeking rewards. (Valc 2.9.11)

children.text: yatra te tu gaṇā mukhyāḥ pitḥṇāṃ parikīrttitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Where those principal groups of <s>Pitṛs</s> (ancestors) have been enumerated,
their endless line of sons and grandsons should also be known. (Valc 2.9.12)
<s>Viśva</s>, <s>Viśvabhuj</s>, <s>Ārādhya</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Dhanya</s>, <s>Śubhānana</s>,

children.text: bhūtido bhūtikṛdbhatiḥ pitḥṇāñca gaṇā nava // Valc_2,9.13 //
children.translated_text: <s>Bhūtida</s>, <s>Bhūtikṛt</s>, <s>Bhūti</s> — these are the nine groups of the <s>Pitṛs</s>. (Valc 2.9.13)
<s>Kalyāṇa</s>, <s>Kalyatākartā</s>, <s>Kalya</s>, <s>Kalyatarāśraya</s>,

children.text: kalyatāheturanaghaḥ ṣaḍime ca gaṇāḥ smṛtāḥ // Valc_2,9.14 //
children.translated_text: <s>Kalyatāhetu</s>, <s>Anagha</s> — these six groups are known. (Valc 2.9.14)
<s>Vara</s>, <s>Vareṇya</s>, <s>Varada</s>, <s>Puṣṭida</s>, and likewise <s>Tuṣṭida</s>,

children.text: viśvapātā tathā dhātā saptaivaite tathā gaṇāḥ // Valc_2,9.15 //
children.translated_text: <s>Viśvapātā</s>, and <s>Dhātā</s> — these are likewise seven groups. (Valc 2.9.15)
<s>Mahān</s>, <s>Mahātmā</s>, <s>Mahita</s>, <s>Mahimāvān</s>, <s>Mahābala</s> —

children.text: gaṇāḥ pañca tathaivaite pitḥṇāṃ pāpanāśanāḥ // Valc_2,9.16 //
children.translated_text: these are likewise five groups of the <s>Pitṛs</s>, destroyers of sin. (Valc 2.9.16)
<s>Sukhada</s>, <s>Dhanada</s>, another called <s>Dharmada</s>, another <s>Bhūtida</s> —

children.text: pitḥṇāṃ kathyate caitat tathā gaṇacatuṣṭayam // Valc_2,9.17 //
children.translated_text: this is declared to be the fourfold group of the <s>Pitṛs</s>. (Valc 2.9.17)

children.text: iti vallālacarite vyāsapurāṇe sṛṣṭivisṛṣṭikathanaṃ nāma navamo 'dhyāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus ends the ninth chapter, called 'The Narration of Creation and Secondary Creation,' in the <s>Vyāsapurāṇa</s> of the <s>Vallālacarita</s>.
Now begins the tenth chapter.
<s>Vyāsa</s> said:
Time created <s>Virāj</s>; <s>Virāṭ</s> created <s>Puruṣa</s>;

children.text: puruṣaṃ taṃ manuṃ viddhi virāja ūrusambhavam // Valc_2,10.1 //
children.translated_text: know that <s>Puruṣa</s> to be <s>Manu</s>, born from the thigh of <s>Virāj</s>. (Valc 2.10.1)

children.text: sa sṛṣṭvā tu prajāstveva āpavaḥ sa prajāpatiḥ /
children.translated_text: Having created the beings, that <s> Āpava</s> (born of water), the <s>Prajāpati</s> (lord of creatures),
