the <s>Puruṣa</s> obtained as wife <s>Śatarūpā</s>, who was not born from a womb. (Valc 2.10.2)
From the <s>Vairāja Puruṣa</s>, <s>Śatarūpā</s> bore <s>Vīra</s>;
<s>Priyavrata</s> and <s>Uttānapāda</s> were born from <s>Vīra</s>, and <s>Kāmyā</s> was also born. (Valc 2.10.3)
The greatly fortunate one named <s>Kāmyā</s> was the daughter of <s>Prajāpati</s> <s>Kardama</s>;

children.text: kanyā putrāśca catvāraḥ samrāṭ kukṣi rvirāṭ prabhuḥ // Valc_2,10.4 //
children.translated_text: and her four sons were <s>Samrāṭ</s>, <s>Kukṣi</s>, <s>Virāṭ</s>, and <s>Prabhu</s>. (Valc 2.10.4)

children.text: priyavrataṃ samāsādya patiṃ sā janayat sutān /
children.translated_text: Having obtained <s>Priyavrata</s> as husband, she bore sons;
<s>Prajāpati</s> <s>Atri</s> took <s>Uttānapāda</s> as a son. (Valc 2.10.5)
From <s>Uttānapāda</s>, <s>Sunṛtā</s> bore four sons;

children.text: dharmmasya kanyā suśroṇī sunṛtā nāma viśrutā // Valc_2,10.6 //
children.translated_text: <s>Sunṛtā</s>, the beautiful-hipped daughter of <s>Dharma</s>, was renowned by name. (Valc 2.10.6)
She was born through <s>Vājimedhā</s> (a horse-sacrifice), the auspicious mother of <s>Dhruva</s>;
<s>Dhruva</s>, <s>Kīrtimān</s>, <s>Āyuṣmān</s>, and <s>Vasu</s> —
<s>Prajāpati</s> <s>Uttānapāda</s> begot these in <s>Sunṛtā</s>. (Valc 2.10.7)
<s>Dhruva</s> attained the position before the seven sages through his austerities;
from <s>Dhruva</s> were born <s>Śliṣṭi</s>, <s>Bhavya</s>, and <s>Śambhu</s>. (Valc 2.10.8)
From <s>Śliṣṭi</s>, <s>Succhāyā</s> bore five sinless sons:

children.text: ripuṃ ripuñjayaṃ ripraṃ vṛkalaṃ vṛkatejasam // Valc_2,10.9 //
children.translated_text: <s>Ripu</s>, <s>Ripuñjaya</s>, <s>Ripra</s>, <s>Vṛkala</s>, and <s>Vṛkatejasa</s>. (Valc 2.10.9)
From <s>Ripu</s>, <s>Vṛhatī</s> bore <s>Cākṣuṣa</s>, endowed with all radiance;

children.text: ajījanat puṣkariṇyāṃ vīraṇyāṃ cākṣuṣo manum // Valc_2,10.10 //
children.translated_text: in <s>Puṣkariṇī</s> (also called <s>Vīraṇī</s>), <s>Cākṣuṣa</s> begot <s>Manu</s>. (Valc 2.10.10)
In the wife of the great-souled <s>Prajāpati</s> <s>Araṇya</s>,
from <s>Manu</s> were born ten sons of great splendor in <s>Naḍvalā</s>. (Valc 2.10.11)
In the daughter of <s>Prajāpati</s> <s>Vairāja</s>, those best of <s>Manavas</s> (men) —

children.text: ūruḥ puruḥ śatadyumnastapasvī satyavāk kaviḥ // Valc_2,10.12 //
children.translated_text: <s>Ūru</s>, <s>Puru</s>, <s>Śatadyumna</s>, <s>Tapasvin</s>, <s>Satyavāk</s>, <s>Kavi</s>, (Valc 2.10.12)
<s>Agniṣṭu</s>, <s>Atirātra</s>, and <s>Sudyumna</s> — these nine,
and <s>Abhimanyu</s> as the tenth, of great splendor, in <s>Naḍvalā</s>. (Valc 2.10.13)
From <s>Ūru</s>, <s>Āgneyī</s> bore six sons of great radiance:

children.text: aṅgaṃ sumanasaṃ svātiṃ kratumaṅgirasaṃ gayam // Valc_2,10.14 //
children.translated_text: <s>Aṅga</s>, <s>Sumanasa</s>, <s>Svāti</s>, <s>Kratu</s>, <s>Aṅgirasa</s>, and <s>Gaya</s>. (Valc 2.10.14)
From <s>Aṅga</s>, in the maiden <s>Sunīthā</s>, one son <s>Veṇa</s> was born;

children.text: veṇasya mathite pāṇau sambabhūva pṛthurnṛpaḥ // Valc_2,10.15 //
children.translated_text: when <s>Veṇa</s>'s hand was churned, King <s>Pṛthu</s> arose. (Valc 2.10.15)
<s>Pṛthu</s> <s>Vainya</s> (son of <s>Veṇa</s>) then protected this earth, born first among <s>Kṣatriyas</s>;
he was the first lord of the earth to be consecrated with the <s>Rājasūya</s> (royal consecration). (Valc 2.10.16)
From him were born two skilled ones, a bard and a panegyrist;

children.text: pṛthoḥ putrau tu dharmmajñau jajñāte 'ntarddhipālinau // Valc_2,10.17 //
children.translated_text: the two sons of <s>Pṛthu</s>, knowers of <s>Dharma</s>, were born as <s>Antarddhi</s> and <s>Pālin</s>. (Valc 2.10.17)
<s>Śikhaṇḍinī</s> bore <s>Havirdhāna</s> from <s>Antarddhi</s>;

children.text: havirdhānāt ṣaḍāgneyī dhīṣaṇā janayat sutān // Valc_2,10.18 //
children.translated_text: from <s>Havirdhāna</s>, <s>Dhīṣaṇā</s> (<s>Āgneyī</s>) bore six sons: (Valc 2.10.18)
<s>Prācīnavarhiṣ</s>, <s>Śukra</s>, <s>Gaya</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Vraja</s>, and <s>Ajina</s>;
the venerable <s>Prācīnavarhis</s> became a great <s>Prajāpati</s>. (Valc 2.10.19)
That lord married a daughter of the ocean;
<s>Suvarṇā</s>, the daughter of the ocean, bore ten sons to <s>Prācīnavarhis</s>. (Valc 2.10.20)
All of them were named <s>Pracetas</s>, masters of the science of archery,
having attained the status of <s>Prajāpati</s>, the sons of <s>Prācīnavarhis</s> were gratified. (Valc 2.10.21)

children.text: bhū khaṃ vyāptaṃ hi tarubhistāṃstarūnadahaṃśca te /
children.translated_text: The earth and sky were covered with trees; and they burned those trees;
then, realizing the destruction of the trees, when only a few trees remained,
King <s>Soma</s> approached and said to those <s>Prajāpatis</s>: (Valc 2.10.22)

children.text: kopaṃ yacchata dāsyanti kanyāṃ vo māriṣāṃ varām /
children.translated_text: 'Restrain your anger! They shall give you the excellent maiden <s>Māriṣā</s> as wife,

children.text: tapasvino muneḥ kaṇḍoḥ pramlocāyāṃ mamaiva ca // Valc_2,10.23 //
children.translated_text: born from <s>Pramlocā</s> and from the ascetic sage <s>Kaṇḍu</s>, and from me as well. (Valc 2.10.23)

children.text: bhaviṣyaṃ jānatā sṛṣṭā bhāryyā vo 'stu kulaṅkarī /
children.translated_text: Knowing the future, she was created; let her be your wife, the ornament of your lineage;
from her shall be born <s>Dakṣa</s>, who will multiply the progeny.' (Valc 2.10.24)
The <s>Pracetases</s> took her; and from her <s>Dakṣa</s> was then born,
a <s>Prajāpati</s>, from the ten <s>Pracetases</s> in <s>Māriṣā</s>. (Valc 2.10.25)

children.text: dakṣo jajñe mahātejāḥ somasyāṃśena bhūmipāḥ putrānutpādayāmāsa śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ /
children.translated_text: The greatly radiant <s>Dakṣa</s> was born with a portion of <s>Soma</s>; O kings, he begot sons by the hundreds and by the thousands;

children.text: haryyaśya nāma dakṣasya sahasrāṇi ca pañca ca putrāṇāṃ vedituṃ pṛthvyāḥ pramāṇaṃ hi gatādiśaḥ // Valc_2,10.26 //
children.translated_text: five thousand sons of <s>Dakṣa</s>, named <s>Haryaśvas</s>, went forth in all directions to measure the extent of the earth. (Valc 2.10.26)
Then another thousand sons went in search of them.

children.text: adyāpi na nivarttante samudrebhya ivāpagāḥ // Valc_2,10.27 //
children.translated_text: Even today they do not turn back, like rivers from the oceans.

children.text: iti vallālacarite vyāsapurāṇe svāyambhuvavaṃśakathanaṃ nāma daśamo 'dhyāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Vallālacarita</s>, in the <s>Vyāsapurāṇa</s>, the tenth chapter named 'The Narration of the <s>Svāyambhuva</s> Lineage' concludes.
Chapter Eleven.
<s>Siṃhagiri</s> said:
From the mind of <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Atri</s> was born, and <s>Soma</s> became his son.

children.text: tasya vaṃśaṃ pravakṣyāmi yatra jāto 'si pārthiva // Valc_2,11.1 //
children.translated_text: I shall narrate his lineage, in which you were born, O king.
<s>Vyāsa</s> said:

children.text: kṛtvā somo rājasūyaṃ trailokyaṃ dakṣiṇāṃ dadau /
children.translated_text: <s>Soma</s>, having performed the <s>Rājasūya</s> sacrifice, gave the three worlds as <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (sacrificial fee),
to the chief officiants, the <s>brahmarṣis</s> (brahmin sages), O scorchers of foes.
When the <s>avabhṛtha</s> (concluding bath) was completed, nine goddesses, desiring to behold <s>Soma's</s> beauty,
their limbs scorched by the arrows of <s>Kāma</s> (desire), attended upon him.
<s>Śinīvālī</s> abandoned <s>Kardama</s>, <s>Haviṣmantā</s> abandoned <s>Kratu</s> himself, <s>Dyuti</s> abandoned <s>Vibhāvasu</s>, <s>Puṣṭi</s> abandoned the imperishable <s>Dhātā</s>,
<s>Prabhā</s> abandoned <s>Prabhākara</s>, <s>Vasu</s> abandoned <s>Kāśyapa</s> the son of <s>Marīci</s>,
<s>Kīrti</s> abandoned her husband <s>Jayanta</s>, <s>Dhṛti</s> abandoned her lord <s>Nandī</s>,

children.text: kīrttirjayantaṃ bharttāraṃ nandīṃ tyaktvā patiṃ dhṛtiḥ /
children.translated_text: and <s>Lakṣmī</s>, abandoning <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, devoted herself to <s>Soma</s> then.
<s>Soma</s> too desired them as if they were his own.
He forcibly abducted <s>Tārā</s>, the illustrious wife of <s>Bṛhaspati</s>,

children.text: vṛhaspateḥ sa vai bhāryyāṃ tārāṃ nāma yaśasvinīm // Valc_2,11.6 //
children.translated_text: showing contempt for the son of <s>Aṅgiras</s>.
Though entreated by the gods along with the <s>devarṣis</s> (divine sages), <s>Soma</s>

children.text: sa yācyamāno devaiśca somo devarṣirbhiḥ saha // Valc_2,11.7 //
children.translated_text: did not release <s>Tārā</s> to that son of <s>Aṅgiras</s>.

children.text: āṅgirase tadā tasmai tārāṃ naiva vyavasarjjayat /
children.translated_text: Then <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, the preceptor of the gods, became enraged against him.
<s>Uśanas</s> (Śukra) then took the side of the son of <s>Aṅgiras</s>,
for he was a disciple of great splendor, senior even to <s>Bṛhaspati's</s> father.

children.text: sa hi śiṣyo mahātejāḥ pituḥ pūrvvo vṛhaspateḥ // Valc_2,11.9 //
children.translated_text: Out of that affection, the blessed Lord <s>Rudra</s>
became an ally of <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, taking up the <s>Ājyagava</s> bow.
By that great-souled one, the supreme weapon called <s>Brahmaśiras</s>

children.text: uddiśya daityānutsṛṣṭaṃ yenaiṣāṃ nāśitaṃ yaśaḥ // Valc_2,11.11 /
children.translated_text: There occurred a terrible war, renowned as the <s>Tārakāmaya</s> (war over Tārā),
between the gods and <s>Dānavas</s>, a great war that caused destruction of the worlds.
Those gods who survived, along with the <s>Tuṣitas</s>, O king,
was released against the <s>Daityas</s>, by which their glory was destroyed.

children.text: tatra śiṣṭāstu ye devāḥ tuṣitāścaiva pārthivāḥ /
children.translated_text: sought refuge in <s>Brahmā</s>, the primeval, eternal god.
<s>Brahmā</s>, restraining <s>Uśanas</s>, gave <s>Tārā</s> back to the son of <s>Aṅgiras</s>.
Seeing her pregnant, the preceptor (<s>Bṛhaspati</s>) said, 'Abandon the embryo!'
The embryo, once cast out, blazed forth and declared, 'I am born of <s>Soma</s>.'
Thus from <s>Soma</s> was born the son <s>Budha</s>, and his son was <s>Purūravas</s>.

children.text: evaṃ somādvudhaḥ putraḥ putrastasya purūravāḥ // Valc_2,11.15 //
children.translated_text: To him were born from <s>Urvaśī</s> seven great-souled sons,

children.text: urvvaśyāṃ jajñire yasya putrāḥ sapta mahātmanaḥ /
children.translated_text: from that <s>Gandharva</s> nymph: <s>Āyu</s>, <s>Dhīmān</s>, <s>Amāvasu</s>,
<s>Viśvāyu</s> the righteous, and <s>Śrutāyu</s>,
<s>Dṛḍhāyu</s>, <s>Vanāyu</s>, and <s>Śatāyu</s> — these were the sons of <s>Urvaśī</s>.
And formerly, from <s>Prabhā</s>, daughter of <s>Svarbhānu</s>, were born—
<s>Siṃhagiri</s> said:
In their lineages, O <s>Vallāla</s>, great and mighty souls —
<s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, <s>Vaiśyas</s>, and <s>Śūdras</s> were born by the thousands.

children.text: brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyāḥ śūdrā jātāḥ sahasraśaḥ // Valc_2,11.17 //
children.translated_text: <s>Vyāsa</s> said:
<s>Nahuṣa</s> was the son of <s>Āyu</s>; then came <s>Vṛddhaśarman</s>,

children.text: āyuṣaḥ nahuṣaḥ putro vṛddhaśarmmā tataḥ param /
children.translated_text: <s>Rambha</s>, <s>Raji</s>, and <s>Anenas</s>; and <s>Raji</s> had a hundred sons.

children.text: rambho rajiranenāśca rajeḥ putraśataṃ hyabhūt // Valc_2,11.18 //
children.translated_text: They were renowned as the <s>Rājeyas</s>. <s>Raji</s>, blessed by <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
slew the <s>Daityas</s> in the war between gods and <s>Asuras</s>, at the request of the gods.
Born from <s>Virajā</s>, a daughter of the <s>Pitṛs</s>, were the mighty
seven sons of <s>Nahuṣa</s>, six of whom were equal in splendor to <s>Indra</s>:
<s>Yati</s>, <s>Yayāti</s>, <s>Saṃyāti</s>, <s>Rāyāti</s>, <s>Pāñcika</s>, <s>Bhava</s>,
and <s>Suyāti</s> as the sixth. Among them, <s>Yayāti</s> became king.

children.text: suyātiḥ ṣaṣṭasteṣāṃ vai yayātiḥ pārthivo 'bhavat // Valc_2,11.21 //
children.translated_text: <s>Yati</s>, having adopted the path of liberation, became a sage absorbed in <s>Brahman</s>.
<s>Yayāti</s>, having conquered this earth from among the five,
obtained as his wife <s>Devayānī</s>, the daughter of <s>Uśanas</s>.
And also <s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s>, the <s>Āsurī</s> (daughter of an Asura), the daughter of <s>Vṛṣaparvan</s>.
<s>Devayānī</s> gave birth to <s>Yadu</s> and <s>Turvasu</s>,
while <s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s>, daughter of <s>Vṛṣaparvan</s>, bore <s>Druhyu</s>, <s>Anu</s>, and <s>Puru</s>.

children.text: duhyuṃ cānuṃ puruñcaiva śarmmiṣṭhā vārṣaparvvaṇī // Valc_2,11.23 //
children.translated_text: <s>Yadu</s> and <s>Puru</s> became the propagators of their lineages.
Now hear the lineage of <s>Yadu</s>, of wondrous valor.
<s>Yadu</s> had five sons, equal to the sons of gods:
<s>Sahasrada</s>, <s>Payoda</s>, <s>Kroṣṭā</s>, <s>Nīla</s>, and <s>Añjika</s>.
The heirs of <s>Sahasrada</s> were three, supremely righteous:
<s>Haihaya</s>, <s>Haya</s>, and King <s>Veṇuhaya</s>.
The wife of <s>Haihaya</s> bore one known as <s>Dharmantra</s>.
The son of <s>Dharmantra</s> was <s>Kārtā</s>, and his son was <s>Sāhañja</s>.
The city named <s>Sāhañjanī</s> was established by that king.

children.text: sāhañjanī nāma purī tena rājñā niveśitā // Valc_2,11.27 //
children.translated_text: The heir of <s>Sāhañja</s> was a king named <s>Mahiṣmān</s>.
The city named <s>Māhiṣmatī</s> was established by that king.

children.text: māhīṣmatī nāma purī tena rājñā niveśitā // Valc_2,11.28 //
children.translated_text: The son of <s>Mahiṣmān</s> was the valorous <s>Bhadraśreṇya</s>,
celebrated in the <s>Purāṇas</s> as the lord of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>.
The heir of <s>Bhadraśreṇya</s> was the renowned <s>Durdama</s>.
The son of <s>Durdama</s> was a king known as <s>Kaṇaka</s>.

children.text: durdamasya suto rājā kaṇako nāma viśrutaḥ // Valc_2,11.30 //
children.translated_text: From <s>Kaṇaka</s> came <s>Kṛtavīrya</s>, then <s>Kṛtāgni</s>, <s>Karavīraka</s>,
and <s>Kṛtaujā</s> as the fourth. From <s>Kṛtavīrya</s> came <s>Arjuna</s>,
who, with his thousand arms, became lord of the seven continents.
He alone conquered the earth with his chariot, resplendent as the sun.
Having bewildered <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, lord of <s>Laṅkā</s>, together with his army, by force,

children.text: laṅkeśaṃ mohayitvā tu sabalaṃ rāvaṇaṃ balāt /
children.translated_text: he bound him with bowstrings and struck the arrogant one with five arrows.

children.text: asau baddhvā dhanurjyābhi rutsiktaṃ pañcabhiḥ śaraiḥ // Valc_2,11.33 //
children.translated_text: Having defeated him, he brought him to <s>Māhiṣmatī</s> and imprisoned him.
His thousand arms, as he fought, O lords of the earth,
manifested through the <s>yoga</s> and <s>māyā</s> (mystical power) of that lord of <s>yogins</s>.
Alas, what valor in battle! When <s>Bhārgava</s> (<s>Paraśurāma</s>) cut off

children.text: aho vata mṛdhe vīryyaṃ bhārgavo 'sya yadācchinat /
children.translated_text: the thousand arms of the king, it was like felling a golden forest of palm trees.
[Folio marker]
Then from <s>Rāma</s> son of <s>Jamadagni</s>, who was slaying the <s>Kṣatriyas</s> born of arms,
the queen of <s>Kārtavīrya</s> fled in terror.
That princess, being pregnant, gave birth in the hermitage of <s>Kauśika</s>

children.text: antarvvatnī tu sā devī suṣuve kauśikāśrame /
children.translated_text: to a son named <s>Subhauma</s>, beautiful as the rising sun.
That lotus-faced son, nurtured by his mother, in due time

children.text: sa mātrā varddhitaḥ kāle putraḥ sarasijānanaḥ /
children.translated_text: received the science of archery (<s>Dhanurvedā</s>) from <s>Kauśika</s>, the mighty-armed one.
Hearing from his mother's mouth that a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> had slain his father, the youth
went forth to slay the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> in all directions, his eyes red with rage.

children.text: jagāma brāhmaṇān hantuṃ dikṣu krodhāruṇekṣaṇaḥ // Valc_2,11.39 //
children.translated_text: Twenty-one times he made this earth devoid of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>;
therefore, no <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> born of the mouth (of <s>Brahmā</s>) are found in the <s>Kali</s> age.

children.text: cakārāto na vidyante brāhmaṇā mukhajāḥ kalau // Valc_2,11.40 //
children.translated_text: Then <s>Bhārgava</s> (<s>Paraśurāma</s>), seeing the <s>Śabaras</s>, <s>Kaḍhu</s> fishermen, and others,
in a land devoid of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, established the sacred thread for them.

children.text: abrāhmaṇye tadā deśe teṣāṃ sūtramakalpayat // Valc_2,11.41 //
children.translated_text: Women are pleased by ornaments, cows by roaming freely,
elephants by showers of dust — but what use is the censure of others?

children.text: kuñjarāḥ pāṃśuvarṣeṇa kiṃ tvete paranindayā // Valc_2,11.42 //
children.translated_text: Then the son of <s>Arjuna</s> (<s>Subhauma</s>) slew <s>Jāmadagnya</s> (<s>Paraśurāma</s>) in battle.
Thus, having conquered the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>Subhīma</s> became victorious, bearing the banner of triumph.

children.text: evaṃ sa brāhmaṇān jitvā subhīmo 'bhūjjayadhvajaḥ // Valc_2,11.43 //
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> women, desiring sons, approached the <s>Kṣatriyas</s>.
From them were born the mixed castes, beginning with <s>Kadambapallavā</s> and others.
Afflicted by the sin of <s>Brahmahatyā</s> (killing of Brāhmaṇas), that king found no peace.
He performed the <s>Vājimedhā</s> (horse sacrifice), the sacrifice that destroys sin.
The stone images of those two (the horse and the king) still exist even today
in the beautiful city of <s>Māhiṣmatī</s>, on the bank of the river <s>Narmadā</s>.
Of <s>Kārtavīrya's</s> hundred sons, five were foremost:

children.text: kārttavīryyasya tu śataṃ putrāṇām pañca vai parāḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Śūrasena</s>, <s>Śūra</s>, <s>Dhṛṣṭokta</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,

children.text: śūrasenaśca śūraśca dhṛṣṭoktaḥ kṛṣṇa eva ca /
children.translated_text: and the renowned <s>Jayadhvaja</s>, and the mighty <s>Subhauma</s>.

children.text: jayadhvaja iti khyātaḥ subhaumaśca mahāvalaḥ // Valc_2,11.47 //
children.translated_text: From <s>Jayadhvaja</s> came <s>Tālajaṅgha</s>; from <s>Tālajaṅgha</s> a hundred sons,
known as the <s>Tālajaṅghas</s>, valiant warriors of supreme prowess.

children.text: tālajaṅghā iti khyātāḥ śūrā uttamapauruṣāḥ // Valc_2,11.48 //
children.translated_text: In the extremely pure lineage of those great <s>Haihayas</s>,
the <s>Vītihotras</s> were born, and also the <s>Bhojas</s> and <s>Āvantyas</s>.

children.text: vītihotrāḥ svayaṃ jātāḥ bhojāścāvantayaḥ smṛtāḥ // Valc_2,11.59 //
children.translated_text: The renowned <s>Tauṇḍikeyas</s> and the <s>Tālajaṅghas</s> likewise,
and the <s>Bharatas</s> and <s>Sujātas</s> — these have been narrated by me in the <s>Purāṇas</s>.

children.text: bharatāśca sujātāśca purāṇe kathitā mayā // Valc_2,11.50 //
children.translated_text: The heroes beginning with <s>Vṛṣa</s>, the <s>Yādavas</s> of meritorious deeds —
<s>Vṛṣa</s> was the dynasty-bearer among them, and his son was <s>Madhu</s>.
<s>Madhu</s> had a hundred sons, and <s>Vṛṣaṇa</s> was the dynasty-founder among them.
From <s>Vṛṣaṇa</s> came all the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>, and from <s>Madhu</s> the <s>Mādhavās</s>.

children.text: vṛṣaṇāt vṛṣṇayaḥ sarvve madhostu mādhavāḥ smṛtāḥ // Valc_2,11.52 //
children.translated_text: The <s>Yādavas</s> were born from <s>Yadu</s> — they are too numerous to recount.
From <s>Turvasu</s> were born the <s>Yavanas</s>, and the <s>Bhojas</s> are known as the sons of <s>Druhyu</s>.

children.text: turvvasoryavanā jātā bhojā druhyoḥ sutāḥ smṛtāḥ /
children.translated_text: From <s>Anu</s> came the <s>Mleccha</s> tribes, and from <s>Puru</s> the <s>Pauravas</s>.
Thus, in the <s>Vallālacarita</s>, in the <s>Vyāsapurāṇa</s>, the eleventh chapter named 'The Description of the <s>Soma</s> Lineage' concludes.

children.text: iti vallālacarite vyāsapurāṇe somavaṃśavarṇanaṃ nāma ekādaśo 'dhyāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Folio marker]
Now begins the twelfth chapter.
<s>Siṃhagiri</s> said:
Hear, O king, the lineage of supreme valor as told by <s>Vyāsa</s>,
in detail and in order, in which you were born, O sovereign.

children.text: vistareṇānupūrvvyā ca yatra jāto 'si pārthiva // Valc_2,12.1 //
children.translated_text: <s>Vyāsa</s> said:
The greatly valorous son of <s>Puru</s> was King <s>Janamejaya</s>.
His son was <s>Pracinvān</s>, who conquered the eastern direction.
From <s>Pracinvān</s> came <s>Pravīra</s>, and his son was <s>Manasyu</s>.
A king named <s>Abhayada</s> was born as the son of <s>Manasyu</s>.

children.text: rājā cābhayado nāma manasyorabhavat sutaḥ // Valc_2,12.3 //
children.translated_text: And from <s>Abhayada</s> came the king <s>Sudhanvā</s>.
From <s>Sudhanvā</s> came <s>Bahugava</s>, and his son was <s>Saṃpāti</s>.
The son of <s>Saṃpāti</s> was <s>Rahampāti</s>, and his son was <s>Raudrāśva</s>.
From <s>Raudrāśva</s> and the <s>Apsaras</s> <s>Ghṛtācī</s> were born ten sons.

children.text: raudrāśvasya ghṛtācyāṃ vai daśāpsarasi sūnavaḥ // Valc_2,12.5 //
children.translated_text: The first among them was <s>Ṛceyu</s>, the second <s>Kṛkaneyu</s>,
<s>Kakṣeyu</s>, <s>Sthaṇḍileyu</s>, and <s>Sannateyu</s> of great intellect,
<s>Daśārṇeyu</s>, <s>Jaleyu</s>, and <s>Sthaleyu</s> of great strength,
<s>Balanitya</s> and <s>Baleyu</s> — these were the ten sons of <s>Raudrāśva</s>.
The sons of <s>Kakṣeyu</s> were three, all of great might:
<s>Sabhānara</s>, <s>Cākṣuṣa</s>, and <s>Paramanthu</s>.
The son of <s>Sabhānara</s> was the learned King <s>Kālānala</s>.
The righteous son of <s>Kālānala</s> was named <s>Sṛñjaya</s>.

children.text: kālānalasya dharmmajñaḥ sṛñjayo nāma vai sutaḥ // Valc_2,12.9 //
children.translated_text: The son of <s>Sṛñjaya</s> was the heroic King <s>Purañjaya</s>.
The illustrious son of <s>Purañjaya</s> was King <s>Janamejaya</s>.
The royal sage <s>Mahāśāla</s> was born of <s>Janamejaya</s>.
He was known among the gods, his fame well-established on earth.

children.text: deveṣu sa parijñātaḥ pratiṣṭhitayaśā bhuvi // Valc_2,12.11 //
children.translated_text: The righteous son of <s>Mahāśāla</s> was named <s>Mahāmanā</s>.
That hero <s>Mahāmanā</s> was born, honored by hosts of warriors.

children.text: jajñe vīraḥ śūragaṇaiḥ pūjitaḥ sa mahāmanāḥ // Valc_2,12.12 //
children.translated_text: And <s>Mahāmanā</s> the excellent begot two sons:
the righteous <s>Uśīnara</s> and the mighty <s>Titikṣu</s>.
and the righteous <s>Uśīnara</s> and the mighty <s>Titikṣu</s>. // Valc 2,12.13 //
The wives of <s>Uśīnara</s> were born of the lineages of five royal sages:

children.text: mṛgā kṛmirnavā darvvā pañcamī ca dṛṣadvatī // Valc_2,12.14 //
children.translated_text: <s>Mṛgā</s>, <s>Kṛmi</s>, <s>Navā</s>, <s>Darvā</s>, and the fifth, <s>Dṛṣadvatī</s>. // Valc_2,12.14 //
The sons of <s>Uśīnara</s>, five upholders of the lineage, were born to these [wives],

children.text: tapasā caiva mahatā jātā vṛddhasya cātmajāḥ // Valc_2,12.15 //
children.translated_text: through great austerity, as sons of [that] aged [king]. // Valc_2,12.15 //
From <s>Nṛgā</s> was born the son <s>Nṛga</s>; from <s>Kṛmī</s> was born <s>Kṛmi</s>;

children.text: navāyāstu navaḥ putro darvvāyāḥ suvrato 'bhavat // Valc_2,12.16 //
children.translated_text: from <s>Navā</s>, the son <s>Nava</s>; from <s>Darvā</s>, <s>Suvrata</s> was born. // Valc_2,12.16 //
From <s>Dṛṣadvatī</s> was born <s>Śivi Auśīnara</s>, the king;

children.text: śivestu śivayaḥ khyātāḥ yaudheyāstu mṛgasya ha // Valc_2,12.17 //
children.translated_text: from <s>Śivi</s>, the <s>Śivayas</s> are renowned; and from <s>Mṛga</s>, the <s>Yaudheyas</s>. // Valc_2,12.17 //
Of <s>Nava</s>, the <s>Navarāṣṭra</s> [kingdom]; of <s>Kṛmi</s>, the city <s>Kṛmilā</s>;
and of <s>Suvrata</s>, the <s>Āmbaṣṭhas</s> — now learn of the sons of <s>Śivi</s>. // Valc_2,12.18 //
Of <s>Śivi</s>, the <s>Śivayas</s>, four sons, renowned in the world:
<s>Vṛṣadarbha</s>, <s>Suvīra</s>, <s>Kaikeya</s>, and <s>Madraka</s>. // Valc_2,12.19 //
Their prosperous territories: the <s>Kaikeyas</s>, the <s>Madrakas</s>,

children.text: vṛṣadarbhāḥ suvīrāśca titikṣoḥ śṛṇuta prajāḥ // Valc_2,12.20 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Vṛṣadarbhas</s>, and the <s>Suvīras</s> — now hear of the progeny of <s>Titikṣu</s>. // Valc_2,12.20 //
The descendants of <s>Titikṣu</s> — <s>Bhadrarāja</s> — were kings in the eastern direction;
<s>Uṣadratha</s>, of great resolve — <s>Phena</s> was his son. // Valc_2,12.21 //

children.text: pheṇātta sutapā jajñe sutaḥ sutapaso valiḥ /
children.translated_text: From <s>Phena</s> was born <s>Sutapā</s>; the son of <s>Sutapā</s> was <s>Vali</s> (Bali),

children.text: jāto mānuṣayaunau sa nṛpatiḥ kāñcaneṣudhiḥ // Valc_2,12.22 //
children.translated_text: born in the human race — that king with a golden quiver. // Valc_2,12.22 //

children.text: mahāyogī sa tu balirbabhūva nṛpatiḥ purā /
children.translated_text: That great <s>yogī</s>, King <s>Bali</s>, existed in ancient times;
he begot five sons, perpetuators of his lineage, on earth. // Valc_2,12.23 //

children.text: aṅgaḥ prathamato jajñe vaṅgaḥ suhmastathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: <s>Aṅga</s> was born first, then <s>Vaṅga</s>, then <s>Suhma</s>,

children.text: puṇḍraḥ kaliṅgaśca tathā bāleyaṃ kṣatramucyate // Valc_2,12.24 //
children.translated_text: <s>Puṇḍra</s>, and <s>Kaliṅga</s> — this is called the <s>Bāleya</s> (lineage of Bali) <s>Kṣatriya</s> race. // Valc_2,12.24 //
The <s>Bāleya</s> Brahmins also are perpetuators of his lineage on earth;

children.text: balestu brahmaṇā datto varaḥ prītena dhīmatā // Valc_2,12.25 //
children.translated_text: to <s>Bali</s>, a boon was given by <s>Brahmā</s>, who was pleased and wise: // Valc_2,12.25 //
great <s>yogī</s>-hood, and lifespan equal to a <s>kalpa</s> (cosmic age),
invincibility in battle, and preeminence in <s>dharma</s>,
the vision of the three worlds, and supremacy in progeny, // Valc_2,12.26 //
incomparability in strength, and the perception of the essence of <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: caturo niyatān varṇān tvañca sthāpayiteti ha // Valc_2,12.27 //
children.translated_text: 'and you shall establish the four ordained <s>varṇas</s> (social orders).' // Valc_2,12.27 //

children.text: ityukte vibhunā rājā baliḥ śāntiṃ parāṃ yayau /

children.translated_text: <s>Bali</s>, having consecrated his five sinless sons here, // Valc_2,12.28 //
fulfilled his purpose, his soul united with <s>yoga</s>, and relying on <s>yoga</s>, that lord,
invincible by all beings, watching for the [right] time, wandered as a sage. // Valc_2,12.29 //
When this was declared by the Lord, King <s>Bali</s> attained supreme peace;
After a great length of time, the resolute one reached his own abode;

children.text: teṣāṃ janapadāḥ pañca aṅgā vaṅgā sasuhmakā // Valc_2,12.30 //
children.translated_text: their five territories: <s>Aṅga</s>, <s>Vaṅga</s>, with <s>Suhma</s>, // Valc_2,12.30 //
<s>Kaliṅga</s>, and <s>Puṇḍra</s> — now hear of the progeny of <s>Aṅga</s>.
The son of <s>Aṅga</s> was the great king of kings, <s>Dadhivāhana</s>. // Valc_2,12.31 //
The son of <s>Dadhivāhana</s> was King <s>Diviratha</s>;

children.text: vidvān dharmmaratho nāma tasya citrarathaḥ sutaḥ // Valc_2,12.32 //
children.translated_text: the learned <s>Dharmaratha</s> by name — his son was <s>Citraratha</s>. // Valc_2,12.32 //
By that <s>Dharmaratha</s>, performing sacrifice on the mountain <s>Viṣṇupada</s>,

children.text: yajatā saha śakreṇa somaḥ pīto mahātmanā // Valc_2,12.33 //
children.translated_text: together with <s>Śakra</s> (Indra), <s>Soma</s> was drunk by that great soul. // Valc_2,12.33 //
Now, the son of <s>Citraratha</s> was <s>Daśaratha</s>;

children.text: lomapāda iti khyāto yasya śāntā sutābhavat // Valc_2,12.34 //
children.translated_text: he was known as <s>Lomapāda</s>, whose daughter was <s>Śāntā</s>. // Valc_2,12.34 //
His son, the heroic <s>Dāśarathi</s>, <s>Caturaṅga</s>, of great fame,
was born by the grace of <s>Ṛṣyaśṛṅga</s>, an increaser of his lineage. // Valc_2,12.35 //
The son of <s>Caturaṅga</s> was known as <s>Pṛthulākṣa</s>;

children.text: pṛthulākṣasuto rājā campo nāma mahāyaśāḥ // Valc_2,12.36 //
children.translated_text: the son of <s>Pṛthulākṣa</s> was the greatly renowned King <s>Campa</s>. // Valc_2,12.36 //

children.text: campasya tu purī campā yā mālinyabhavatpurā /
children.translated_text: The city of <s>Campa</s> was <s>Campā</s>, which was formerly called <s>Mālinī</s>;
by the grace of <s>Pūrṇabhadra</s>, <s>Haryakṣa</s> was his son. // Valc_2,12.37 //
Then, <s>Vaibhāṇḍaki</s> (the son of Vibhāṇḍaka) caused to descend upon the earth for him
<s>Vāraṇa</s>, the subduer of enemies — a supreme mount, by means of mantras. // Valc_2,12.38 //

children.text: haryyakṣasya tu dāyādo rājā bhadrarathaḥ smṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: The heir of <s>Haryakṣa</s> is remembered as King <s>Bhadraratha</s>;
the son of <s>Bhadraratha</s> was <s>Vṛhatkarman</s>, lord of creatures. // Valc_2,12.39 //
His son was <s>Vṛhadarbha</s>, from whom [was born] the greatly renowned <s>Vṛhanmanā</s>;

children.text: vṛhanmanāstu rājendro janayāmāsa vai sutam // Valc_2,12.40 //
children.translated_text: King <s>Vṛhanmanā</s>, foremost among kings, begot a son, // Valc_2,12.40 //
the hero <s>Jayadratha</s> by name, from whom King <s>Dṛḍharatha</s> [descended];
and the son of <s>Dṛḍharatha</s> was <s>Viśvajit</s>, the delight of the family. // Valc_2,12.41 //
His heir was <s>Karṇa</s>, and the son of that one was <s>Vikarṇa</s>;
his sons were a hundred, increasers of the <s>Aṅga</s> lineage. // Valc_2,12.42 //
The son of <s>Vṛhadarbha</s>, the king named <s>Vṛhanmanā</s>,

children.text: tasya patnīdvayaṃ cāsīt vainateyasute śubhe // Valc_2,12.43 //
children.translated_text: he had two wives, both auspicious daughters of <s>Vainateya</s> (Garuḍa). // Valc_2,12.43 //

children.text: yaśodevī ca satyā ca tābhyāṃ vaṃśastu vidyate /
children.translated_text: <s>Yaśodevī</s> and <s>Satyā</s> — from them the lineage is known;
King <s>Jayadratha</s>, the foremost of kings, was born to <s>Yaśodevī</s>. // Valc_2,12.44 //
In <s>Satyā</s> [was born] one named <s>Vijaya</s>, known as [one who combined] both Brahmin and <s>Kṣatriya</s> [qualities];

children.text: vijayasya dhṛtiḥ putrastasya putro dhṛtavrataḥ // Valc_2,12.45 //
children.translated_text: the son of <s>Vijaya</s> was <s>Dhṛti</s>; his son was <s>Dhṛtavrata</s>. // Valc_2,12.45 //
The son of <s>Dhṛtavrata</s> was <s>Satyakarmā</s>, of great fame;
his son was <s>Adhiratha</s>, also known by the other name <s>Sūta</s>. // Valc_2,12.46 //

children.text: yaḥ karṇaṃ pratijagrāha tena karṇastu sūtajaḥ /
children.translated_text: He who adopted <s>Karṇa</s> — hence <s>Karṇa</s> is [called] the son of a <s>Sūta</s> (charioteer);
the son of <s>Karṇa</s> was <s>Vṛṣasena</s>; <s>Pṛthusena</s> was his son. // Valc_2,12.47 //
In the line of <s>Pṛthusena</s>, the hero <s>Vīrasena</s> shall be born,
who shall marry <s>Somaṭā</s>, a daughter of a <s>Gauḍa</s> Brahmin family. // Valc_2,12.48 //
The kings born of that descendant line, of immeasurable prowess,
those heroes shall make the lords of the seven continents their vassals. // Valc_2,12.49 //
In that lineage, <s>Sāmantasena</s>, having become the mighty protector,
[shall rule] the earth girdled by oceans, from the <s>Vindhya</s> to the bridge [of Rāma (Setubandha)]. // Valc_2,12.50 //
<s>Siṃhagiri</s> said:
From him [arose] <s>Hemantasena</s>, O king — your grandfather,
the abode of splendors and glories, the fire that consumed the armies of enemies. // Valc_2,12.51 //
From him [arose] <s>Vijayasena</s>, a king who was a companion of the <s>Coḍa</s> (Chola) and <s>Gaṅga</s> [kings],
who conquered the entire earth girdled by the four oceans. // Valc_2,12.52 //
You are his son, <s>Vallāla</s>, a sovereign king of the whole earth,

children.text: pratyarthi-pṛthivīpālā yasya te śaraṇaṃ gatāḥ // Valc_2,12.53 //
children.translated_text: to whom rival kings have come for refuge. // Valc_2,12.53 //
That which is the origin of both Brahmin and <s>Kṣatriya</s> [lines], the lineage descended from <s>Kṣatriyas</s> —
the <s>Sena</s> lineage arose from that, in which also a <s>Pāṇḍava</s> was born. // Valc_2,12.54 //

children.text: dveṣṭi yaḥ pāṇḍavaṃ mūḍho durbuddhiśca vinindati /
children.translated_text: The fool who hates a <s>Pāṇḍava</s>, the one of evil intellect who reviles [him] —

children.text: sa viṣṭhāyāṃ kṛmirbhūtvā pacyeta narake ciram // Valc_2,12.55 //
children.translated_text: he, having become a worm in excrement, shall be cooked in hell for a long time. // Valc_2,12.55 //
He is <s>Vallabhānandacandra</s>, beloved of ten thousand moons;

children.text: tasyedānīṃ mahārāja kāryyaṃ bhavati śāsanam // Valc_2,12.56 //
children.translated_text: now, O great king, his command must be [carried out]. // Valc_2,12.56 //
He has a jewel of a daughter, of beauty unmatched on earth;

children.text: suprabhāmiva nābhāgastāṃ kanyāṃ hara paurava // Valc_2,12.57 //
children.translated_text: like <s>Suprabhā</s> to <s>Nābhāga</s> — take that maiden, O descendant of <s>Puru</s>! // Valc_2,12.57 //

children.text: uccandre sā yāti vālā gaurīṃ snātuṃ yadā yadā /
children.translated_text: When <s>Uccandra</s>'s daughter goes to bathe [at the shrine of] <s>Gaurī</s>,

children.text: tadā tadā tvarayati draṣṭuṃ tāmaruṇo 'ruṇam // Valc_2,12.58 //
children.translated_text: each time, <s>Aruṇa</s> (the Dawn) hastens the dawn to behold her. // Valc_2,12.58 //
When only two <s>daṇḍas</s> (time-units) of the night remain before the rising of dawn,

children.text: vilokya ghariyāreṣu viśvasanti na naigamāḥ // Valc_2,12.59 //
children.translated_text: the townspeople, seeing [the light], do not trust the water-clocks. // Valc_2,12.59 //

children.text: iti vallālacarite vyāsapurāṇe puruvaṃśakīrttanaṃ nāma dvādaśo 'dhyāyaḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus in the <s>Vallālacarita</s>, in the <s>Vyāsa Purāṇa</s>, the twelfth chapter called 'The Glorification of the <s>Puru</s> Lineage.'
Now, the thirteenth chapter.
<s>Vyāsa</s> said:

children.text: vedaḥ smṛtiḥ sadācāraḥ svasya ca priyamātmanaḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>Veda</s>, <s>Smṛti</s> (tradition), right conduct, and that which is pleasing to one's own self,
desire born of a proper resolve — this is remembered as the root of <s>dharma</s>. // Valc_2,13.1 //
Teaching, study, performing sacrifices, officiating at sacrifices,
giving, and accepting gifts — these are stated as the duties of Brahmins. // Valc_2,13.2 //
<s>Śruti</s> (revelation) and <s>Smṛti</s> (tradition) are the two eyes of Brahmins, created by the gods;
one lacking in one of them is one-eyed; one lacking both is declared blind. // Valc_2,13.3 //
In the nuptial fire, the householder should perform the domestic rites according to rule,
the procedure of the five great sacrifices, and the daily cooking. // Valc_2,13.4 //
Teaching is the <s>brahmayajña</s> (sacrifice to Brahman); the <s>pitṛyajña</s> (sacrifice to ancestors) is <s>tarpaṇa</s> (libation);

the <s>homa</s> (fire-offering) is the <s>daivayajña</s> (sacrifice to gods); the <s>balibhoga</s> (offering of food) is the <s>nṛyajña</s> (sacrifice to humans), which is the honoring of guests. // Valc_2,13.5 //
He who does not offer to the five — gods, guests, servants,

children.text: na nirvvapati pañcānāmucchvasanna sa jīvati // Valc_2,13.6 //
children.translated_text: ancestors, and himself — though breathing, does not truly live. // Valc_2,13.6 //
A Brahmin or a <s>Kṣatriya</s> staying for one night is considered a guest;
since his stay is impermanent, therefore he is called <s>atithi</s> (guest). // Valc_2,13.7 //
Even <s>Vaiśyas</s> and <s>Śūdras</s> who have arrived at one's household, fulfilling the duty of a guest,
should be fed along with the servants, showing compassion. // Valc_2,13.8 //
Always devoted to one's own wife, shunning the wives of others,
having performed the <s>homa</s> (fire-offering), one of noble mind should eat at evening and morning. // Valc_2,13.9 //
A twice-born, pressed by lack of livelihood, may accept [gifts] from all;

children.text: na bhaveddoṣabhāk tena jvalanārkasamo hi saḥ // Valc_2,13.10 //
children.translated_text: he would not be tainted by that fault, for he is like fire or the sun. // Valc_2,13.10 //
Protection of beings, charity, sacrifice, and study,
worship of <s>Śiva</s>, and likewise worship of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> — [these are prescribed] for <s>Kṣatriyas</s>. // Valc_2,13.11 //
Ever zealous in the slaying of robbers, he should display valor in battle;

children.text: nāsya kṛtyatamaṃ kiñcit rājño dasyuvinigrahāt // Valc_2,13.12 //
children.translated_text: there is no duty more paramount for a king than the suppression of robbers. // Valc_2,13.12 //
From spies, soldiers, thieves, and from great robbers and the like,

children.text: pīḍyamānāḥ prajā rakṣet kāyasthaiśca viśeṣataḥ // Valc_2,13.13 //
children.translated_text: he should protect the subjects who are being harassed, and especially from the <s>Kāyasthas</s> (scribes/officials). // Valc_2,13.13 //
Through honor, gifts, and respectful treatment, he should always maintain the <s>Vedic</s> scholars;
the nobleman should perform religious duties with great effort. // Valc_2,13.14 //
He should always maintain a learned person versed in <s>Nītiśāstra</s> (political science),

children.text: niyojayet sabhāmadhye nityaṃ sadbhiśca saṃyutaḥ // Valc_2,13.15 //
children.translated_text: and should appoint him in the assembly, always associated with good men. // Valc_2,13.15 //
He should go to sleep to the sound of musical instruments and wake up likewise;
he should contemplate the scriptures with his intellect, and all that is to be done. // Valc_2,13.16 //

children.text: dṛṣṭvā jyotirvvido vaidyān dadyāt gāṃ kāñcanaṃ mahīm /
children.translated_text: Having consulted astrologers and physicians, he should give cows, gold, and land,

children.text: niveśikāni ca tathā śrotriyāṇāṃ gṛhāni ca // Valc_2,13.17 //
children.translated_text: and also dwellings and houses to <s>Śrotriyas</s> (Vedic scholars). // Valc_2,13.17 //
Whatever <s>dharma</s> the king [earns] in protecting his own kingdom,

children.text: tameva kṛtsnamāpnoti pararāṣṭraṃ vaśaṃ nayan // Valc_2,13.18 //
children.translated_text: he obtains that very same in full by bringing another's kingdom under his control. // Valc_2,13.18 //
Devoted to the gods and Brahmins, dedicated to ancestral rites,

children.text: svabhāryyānirato nityaṃ ṣaḍbhāgārhaḥ sadā nṛpaḥ // Valc_2,13.19 //
children.translated_text: always devoted to his own wife — such a king is always worthy of a sixth [share of revenue]. // Valc_2,13.19 //
One share should be applied to the army, two shares for gifts,
one share for the subjects, and one share for the officials. // Valc_2,13.20 //
One share for personal enjoyment and the maintenance of family and the like;
thus the king should distribute expenditure in six portions of the revenue. // Valc_2,13.21 //
After worshipping at twilight, he should enjoy delightful song and music,

children.text: nṛtyagītaiśca jagdhīṃ vā strībhirniśi sukhāvahām // Valc_2,13.22 //
children.translated_text: and with dance, song, and dining — with women at night, bringing pleasure. // Valc_2,13.22 //
A <s>Vaiśya</s> should pursue cattle-rearing, agriculture, and trade according to rule;

children.text: dānaṃ deyaṃ yathāśaktyā brāhmaṇānāñca bhojanam // Valc_2,13.23 //
children.translated_text: he should give charity according to his ability, and feed the Brahmins. // Valc_2,13.23 //
Free from pride and delusion, truthful in speech, not censorious,
devoted to his own wife, self-controlled, shunning the wives of others, // Valc_2,13.24 //
having fed Brahmins with wealth, and the officiating priests at the time of sacrifice,
he should live in a state of non-sovereignty, devoted to <s>dharma</s> until the fall of the body. // Valc_2,13.25 //
He should perform sacrifices, study, and charity always without laziness,
devoted to ancestral rites and dedicated to the worship of <s>Viṣṇu</s> and <s>Śiva</s>. // Valc_2,13.26 //
A <s>Śūdra</s> should diligently perform service to the three <s>varṇas</s> (social classes),
and should especially conduct himself as a servant toward <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>.
He should be a giver without being asked, and should resort to agriculture for his livelihood;

children.text: śuddhā tu vṛttistasyaiva kāru-cāraṇa-karmma ca // Valc_2,13.28 //
children.translated_text: pure livelihood for him consists of artisan work and the occupation of a wandering performer.
He should worship the gods through the rites of <s>pākayajña</s> (cooked-food sacrifice), without laziness;

children.text: tasya tu dvijaśuśrūṣā paro dharmmaḥ prakīrttitaḥ // Valc_2,13.29 //
children.translated_text: for him, service to the twice-born is declared to be the highest <s>dharma</s> (duty).
Wearing worn-out clothing, eating the leftovers of a <s>Vipra</s> (Brāhmaṇa),
taking pleasure in one's own wife, and avoiding the wives of others —
folio marker

children.text: lavaṇaṃ madhutailaṃ ca dadhi takraṃ ghṛtaṃ payaḥ /
children.translated_text: salt, honey, oil, curd, buttermilk, ghee, and milk —

children.text: na duṣyecchūdrajātīnāṃ kuryyāt sarvvasya vikrayam // Valc_2,13.31 //
children.translated_text: these are not defiled by those of <s>Śūdra</s> birth; he may sell all of these.
For all classes, livelihood through hired service with different occupations is blameless;
agriculture with different ploughs is prescribed by <s>Manu</s> and others for <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and the rest.
By <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, a plough of sixteen oxen; by the next classes, four fewer;

children.text: dvigavaṃ vāntyajaiḥ sīraṃ dṛṣṭvā bhūmārddavaṃ tathā // Valc_2,13.33 //
children.translated_text: by the lowest castes, a plough of two oxen — having assessed the softness of the soil.
Having broken the earth, cut the plants, and killed insects and ants,

children.text: punanti khalu yajñena karṣakā devapūjanāt // Valc_2,13.34 //
children.translated_text: farmers indeed purify themselves through <s>yajña</s> (sacrifice) and worship of the gods.
Through sacred Vedic rites, the bodily <s>saṃskāras</s> (purificatory rites) beginning with <s>niṣeka</s> (conception)

children.text: kāryyaḥ śarīrasaṃskāraḥ pāvanaḥ pretya ceha ca // Valc_2,13.35 //
children.translated_text: should be performed for the twice-born — purifying both in this world and the next.
<s>Garbhādhāna</s> (the rite of conception) is performed during the wife's fertile period; <s>puṃsavana</s> (the rite for a male child) before the quickening;

children.text: turyye 'ṣṭame vā sīmanto janane jātakarmma ca // Valc_2,13.36 //
children.translated_text: in the fourth or eighth month, <s>sīmanta</s> (the parting-of-the-hair ceremony); and at birth, <s>jātakarma</s> (the birth rite).
<s>Niṣkrama</s> (the first outing) in the third month; <s>nāma</s> (the naming ceremony) at the completion of a hundred days;

children.text: ṣaṣṭhe 'nnaprāśanaṃ cūḍā janyabde vā yathākulam // Valc_2,13.37 //
children.translated_text: in the sixth month, <s>annaprāśana</s> (the first feeding of solid food); <s>cūḍā</s> (the tonsure) in the birth year or according to family custom.
<s>Karṇavedha</s> (ear-piercing), <s>vratādeśa</s> (instruction for observances), <s>vedārambha</s> (commencement of Vedic study), the rite of initiation,
<s>keśānta</s> (the first shaving of the beard), <s>snāna</s> (the ceremonial bath), <s>udvāha</s> (marriage), <s>vivāhāgniparigraha</s> (taking up the marriage fire),
and the taking up of the three sacred fires — these are declared to be the sixteen <s>saṃskāras</s>.

children.text: navaitāḥ karṇavedhāntāḥ mantravarjjaṃ kriyā striyāḥ // Valc_2,13.39 //
children.translated_text: Of these, nine up to ear-piercing are performed for women as well, but without Vedic <s>mantras</s>.

children.text: vipro garbhāṣṭame varṣe kṣatra ekādaśe tathā /
children.translated_text: A <s>Vipra</s> (Brāhmaṇa) in the eighth year from conception, a <s>Kṣatriya</s> in the eleventh,
and one born of the <s>Vaiśya</s> class in the twelfth — is eligible for the <s>vratopanayana</s> (investiture with the sacred thread).
For one who has attained the proper age, the time limit extends to double that;
one who falls from Vedic observance becomes a <s>vrātya</s> (outcaste) — such a <s>vrātya</s> is eligible for the <s>vrātyastoma</s> (redemptive sacrifice).
<s>Brāhma</s>, <s>Daiva</s>, likewise <s>Ārṣa</s>, <s>Prājāpatya</s>, and then <s>Āsura</s>,
<s>Gāndharva</s>, <s>Rākṣasa</s>, and <s>Paiśāca</s> — the eighth and the lowest.

children.text: ete dharmmāstu catvāraḥ pūrvvaṃ vipre prakīrttitāḥ /
children.translated_text: The first four of these forms of marriage are declared for <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>;
<s>Gāndharva</s> and <s>Rākṣasa</s> are commended for the <s>Kṣatriya</s>.
The <s>Brāhma</s> marriage is declared as giving the bride unsolicited, with effort;
the <s>Prājāpatya</s> is declared as the giving upon a request for a desired purpose.
The <s>Āsura</s> involves the giving of wealth; the <s>Gāndharva</s> arises from mutual agreement;
the <s>Rākṣasa</s> from abduction in battle; the <s>Paiśāca</s> from deception of the maiden.

children.text: tisrastu bhāryyāḥ kṣatrasya bhāryaikā brāhmaṇasya tu /
children.translated_text: A <s>Kṣatriya</s> may have three wives; a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, however, only one wife;

children.text: ekaiva bhāryyā vaiśyasya śūdrasya ca vidhīyate // Valc_2,13.46 //
children.translated_text: one wife is ordained for the <s>Vaiśya</s>, and one for the <s>Śūdra</s> as well.

children.text: kṣatriyā vaiśyā śūdrā ca kṣatriyasya prakīrttitā /
children.translated_text: A <s>Kṣatriya</s> woman, a <s>Vaiśya</s> woman, and a <s>Śūdra</s> woman are declared for the <s>Kṣatriya</s>;

children.text: ekaiva bhāryyā viprasya brāhmaṇī tu vidhīyate // Valc_2,13.47 //
children.translated_text: but the one wife of a <s>Vipra</s> (Brāhmaṇa) is ordained to be a <s>Brāhmaṇī</s> alone.

children.text: vaiśyaiva bhāryyā vaiśyasya śūdrā śūdrasya kīrttitā /
children.translated_text: A <s>Vaiśya</s> woman alone is the wife of a <s>Vaiśya</s>; a <s>Śūdra</s> woman is declared for the <s>Śūdra</s>;
a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should never marry a maiden not of his own <s>varṇa</s> (class).
From a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> with a <s>Vaiśya</s> maiden, an <s>Ambaṣṭha</s> (mixed-caste offspring) is born;

children.text: sa tu śūdratvamāpanno vivahenna tato viśām // Valc_2,13.49 //
children.translated_text: he, having attained the status of a <s>Śūdra</s>, should not thereafter marry into the <s>Vaiśya</s> community.
As for the fall from caste that is said to result for a <s>Kṣatriya</s> who takes a <s>Śūdra</s> wife,

children.text: naitanmama mataṃ jñeyaṃ sā tenonnīyate yataḥ // Valc_2,13.50 //
children.translated_text: that should not be regarded as my view, since she is thereby elevated by him.
A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and a <s>Vaiśya</s> fall by marrying a <s>Śūdra</s> maiden;
but there is no fall for a <s>Kṣatriya</s> from taking a <s>Śūdra</s> wife.
Even marriage with a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> maiden was performed by royal sages of old;

children.text: tejīyasāṃ na doṣāya vahneḥ sarvvabhujo yathā // Valc_2,13.52 //
children.translated_text: for the mighty, there is no fault — just as fire consumes everything.
folio marker
A king should not be slighted with the thought that he is a mere mortal — so said <s>Manu</s>;

children.text: mahatī devatā hyeṣā nararūpeṇa tiṣṭhati // Valc_2,13.53 //
children.translated_text: for this is a great deity standing in human form.
What has been practiced by the gods, what has been practiced by the sages —
that should not be left unperformed by men; one should carry out the prescribed action.
Having married a woman of equal <s>varṇa</s>, one may freely wed one who is not a <s>Brāhmaṇī</s>;

children.text: tasyāmutpāditaḥ putro na savarṇāt prahīyate // Valc_2,13.55 //
children.translated_text: a son begotten upon her is not inferior to one born of the equal-caste wife.

children.text: kṣatrājjātaḥ kṣatriyāyāṃ kṣatriyaḥ syāt na saṃśayaḥ /
children.translated_text: One born from a <s>Kṣatriya</s> with a <s>Kṣatriya</s> woman is a <s>Kṣatriya</s> without doubt;

children.text: vaiśyāyāṃ ca tathaiva syāt śadrāyāmapi caiva hi // Valc_2,13.56 //
children.translated_text: and so too from a <s>Vaiśya</s> woman, and indeed from a <s>Śūdra</s> woman as well.
As long as a man does not obtain a wife, so long he remains but half;

children.text: nārddhaṃ prajāyate sarvvaṃ prajāyete iti śrutiḥ // Valc_2,13.57 //
children.translated_text: he is not half — everything is born — so declares the <s>Śruti</s> (Vedic revelation).
When a willing maiden gives herself in union, there is no transgression;

children.text: kintvalaṃkṛtya satkṛtya sa evaināṃ samudvahet // Valc_2,13.58 //
children.translated_text: but he should adorn and honor her, and should marry her himself.
One should first marry a wife of equal <s>varṇa</s> for the fulfillment of <s>dharma</s>;
thereafter, a king may marry as he pleases, provided it is in the natural order and not in the reverse.
Just as <s>amṛta</s> (nectar) may be taken even from poison, as gold from an impure substance,
as the highest knowledge from one of low status — so too a jewel of a woman from a lowly family.
Women, gems, knowledge, <s>dharma</s>, purity, good speech,

children.text: vividhāni ca śilpāni samādeyāni sarvvataḥ // Valc_2,13.61 //
children.translated_text: and various arts — these may be received from anywhere.

children.text: yatra nāryyastu pūjyante ramante tatra devatāḥ /
children.translated_text: Where women are honored, there the gods rejoice;

children.text: yatraitāstu na pūjyante sarvvāstatrāphalāḥ kriyāḥ // Valc_2,13.62 //
children.translated_text: where they are not honored, all rites are fruitless.
Of great fortune, worthy of worship, illuminators of the household —

children.text: striyaḥ śriyaśca geheṣu na viśeṣo 'sti kaścana // Valc_2,13.63 //
children.translated_text: between women and <s>Śrī</s> (the goddess of prosperity) in the home, there is no difference whatsoever.
The begetting of offspring, the nurturing of those born,

children.text: pratyahaṃ lokayātrāyāḥ pratyakṣaṃ strī nibandhanam // Valc_2,13.64 //
children.translated_text: and the daily conduct of worldly life — all these visibly depend upon women.
Offspring, household duties, devoted service, and the highest pleasure —
heaven itself for one's ancestors and oneself depends upon one's wife.

children.text: iti vallālacarite vyāsapurāṇe varṇadharmmādikīrttanaṃ nāma trayodaśo 'dhyāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Vallālacarita</s>, in the <s>Vyāsapurāṇa</s>, the chapter entitled 'The Declaration of <s>Varṇadharma</s> and Other Duties' — the thirteenth chapter.
folio marker
Now begins the fourteenth chapter.
<s>Vyāsa</s> said:
A praiseworthy woman is one whose every limb is beautiful, who walks with the gait of an elephant in rut,
who has full, heavy hips, and eyes like those of a black antelope.
With beautiful dark hair, slender of body, with fine body hair, captivating,

children.text: samabhūmispṛśau pādau saṃhatau ca tathā stanau // Valc_2,14.2 //
children.translated_text: whose feet touch the ground evenly, and whose breasts are firm and close-set.
Her navel spirals to the right; her secret part is shaped like a leaf of the <s>aśvattha</s> (sacred fig) tree;
her ankles are well-concealed, and the distance from her waist to her navel measures a thumb's breadth.
With cheeks like <s>madhūka</s> flowers, neither veiny nor hairy,
neither with knitted brows nor frowning — devoted to her husband, dear to her husband.
a young woman takes pleasure in garments, ornaments, embraces, and the like.
A young girl is delighted by playthings given at the proper time and by eating divine fruits;
A mature woman in the prime of life is gratified by skill in the arts of love;

children.text: vṛddhā tu madhurālāpai rgauraveṇa ca yujyate // Valc_2,14.6 //
children.translated_text: an aged woman is won over by sweet words and is honored with respect.
A girl of sixteen years is considered a <s>bālā</s> (young maiden); up to thirty, she is in the bloom of youth;

children.text: pañca pañcāśatā prauḍhā vṛddhā strī tadanantaram // Valc_2,14.7 //
children.translated_text: up to fifty-five, she is a <s>prauḍhā</s> (mature woman); thereafter, a woman is considered old.
They should be enjoyed but not overindulged by a king who seeks dominion.
When a woman is sixteen years of age, a man of twenty-four years,
if wise, should make the effort, desiring the finest pleasure.
Women are indeed subject to desire; for that purpose is the collection of gems.

children.text: tathā pūrṇāṅgavīryyau tau puttraṃ janayataḥ param /
children.translated_text: When both are thus of full body and vigor, they beget an excellent son,
endowed with all the senses, strong, and destined to live a hundred years.
In summer and autumn, a slender woman is considered beneficial for a pleasure-seeking man;
a young woman in the cold season; and one of middle age during the rains and spring.

children.text: nityaṃ bālā sevyamānā nityaṃ varddhayate balam /
children.translated_text: A young maiden, constantly enjoyed, constantly increases one's strength;
a youthful woman diminishes one's vigor; a middle-aged woman brings on old age.

children.text: sadyo māṃsaṃ ca śālyannaṃ bālāstrīsevanaṃ ghṛtam /
children.translated_text: Fresh meat, rice cooked with <s>śāli</s> (fine rice), the company of a young woman, ghee,

children.text: kṣīramuṣṇodake snānaṃ sadyaḥ prāṇakarāṇi ṣaṭ // Valc_2,14.13 //
children.translated_text: milk, and bathing in hot water — these six immediately restore vital energy.

children.text: seveta kāmataḥ kāmī balāt vājīkṛto hime /
children.translated_text: A man desirous of pleasure, strengthened by aphrodisiacs, may indulge freely in winter;

children.text: prakāmaṃ tu niṣeveta surataṃ śiśirāgame // Valc_2,14.14 //
children.translated_text: and he should enjoy lovemaking abundantly at the onset of the cool season.

children.text: śīte rātrau dine grīṣme vasante ca divāniśi /
children.translated_text: In the cold season, at night; in summer, during the day; in spring, both day and night;
in the rainy season, when clouds thunder; and in autumn, at the appropriate time, with passion.
One filled with desire, having first aroused her through embraces and other caresses,
should skillfully unite with the beloved, invigorated by aphrodisiacs.
Daily bathing in warm water, drinking milk, fresh young women,
O kings, this is wholesome for you — food that is well-oiled and in small quantity.
By a preparation of <s>kapittha</s> (wood-apple) powder, or with curd, or with <s>sṛja</s> (resin),

children.text: ghṛtaṃ sugandhi bhavati dugdhaiḥ kṣiptaistathā yavaiḥ // Valc_2,14.18 //
children.translated_text: ghee becomes fragrant; likewise by adding milk and barley.
folio marker
Such is the preparation of food; now the art of fragrance is set forth.

children.text: śaucamācamanaṃ samyak tathaiva ca virecanam // Valc_2,14.19 //
children.translated_text: Purification, proper rinsing, and also cleansing,

children.text: bhāvanā caiva pākaśca bodhanaṃ dhūpanaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: infusion, cooking, awakening, fumigation,
and scenting — these are prescribed as the eightfold process.
With the young shoots of <s>kapittha</s> (wood-apple), <s>bilva</s> (bael), <s>jambū</s> (rose-apple), <s>āmra</s> (mango), and <s>karavīraka</s> (oleander),

children.text: kṛtvodakantu yaddravyaṃ śocitaṃ śaucanantu tat // Valc_2,14.21 //
children.translated_text: whatever substance is purified by preparing it with water — that is called purification.
In the absence of these, purification may be achieved with musk-water.

children.text: nakhaṃ kuṣṭhaṃ ghanaṃ māṃsaṃ spṛkkā śaileyajaṃ jalam // Valc_2,14.22 //
children.translated_text: <s>Nakha</s> (nail-shell), <s>kuṣṭha</s> (costus root), <s>ghana</s> (nutgrass), <s>māṃsa</s> (spikenard), <s>spṛkkā</s> (priyangu), <s>śaileya</s> (rock lichen) — these with water,
and likewise <s>kuṅkuma</s> (saffron), <s>lākṣā</s> (lac), <s>candana</s> (sandalwood), <s>aguru</s> (aloe-wood), <s>nīrada</s> (vetiver),

children.text: saralaṃ devakāṣṭhañca karparaṃ kāntayā saha // Valc_2,14.23 //
children.translated_text: <s>sarala</s> (pine resin), <s>devakāṣṭha</s> (deodar wood), <s>karpara</s> (camphor), together with <s>kāntā</s> (a fragrant substance),
<s>bālā</s> (a fragrant herb), <s>kunduraka</s> (frankincense), <s>guggulu</s> (bdellium), <s>śrīnivāsaka</s> (a resinous substance),
together with <s>sarjarasa</s> (sal resin) — these are the twenty-one incense ingredients.
From this group of twenty-one incense substances, as one wishes,

children.text: dve dve dravye samādāya sarjjabhāgairniyojayet // Valc_2,14.25 //
children.translated_text: taking any two substances at a time, one should combine them with portions of <s>sarjarasa</s> (sal resin).
By combining nail-shell, oil-cake, and sandalwood paste with honey,

children.text: dhūpayogā bhavantīha yathāvat svecchayā kṛtāḥ // Valc_2,14.26 //
children.translated_text: incense preparations are made here, properly and as desired.

children.text: tvacaṃ nāḍīṃ phalaṃ tailaṃ kuṅkumaṃ granthiparṇakam /
children.translated_text: Bark, root, fruit, oil, <s>kuṅkuma</s> (saffron), <s>granthiparṇaka</s> (patchouli),

children.text: śaileyaṃ tagaraṃ kāntām colakarpūrameva ca // Valc_2,14.27 //
children.translated_text: <s>śaileya</s> (rock lichen), <s>tagara</s> (valerian), <s>kāntā</s>, and <s>colakarpūra</s> (a type of camphor),
<s>māsī</s> (a fragrant plant), <s>murā</s> (a fragrant root), and <s>kuṣṭha</s> (costus root) — these are prescribed as bathing substances.
From these, taking any three substances as one wishes,
combined with musk, a bath should be prepared that enhances desire.
With equal parts of cinnamon bark, <s>murā</s>, and <s>nalada</s> (Indian spikenard), combined with half a portion of <s>vāsaka</s>,
the bath acquires the fragrance of the blue lotus; with oil added, it becomes saffron-scented.
It becomes fragrant like <s>jāti</s> (jasmine) flowers when combined with half a portion of <s>tagara</s> (valerian);
with <s>vāsaka</s> and <s>vakula</s> (mimusops) flowers, it acquires a matching fragrance, captivating.

children.text: mañjiṣṭhā tagaraṃ colaṃ tvacaṃ vyāghranakhaṃ nakham /
children.translated_text: <s>Mañjiṣṭhā</s> (madder), <s>tagara</s> (valerian), <s>cola</s> (a fragrant bark), cinnamon bark, <s>vyāghranakha</s> (tiger's claw shell), <s>nakha</s> (nail-shell),
and <s>gandhapattra</s> (bay leaf) — arranging these, a fragrant oil of excellent quality is produced.
Oil scented with <s>mallī</s> (jasmine) flowers, pressed from sesame, is beloved of women.
Oil pressed in the mill from sesame seeds perfumed with flowers

children.text: vāsanāt puṣpasadṛśaṃ gandhena tu bhaveddhruvam // Valc_2,14.32 //
children.translated_text: would surely become similar to the flowers in fragrance due to the perfuming. // <s>Valc</s> 2,14.32 //
Cardamom, clove, <s>kakkola</s> (pepper berry), nutmeg, and turmeric,
together with mace — these are independent mouth-fresheners. // <s>Valc</s> 2,14.33 //
Camphor, saffron, a lovely musk-deer's navel secretion, <s>hareṇuka</s> (a fragrant seed),
<s>kakkola</s>, cardamom, clove, and nutmeg and its outer covering, // <s>Valc</s> 2,14.34 //

children.text: tvakpatraṃ truṭimustau ca latāṃ kasturikaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: cinnamon bark, <s>truṭi</s> (a spice), <s>mustā</s> (cyperus grass), <s>latā</s> (a creeper), and musk likewise,

children.text: kaṇṭakāni lavaṅgasya phalapatre ca jātitaḥ // Valc_2,14.35 //
children.translated_text: the thorns of clove, the fruit-leaves of nutmeg — // <s>Valc</s> 2,14.35 //
taking <s>kuṭaka</s> and its fruit, one should prepare the ingredients in <s>kārṣika</s> (one <s>karṣa</s>) measures;

children.text: taccūrṇe khadiraṃ sāraṃ dadyātturyyantu vāsitam // Valc_2,14.36 //
children.translated_text: to that powder, one should add the essence of <s>khadira</s> (catechu), the fourth part being perfumed. // <s>Valc</s> 2,14.36 //
From this, auspicious pills should be made with the juice of mango;
placed in the mouth, they are fragrant and destroy diseases of the mouth. // <s>Valc</s> 2,14.37 //
Betel-nut, properly washed with water of the five leaves,

children.text: śaktyā tu guṭikā dravyairvāsitaṃ mukhavāsakam // Valc_2,14.38 //
children.translated_text: with pills prepared as far as possible from fragrant ingredients — this is the mouth-freshener. // <s>Valc</s> 2,14.38 //
A pungent toothbrush-stick, soaked in cow's urine for three days,
properly prepared like betel-nut — this also produces fragrance of the mouth. // <s>Valc</s> 2,14.39 //
Equal portions of cinnamon and <s>pathyā</s> (chebulic myrobalan), combined with half a portion of camphor —
a mouth-freshener equal to betel-leaf (<s>nāgavallī</s>) appears, captivating. // <s>Valc</s> 2,14.40 //

children.text: evaṃ kuryyāt sadā strīṇāṃ rakṣaṇaṃ pṛthivīpatiḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, a king should always ensure the protection of women,
and should never trust them — especially the mother of his son. // <s>Valc</s> 2,14.41 //

children.text: iti vallālacarite vyāsapurāṇe strīlakṣaṇādikīrttanaṃ nāma caturdaśo 'dhyāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fourteenth chapter, named 'The Description of the Characteristics of Women and Other Matters,' in the <s>Vallālacarita</s>, a <s>Vyāsapurāṇa</s>.
Now begins the fifteenth chapter.
<s>Vyāsa</s> said:
In the <s>Kṛtayuga</s>, <s>tapas</s> (austerity) is supreme; in the <s>Tretā</s>, knowledge is declared supreme;
in the <s>Dvāpara</s>, they say sacrifice alone; in the <s>Kaliyuga</s>, charity (<s>dāna</s>) alone. // <s>Valc</s> 2,15.1 //

children.text: dānadharmmāt paro dharmmo bhūtānāṃ neha vidyate /
children.translated_text: There is no <s>dharma</s> higher than the <s>dharma</s> of giving for living beings here;
one desiring heavenly life, prosperity, and merit should give for the pacification of sins. // <s>Valc</s> 2,15.2 //
Nothing greater than charity is seen in the three worlds;

children.text: dānena prāpyate svargaḥ śrī dānenaiva labhyate // Valc_2,15.3 //
children.translated_text: through charity one attains heaven; through charity alone is fortune obtained. // <s>Valc</s> 2,15.3 //
Through charity one conquers enemies; through charity disease is destroyed;

children.text: dānena labhyate vidyā dānena yuvatījanaḥ // Valc_2,15.4 //
children.translated_text: through charity one attains learning; through charity, the company of young women. // <s>Valc</s> 2,15.4 //
Through charity one obtains pleasures; through charity one finds long life;
it is considered the supreme means for <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, <s>kāma</s>, and <s>mokṣa</s>. // <s>Valc</s> 2,15.5 //
One should give facing east; one should receive facing north.

children.text: āyurvvivarddhate dāturgṛhītuḥ kṣīyate na tat // Valc_2,15.6 //
children.translated_text: The life of the giver increases; that of the recipient does not diminish. // <s>Valc</s> 2,15.6 //
A gift to one's mother yields a hundredfold merit; to one's father, a thousandfold, it is said;
to one's daughter, the merit is infinite; to one's sibling, what is given is imperishable. // <s>Valc</s> 2,15.7 //

children.text: amanuṣye samaṃ dānaṃ pāpe jñeyaṃ mahāphalam /
children.translated_text: A gift to a non-human being yields equal merit; to a sinner, it should be known as of great fruit;

children.text: varṇasaṅkare dviguṇaṃ śūdre dānaṃ caturguṇam // Valc_2,15.8 //
children.translated_text: to a person of mixed caste, it is doubled; to a <s>Śūdra</s>, a gift yields fourfold merit. // <s>Valc</s> 2,15.8 //
To a <s>Vaiśya</s>, eightfold; to a <s>Kṣatriya</s>, sixteenfold; to one versed in the two <s>Vedas</s>, (it is called supreme);
to a student of the <s>Vedas</s>, a hundredfold; to a teacher of the <s>Vedas</s>, it is infinite. // <s>Valc</s> 2,15.9 //
A gift to a preceptor, family priest, and the like is declared imperishable;
what is given to the destitute is infinite, and so also to one who performs sacrifices. // <s>Valc</s> 2,15.10 //

children.text: kanyā dāsāstathā dāsī prājāpatyāḥ prakīrttitāḥ // Valc_2,15.11 /
children.translated_text: maidens, male servants, and female servants are proclaimed to belong to <s>Prajāpati</s>. // <s>Valc</s> 2,15.11 //
An elephant is declared to belong to <s>Prajāpati</s>; a horse to <s>Yama</s> as its deity;

children.text: tathā caikaśaphāḥ sarvve yāmyaśca mahiṣastathā // Valc_2,15.12 //
children.translated_text: and all single-hoofed animals likewise; the buffalo also belongs to <s>Yama</s>. // <s>Valc</s> 2,15.12 //
The gift of safety belongs to all deities; land indeed has <s>Viṣṇu</s> as its deity;
The camel belongs to <s>Nirṛti</s>; cows to <s>Rudra</s>; the goat to <s>Agni</s> (Fire);

children.text: āpyo meṣo hariḥ kroḍaḥ āraṇyāḥ paśavo nilāḥ // Valc_2,15.13 //
children.translated_text: the ram to <s>Āpas</s> (Water); <s>Hari</s> is the boar; forest animals are of <s>Nīla</s> (the Wind). // <s>Valc</s> 2,15.13 //
A water reservoir belongs to <s>Varuṇa</s>; water-vessels such as pots likewise;
ocean-born gems and gold and iron belong to <s>Agni</s> (Fire). // <s>Valc</s> 2,15.14 //
Crops belong to <s>Prajāpati</s>; cooked food also, O kings;

children.text: gāndharbba gandhamityāhu rvastraṃ vārhaspataṃ smṛtam // Valc_2,15.15 //
children.translated_text: fragrance is said to belong to the <s>Gandharvas</s>; cloth is considered to belong to <s>Bṛhaspati</s>. // <s>Valc</s> 2,15.15 //

children.text: vāyavyāḥ pakṣiṇaḥ sarvve vidyā brāhmī tathāṅgakam /
children.translated_text: All birds belong to <s>Vāyu</s> (Wind); learning belongs to <s>Brahmā</s>, as do the limbs (of the <s>Vedas</s>);

children.text: sārasvataṃ pustakādi viśvakarmmā tu śilpake // Valc_2,15.16 //
children.translated_text: books and the like belong to <s>Sarasvatī</s>; craftsmanship belongs to <s>Viśvakarmā</s>. // <s>Valc</s> 2,15.16 //
Trees and plants have the forest-lord as their deity; the substance-god is the body of <s>Hari</s>;

children.text: chatraṃ kṛṣṇājinaṃ śayyā ratha āsanameva ca // Valc_2,15.17 //
children.translated_text: a parasol, a black-antelope skin, a bed, a chariot, and a seat, // <s>Valc</s> 2,15.17 //
a pair of shoes, and a vehicle — these eight are declared to belong to <s>Aṅgiras</s>;
chariot-equipment, weapons, banners, and the like belong to all deities. // <s>Valc</s> 2,15.18 //

children.text: śivo vā na tato dravyaṃ vyatiriktaṃ yato 'sti hi // Valc_2,15.19 /
children.translated_text: or <s>Śiva</s> — there is no substance that is excluded from these. // <s>Valc</s> 2,15.19 //
Hear! I shall now declare the sixteen great gifts (<s>mahādānas</s>). // <s>Valc</s> 2,15.20 //
A house also belongs to all deities; everything has <s>Viṣṇu</s> as its deity,
<s>Tulāpuruṣa</s> (weighing a man in gold) is the first; then the gift of a golden embryo (<s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>);
<s>Brahmāṇḍa</s> (cosmic egg), <s>Kalpavṛkṣa</s> (wish-fulfilling tree), and a thousand cows as the fifth. // <s>Valc</s> 2,15.21 //
A golden wish-fulfilling cow (<s>Hiraṇyakāmadhenu</s>) and a golden horse (<s>Hiraṇyāśva</s>) as the seventh,
a golden horse-chariot (<s>Hiraṇyāśvaratha</s>) likewise, and a golden elephant-chariot (<s>Hemahastiratha</s>), // <s>Valc</s> 2,15.22 //
the five-plough gift (<s>Pañcalāṅgalaka</s>) likewise, and the land-gift (<s>Dharādāna</s>) of great fruit;
the twelfth is the Disc of <s>Viṣṇu</s> (<s>Viṣṇucakra</s>); then the Wish-fulfilling Creeper (<s>Kalpalatā</s>). // <s>Valc</s> 2,15.23 //
The gift of the Seven Oceans (<s>Saptasāgara</s>), and the Jewel-cow (<s>Ratnadhenu</s>) likewise,
and the Great Element Vessel (<s>Mahābhūtaghaṭa</s>) — these gifts should be offered on an auspicious day. // <s>Valc</s> 2,15.24 //
On a ritual platform (<s>maṇḍapa</s>), on a ritual diagram (<s>maṇḍala</s>), one should offer the gift, invoking the gods of the eastern direction, to a twice-born;

children.text: dravyasya nāma gṛhṇīyāt dadāni ca tathā vadet // Valc_2,15.25 //
children.translated_text: one should take the name of the substance and also say 'I give.' // <s>Valc</s> 2,15.25 //

children.text: toyaṃ dadyāttato haste dāne vidhirayaṃ smṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then one should give water into the hand — this is the prescribed ritual for gifts;

children.text: manasā pātramuddiśya jalaṃ bhūmau vinikṣapet // Valc_2,15.26 //
children.translated_text: mentally designating the recipient, one should sprinkle water on the ground. // <s>Valc</s> 2,15.26 //

children.text: vidyate sāgarasyānto dānasyānto na vidyate // Valc_2,15.27 //
children.translated_text: The ocean has a limit; charity has no limit. // <s>Valc</s> 2,15.27 //
[The giving formula:] To one of such name, such <s>gotra</s> (lineage), such <s>pravara</s> (ancestral line), facing such direction,
to a worthy recipient endowed with the <s>Vedas</s> and <s>Vedāṅgas</s>, of great soul, // <s>Valc</s> 2,15.28 //
for the increase of merit and fame of one's mother, father, and oneself,
for the pacification of all sins, for the attainment of heaven, for enjoyment and liberation, // <s>Valc</s> 2,15.29 //
this great substance of such name, having <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, and other deities,

children.text: etattubhyaṃ sampradade prīyatāṃ me hariḥ śivaḥ // Valc_2,15.30 //
children.translated_text: I bestow upon you — may <s>Hari</s> and <s>Śiva</s> be pleased with me! // <s>Valc</s> 2,15.30 //
For the establishment of this gift, I give gold as the fee (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>);

children.text: anena dānavākyena sarvvadānāni vai dadet // Valc_2,15.31 //
children.translated_text: with this formula of giving, all gifts should be given. // <s>Valc</s> 2,15.31 //
When gold is being given, silver is prescribed as the fee;

children.text: anyeṣāmapi dānānāṃ suvarṇaṃ dakṣiṇā smṛtā // Valc_2,15.32 //
children.translated_text: for all other gifts, gold is considered the fee. // <s>Valc</s> 2,15.32 //

children.text: suvarṇaṃ rajataṃ tāmraṃ taṇḍulaṃ dhānyameva ca /
children.translated_text: Gold, silver, copper, husked rice, and unhusked grain —
daily <s>śrāddha</s> and worship of gods — all these are without fee (self-sufficient). // <s>Valc</s> 2,15.33 //
Silver is the fee in ancestral rites — it accomplishes <s>dharma</s>, <s>kāma</s>, and <s>artha</s>;

children.text: suvarṇaṃ rajataṃ tāmraṃ maṇimuktāvasūni ca // Valc_2,15.34 //
children.translated_text: gold, silver, copper, gems, pearls, and riches — // <s>Valc</s> 2,15.34 //
all this, O wise one, is given by one who gives the earth;
such a one satisfies the ancestors in the world of the ancestors and the gods in the abode of the gods. // <s>Valc</s> 2,15.35 //
He who, with a serene soul, gives the earth —

children.text: kharvvaṭaṃ kheṭakaṃ vāpi grāmaṃ vā śasyaśālinam // Valc_2,15.36 //
children.translated_text: whether a market-town, a hamlet, or a village rich in grain, // <s>Valc</s> 2,15.36 //
or a hundred <s>nivartanas</s> (a unit of land), or half that, or a house and the like,

children.text: apyāḍhāvāpamātraṃ vā dattvorvvīṃ phalabhāk bhavet // Valc_2,15.37 //
children.translated_text: or even a mere ploughing-strip — by giving land, one becomes a recipient of its fruit. // <s>Valc</s> 2,15.37 //
He who gives to one learned in the <s>Vedas</s> land rich in sugarcane,

children.text: dadāti vedaviduṣe sa na bhūyobhijāyate // Valc_2,15.38 //
children.translated_text: barley, wheat, and rice — he is not born again. // <s>Valc</s> 2,15.38 //
Having given plough-tilled land with trees and rich in grain,
one is honored in heaven as long as the rays of the sun shine. // <s>Valc</s> 2,15.39 //
One should give to a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> endowed with virtues,
devoted to austerities, with senses conquered —
as long as the earth stands with the ocean as its boundary,
so long shall the fruit for him be infinite. // <s>Valc</s> 2,15.40 //
Just as seeds sprout when scattered upon the earth,
so do desires sprout, acquired through the gift of land. // <s>Valc</s> 2,15.41 //
Just as a drop of oil falling upon water immediately spreads,

children.text: evaṃ bhūmikṛtaṃ dānaṃ śasye śakṣye prarohati // Valc_2,15.42 //
children.translated_text: so does the gift of land multiply in the crops. // <s>Valc</s> 2,15.42 //
Givers of food are always happy; givers of cloth are handsome;

children.text: sa naraḥ sarvvado bhūpā yo dadāti vasundharām // Valc_2,15.43 //
children.translated_text: but, O kings, the man who gives land is a giver of everything. // <s>Valc</s> 2,15.43 //
Just as a cow that gives milk nourishes her calf,

children.text: evaṃ dattā mahīpālā bhūmirbharati bhūmidam // Valc_2,15.44 //
children.translated_text: so, O kings, the land that is given nourishes the giver of land. // <s>Valc</s> 2,15.44 //
<s>Āditya</s> (the Sun), <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Soma</s> (the Moon), <s>Hutāśana</s> (Fire),
and the blessed <s>Śūlapāṇi</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) — all applaud the giver of land. // <s>Valc</s> 2,15.45 //
The ancestors clap their hands and the grandfathers praise, saying:

children.text: bhūmidātā kule jātaḥ sa nastrātā bhaviṣyati // Valc_2,15.46 //
children.translated_text: "A giver of land has been born in our family — he will be our savior!" // <s>Valc</s> 2,15.46 //
Earth has been given by many kings, beginning with <s>Sagara</s>;

children.text: yasya yasya yadā bhūmistasya tasya tadā phalam // Valc_2,15.47 //
children.translated_text: whoever possesses the land at any time, to him belongs the fruit at that time. // <s>Valc</s> 2,15.47 //

children.text: bhūmiṃ yaḥ pratigṛhṇāti yaśca bhūmiṃ prayacchati /
children.translated_text: He who receives the land and he who gives the land —

children.text: ubhau tau puṇyakarmmāṇau niyatau svargagāmiṇau // Valc_2,15.48 //
children.translated_text: both are doers of meritorious deeds, and are certainly destined for heaven. // <s>Valc</s> 2,15.48 //

children.text: dadyādbhūmiṃ nibandhaṃ vā kṛtvā lekhyañca kārayet /
children.translated_text: A king should give land or a revenue-grant, and should have a document prepared,
for the knowledge of future good kings. // <s>Valc</s> 2,15.49 //
On cloth or on a copper plate, marked with his own seal,
the king should inscribe his lineage and himself. // <s>Valc</s> 2,15.50 //
A description of the extent of the gift, the demarcation of the donee's share, and the prohibition of its revocation —
he should have an edict prepared, endowed with his own signature and date, making it firm. // <s>Valc</s> 2,15.51 //
The gift of gold, the gift of cows, and the gift of land, O kings —
he who offers these is freed from all sins. // <s>Valc</s> 2,15.52 //
Gold is the first offspring of <s>Agni</s> (Fire);
the earth belongs to <s>Viṣṇu</s>; cows are the daughters of the Sun.
He who gives gold, cows, and land —
by him the three worlds have been given. // <s>Valc</s> 2,15.53 //

children.text: yastaṭākaṃ navaṃ kuryyāt purāṇaṃ vāpi khānayet /
children.translated_text: He who constructs a new tank, or digs and restores an old one —

children.text: sa sarvvaṃ kulamuddhṛtya svarge loke mahīyate // Valc_2,15.54 //
children.translated_text: he, having uplifted his entire family, is honored in the heavenly world. // <s>Valc</s> 2,15.54 //
Even one who has committed sinful deeds, if he gives food to one in need,

children.text: brāhmaṇāya viśeṣeṇa sa pāpena na lipyate // Valc_2,15.55 //
children.translated_text: especially to a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, is not tainted by that sin. // <s>Valc</s> 2,15.55 //
Having uplifted thrice-seven generations of his family, the giver of a maiden attains the world of <s>Brahmā</s>;
and he who causes a temple and an image to be made, he obtains everything. // <s>Valc</s> 2,15.56 //
He who gives female servants to the best of twice-born attains the world of the <s>Apsarases</s>;

children.text: tasya śiśnendriyaṃ bhūpā nāgnirdahati karhicit // Valc_2,15.57 //
children.translated_text: O kings, the fire never burns his genital organ. // <s>Valc</s> 2,15.57 //
<s>Siṃhagiri</s> said:
"Having given many well-adorned slave-girls — adorned with garments, ornaments, sandalwood, and flowers, beautiful in the loveliness of their youthful form, delightful to enjoy —

children.text: dāsīḥ pradāya bahuśo dvijasattamebhyaḥ śrīlādiśūranṛpatīramate 'psarobhiḥ // Valc_2,15.58 //
children.translated_text: to the best of twice-born, King <s>Śrī Lādiśūra</s> sports with the <s>Apsarases</s>." // <s>Valc</s> 2,15.58 //

children.text: iti vallālacarite vyāsapurāṇe dānamāhātmādikīrttanaṃ nāma pañcadaśo 'dhyāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fifteenth chapter, named 'The Description of the Glory of Gifts and Other Matters,' in the <s>Vallālacarita</s>, a <s>Vyāsapurāṇa</s>.
Now begins the sixteenth chapter.
<s>Vyāsa</s> said:
The preceptor, the father, the elder brother, and the king,
the maternal uncle, the father-in-law, the protector, the maternal grandfather, and the paternal grandfather — // <s>Valc</s> 2,16.1 //
a kinsman, an elder, and a paternal uncle — these are considered <s>gurus</s> (elders/preceptors) among men;
the mother, the maternal grandmother, the paternal and maternal aunts and the like, // <s>Valc</s> 2,16.2 //

children.text: śvaśrūḥ pitāmahī jyeṣṭhā dhātrī ca guravaḥ striyaḥ /
children.translated_text: the mother-in-law, the paternal grandmother, the elder sister, and the wet-nurse — these are the female <s>gurus</s>.
Thus has been stated this class of <s>gurus</s>, from the mother's and father's side, O kings;
compliance with these, by mind, speech, and bodily action, // <s>Valc</s> 2,16.3 //
Seeing the <s>guru</s> (teacher), one should rise and salute him with joined palms;
one should not sit together with them, nor argue for one's own sake. // Valc_2,16.4 //
Even for the sake of one's life, one should never speak out of hatred against <s>gurus</s>;
even if distinguished by other virtues, one who hates his <s>guru</s> falls down. // Valc_2,16.5 //
Among all <s>gurus</s>, five are to be worshipped with special effort;
of these, the first three are the best, and among them, the mother is the most venerable. // Valc_2,16.6 //

children.text: yo bhāvayati yā sūte yena vidyopadiśyate /
children.translated_text: He who nourishes, she who gives birth, he by whom knowledge is imparted,

children.text: jyeṣṭhabhrātā ca bharttā ca pañcaite guravaḥ smṛtāḥ // Valc_2,16.7 //
children.translated_text: the elder brother, and the husband — these five are remembered as <s>gurus</s>. // Valc_2,16.7 //
these five are especially to be worshipped by one who desires prosperity.

children.text: nāsti pitṛsamo devo nāsti mātṛsamo guruḥ // Valc_2,16.8 //
children.translated_text: There is no deity equal to the father; there is no <s>guru</s> equal to the mother. // Valc_2,16.8 //
With all effort on one's own part, or even by the sacrifice of one's life,

children.text: tayornityaṃ priyaṃ kuryyāt karmmaṇā manasā girā /
children.translated_text: One should always do what is pleasing to those two, by deed, mind, and speech;
without their permission, one should not resort to any other <s>dharma</s>. // Valc_2,16.9 //
The <s>guru</s> is the fire for the twice-born; a Brahmin is the <s>guru</s> of all <s>varṇas</s>;

children.text: patireko guruḥ strīṇāṃ sarvvatrābhyāgato guruḥ // Valc_2,16.10 //
children.translated_text: the husband alone is the <s>guru</s> of women; a guest is the <s>guru</s> everywhere. // Valc_2,16.10 //
The best of men who bows to a Brahmin with the thought that he is <s>Viṣṇu</s> —

children.text: āyuḥ putraśca kīrttiśca sampattistasya varddhate // Valc_2,16.11 //
children.translated_text: his life-span, sons, fame, and prosperity increase. // Valc_2,16.11 //

children.text: duḥśīlo 'pi dvijaḥ pūjyo na śūdro vijetendriyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Even a Brahmin of bad conduct is to be honored; not so a <s>Śūdra</s>, even if he has conquered his senses;

children.text: viprā hi kṣatriyātmāno nāvajñeyāḥ kadācana // Valc_2,16.12 //
children.translated_text: Brahmins, who are the very soul of <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, are never to be despised. // Valc_2,16.12 //
Mounted on the chariot of <s>Dharmaśāstra</s>, wielding the sword of the <s>Vedas</s>, Brahmins —
