children.text: krīḍārthamapi yadbrūyuḥ sa dharmmaḥ paramaḥ smṛtaḥ // Valc_2,16.13 //
children.translated_text: whatever they say, even in jest, is regarded as the supreme <s>dharma</s>. // Valc_2,16.13 //

children.text: iti vallālacarite vyāsapurāṇe guruvargakīrttanaṃ nāma ṣoḍaśo 'dhyāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus in the <s>Vallālacarita</s>, in the <s>Vyāsa Purāṇa</s>, the sixteenth chapter called 'The Glorification of the Class of <s>Gurus</s>.'
Now, the seventeenth chapter.
<s>Vyāsa</s> said:
<s>Mānavya</s>, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, <s>Kāṅkāyana</s>, <s>Rahūgaṇa</s>,
<s>Bharadvāja</s>, <s>Gautama</s>, and <s>Kalviṣa</s> and <s>Sukālina</s>, // Valc_2,17.1 //
<s>Ārṣṭiṣeṇa</s>, <s>Agniveśa</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Cyavana</s>, and <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>,
<s>Viśvāmitra</s>, <s>Gālava</s>, <s>Candrātreya</s>, and <s>Kauśika</s>, // Valc_2,17.2 //
<s>Ghṛtakauśika</s>, <s>Maudgalya</s>, <s>Lābhāyana</s>, <s>Parāśara</s>,
<s>Saupāyana</s>, <s>Atrikuhala</s>, <s>Vāsuki</s>, and <s>Rohita</s>, // Valc_2,17.3 //
<s>Vārdhyaśva</s>, <s>Vaiyāghrapadya</s>, <s>Darbha</s>, <s>Śālāvata</s>, <s>Kapi</s>,
<s>Jamadagni</s>, <s>Kāñcana</s>, <s>Kātyāyana</s>, and <s>Vṛhaspati</s>, // Valc_2,17.4 //
<s>Viśuvṛddha</s>, <s>Sāṅkṛtya</s>, <s>Garga</s>, <s>Kauṇḍinya</s>, <s>Baṃpula</s>,
<s>Sāvarṇa</s>, <s>Āṅgirasa</s>, <s>Mauna</s>, <s>Kauśya</s>, <s>Yaugana</s>, and <s>Jaimini</s>, // Valc_2,17.5 //
<s>Śaktri</s>, <s>Kātyāyana</s>, <s>Vātsya</s>, <s>Logākṣi</s>, and <s>Śunaka</s>,

children.text: agastiḥ somarājaśca sandāno mādhavo bhṛguḥ // Valc_2,17.6 //
children.translated_text: <s>Agasti</s>, <s>Somarāja</s>, <s>Sandāna</s>, <s>Mādhava</s>, and <s>Bhṛgu</s>, // Valc_2,17.6 //
<s>Maitrāyaṇi</s>, <s>Śāṇḍilya</s>, <s>Upamanyu</s>, and <s>Dhanañjaya</s>,
<s>Madhukula</s>, <s>Hārita</s>, <s>Vidala</s>, and <s>Gobhila</s>, // Valc_2,17.7 //
<s>Kāskāyana</s>, <s>Yāska</s>, <s>Vārṣṇeya</s>, and <s>Brahmakṣatra</s>,
<s>Yuvanāśva</s>, <s>Vaiṇya</s>, <s>Jātūkarṇa</s>, and <s>Aghamarṣaṇa</s>, // Valc_2,17.8 //
<s>Ambarīṣa</s>, <s>Idhmavāha</s>, <s>Lauhitya</s>, <s>Indrakauśika</s>,

children.text: ajaśca nidhruvo rebha ṛṣayo gotrakārakāḥ // Valc_2,17.9 //
children.translated_text: <s>Aja</s>, <s>Nidhruva</s>, and <s>Rebha</s> — [these are] the sages who founded <s>gotras</s>. // Valc_2,17.9 //

children.text: iti vallālacarite vyāsapurāṇe gotrakīrttanaṃ nāma saptadaśo 'dhyāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus in the <s>Vallālacarita</s>, in the <s>Vyāsa Purāṇa</s>, the seventeenth chapter called 'The Glorification of <s>Gotras</s>.'
Now, the eighteenth chapter.
The royal sages said:
'Of the Brahmins, <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, <s>Vaiśyas</s>, and of those of the lowest birth —

children.text: bhedān brūhi mahāprājña śrotuṃ kautuhalaṃ param // Valc_2,18.1 //
children.translated_text: tell us the divisions, O greatly wise one; our curiosity to hear is supreme.' // Valc_2,18.1 //
<s>Vyāsa</s> said:
The <s>Sārasvatas</s>, <s>Kānyakubjas</s>, <s>Gauḍas</s>, <s>Maithilas</s>, and <s>Kotkalas</s> —

children.text: pañca gauḍā iti khyātā vindhyasyottaravāsinaḥ // Valc_2,18.2 //
children.translated_text: these five are known as <s>Gauḍas</s>, dwelling north of the <s>Vindhya</s>. // Valc_2,18.2 //
The <s>Karṇāṭas</s>, <s>Tailaṅgas</s>, <s>Gurjaras</s>, dwellers of the <s>Rāṣṭra</s>,
the <s>Andhras</s>, and the <s>Drāviḍas</s> — [these] five dwell south of the <s>Vindhya</s>. // Valc_2,18.3 //
The <s>Magas</s>, who are Brahmins, originally emerged from the solar orb,
blazing like the radiant sun, and descended to <s>Śākadvīpa</s>. // Valc_2,18.4 //
Thus the Brahmin classes.
The <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>, <s>Pauravas</s>, <s>Baudhas</s>, <s>Sahasrārjuna-Haihayas</s>,
<s>Candrātreyas</s>, <s>Kalacuris</s>, <s>Raṭṭas</s>, <s>Yādavas</s>, and <s>Tomaras</s>, // Valc_2,18.5 //

children.text: kauśikāḥ kaukurāḥ kuśyā ete saumyāḥ prakīrttitāḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Kauśikas</s>, <s>Kaukuras</s>, and <s>Kuśyas</s> — these are declared as [descended from] the Moon (<s>Saumyas</s>);
the <s>Aikṣvākus</s>, <s>Nikumbhas</s>, <s>Mauryas</s>, and <s>Sāgaras</s>, // Valc_2,18.6 //
and the <s>Kacchapa-ghātas</s>, <s>Rāghavas</s>, and <s>Gobhilas</s>,

children.text: tathā gāhaḍavālāśca ete saurāḥ prakīrttitāḥ // Valc_2,18.7 //
children.translated_text: and the <s>Gāhaḍavālas</s> — these are declared as [descended from] the Sun (<s>Sauras</s>). // Valc_2,18.7 //
The <s>Cāhamānas</s> (Chauhans), <s>Mallas</s>, <s>Chindas</s>, and <s>Āpotkaṭas</s>,
the <s>Caulukyas</s> (Solankis), <s>Silāras</s>, and <s>Hūṇas</s> — born from the arm of <s>Brahmā</s>. // Valc_2,18.8 //
Born from the fire-pit, the <s>Paramāras</s> of great strength,

children.text: śālukikāḥ sendrakāśca kādraveyā iti smṛtāḥ // Valc_2,18.9 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Śālukikas</s>, <s>Sendrakas</s>, and the <s>Kādraveyas</s> — these are remembered. // Valc_2,18.9 //
From the reed (<s>Veṇa</s>) was born <s>Vaiṇya Pṛthu</s>; from him arose the <s>Pṛthvīhāras</s>;

children.text: vainateyāstu tārkṣyā vai pālāstu kṣatriyādhamāḥ // Valc_2,18.10 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Vainateyas</s> are indeed <s>Tārkṣyas</s>; the <s>Pālas</s> are the lowest of <s>Kṣatriyas</s>. // Valc_2,18.10 //
Thus the <s>Kṣatriya</s> classes.
The <s>Upakeśas</s>, <s>Prākvāṭas</s>, <s>Rohitas</s>, and <s>Mahotsavas</s>,
those of <s>Māhiṣmatī</s>, of <s>Vaiśālī</s>, of <s>Kauśāmbī</s>, and the <s>Śrāvakas</s>, // Valc_2,18.11 //
the <s>Āyodhyikas</s>, and the merchants, and the <s>Gurjaras</s> — renowned on earth,
and the <s>Ujānikas</s>, and the wealthy, and the <s>Suvarṇas</s>, the lowest among merchants. // Valc_2,18.12 //
The <s>Jejātutīya</s> merchants, sprung from the rays of the moon. // Valc_2,18.13 //
Thus the <s>Vaiśya</s> classes.
Thus in the <s>Vallālacarita</s>, in the <s>Vyāsa Purāṇa</s>, the eighteenth chapter called 'The Glorification of the Three <s>Varṇa</s> Classes.'
Now, the nineteenth chapter.
<s>Vyāsa</s> said:
A <s>Śūdra</s> is of two kinds: a good <s>Śūdra</s> and a [mere] <s>Śūdra</s>;

children.text: ādyo vipraviśoḥ śūdryāṃ dvitīyaḥ pādajaḥ smṛtaḥ // Valc_2,19.1 //
children.translated_text: the first is born from a <s>Śūdra</s> woman by a Brahmin or <s>Vaiśya</s>; the second is said to be born from the feet [of Brahmā]. // Valc_2,19.1 //
From a Brahmin with a <s>Kṣatriya</s> woman is born one called <s>Maula</s>;
from a Brahmin with a <s>Vaiśya</s> woman, the son is known as <s>Ambaṣṭha</s>. // Valc_2,19.2 //

children.text: śūdrāyāṃ karaṇo vaiśyāt karaṇyāñca tataḥ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: from a <s>Vaiśya</s> with a <s>Śūdra</s> woman, a <s>Karaṇa</s> [is born]; and from a <s>Karaṇī</s> again,
stationed in the work of <s>Karaṇas</s>, therefore he is called a <s>Kāyastha</s> (scribe);
there are <s>Kāyasthas</s> born from the feet [of Brahmā], and also those born from <s>Ambaṣṭhas</s>;

children.text: ye tu kirātakāyasthā te sarvve ninditāḥ smṛtā // Valc_2,19.3 //
children.translated_text: but those who are <s>Kirāta-Kāyasthas</s> — they are all considered despised. // Valc_2,19.3 //
From an <s>Ambaṣṭha</s> with a <s>Vaiśya</s> woman is born one called <s>Vaidya</s> (physician);
The <s>Nigama</s> (townsman) and the <s>Gandhika</s> (perfumer), both sprung from the <s>Vaiśya</s> lineage,
gradually attained the status of <s>Śūdras</s> due to the lapse of [prescribed] rituals. // Valc_2,19.4 //
Gem-workers, goldsmiths, silver-workers and scribes,
coppersmiths, ironsmiths, conch-workers, and string-makers, // Valc_2,19.5 //
rice-dealers and vegetable-sellers are declared as good <s>Śūdras</s>;
from a <s>Vaiśya</s> [are born] a <s>Rāmaka</s> and a <s>Vaideha</s>, sons by Brahmin and <s>Kṣatriya</s> women [respectively]. // Valc_2,19.6 //
From a <s>Rāmaka</s> with a <s>Kṣatriya</s> woman is born one called <s>Ugra</s>;
from a Brahmin with an <s>Ugra</s> woman is born one called <s>Āvṛta</s>. // Valc_2,19.7 //
An <s>Ābhīra</s> is a <s>Śūdra</s> [born] from a <s>Śūdra</s> woman by an outcast <s>Kṣatriya</s> or <s>Vaiśya</s>;
from a <s>Vaiśya</s> with a <s>Vaideha</s> woman is born a <s>Kāṃsakāra</s> (bell-metal worker). // Valc_2,19.8 //
From a <s>Vaiśya</s> with an <s>Ambaṣṭha</s> woman, the sons are <s>Gopa</s> and <s>Gopālaka</s> (cowherds);
from a <s>Rāmaka</s> with a <s>Vaideha</s> woman is born a <s>Leṣakāra</s>. // Valc_2,19.9 //

children.text: vaiśyāyāṃ jāyate śūdrāt tailakāra iti smṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: From a <s>Śūdra</s> with a <s>Vaiśya</s> woman is born one known as <s>Tailakāra</s> (oil-presser);

children.text: ambaṣṭhāyāṃ svarṇakārāt śauciko nāma jāyate // Valc_2,19.10 //
children.translated_text: from a goldsmith with an <s>Ambaṣṭha</s> woman is born one called <s>Śaucika</s> (tailor). // Valc_2,19.10 //
From a <s>Vaiśya</s> with a <s>Kuvinda</s> (weaver) woman is born one called <s>Kṛṣika</s> (farmer);
from a <s>Kṛṣika</s> with a <s>Gopa</s> (cowherd) woman, a <s>Tāmbolī</s> (betel-seller) is born — so we have heard. // Valc_2,19.11 //
From a merchant with a <s>Śūdra</s> woman is born one called <s>Kanduka</s>;
from a <s>Kanduka</s> with a Brahmin woman, a <s>Kalupāla</s> was born. // Valc_2,19.12 //
From a <s>Śūdra</s> [are born] <s>Āyogava</s>, <s>Vaiṇa</s>, and <s>Caṇḍāla</s> — the lowest of men —
born from <s>Vaiśya</s>, <s>Kṣatriya</s>, and Brahmin women; these are <s>varṇasaṅkaras</s> (mixed castes). // Valc_2,19.13 //
Sometimes due to the greatness of the seed, sometimes due to the greatness of the field (womb),
lowness and superiority arise; the best is [determined] by both field and seed. // Valc_2,19.14 //

]
[[verse number jumps from "14" to "16"]]
Sometimes, in the case of <s>anuloma</s> (marriage with the natural order), the caste is regarded as equal to the mother's;
by action, superiority and inferiority [are determined], and by time also, through qualities. // Valc_2,19.16 //
One born from an <s>Ānārya</s> (non-noble) woman by an <s>Ārya</s> (noble) man becomes an <s>Ārya</s> through qualities;
one born from an <s>Ārya</s> woman by an <s>Anārya</s> man is definitely an <s>Anārya</s>. // Valc_2,19.17 //
From a <s>Kṛṣika</s> with an <s>Ambaṣṭha</s> woman were born the <s>Kuṭumbins</s> (householders);
from a <s>Kuṭumbin</s> with a <s>Gopālī</s> (cowherd woman), a <s>Kumbhakāra</s> (potter) was born. // Valc_2,19.18 //
From an ironsmith with a <s>Karaṇī</s> woman is born one called <s>Vardhaki</s> (carpenter);
from a <s>Vardhaki</s> with a coppersmith woman is born one called <s>Vāraki</s>. // Valc_2,19.19 //
By a potter with a <s>Śūdra</s> woman was begotten a <s>Palagaṇḍaka</s>;
from a <s>Śūdra</s> with a potter woman, a <s>Mālākāra</s> (garland-maker) is born. // Valc_2,19.20 //
From daughters bought with a price, slave castes are born;
from a Brahmin with a <s>Śūdra</s> woman, one called <s>Nāpita</s> (barber) is born. // Valc_2,19.21 //
There were also born in the fields of the slain ones among the mouth-born (Brahmins),
by <s>Śūdras</s>, <s>Vaiśyas</s>, and <s>Kṣatriyas</s> — <s>Caṇḍālas</s>, <s>Kirātas</s>, and <s>Abhara</s> castes. // Valc_2,19.22 //
From a <s>Kirāta</s> man with an ironsmith woman, a <s>Karmāra</s> (arms-dealer) who sells weapons [is born];
from a weaver with a copper-beating woman, a <s>Paṭṭakāra</s> (silk-weaver) is born. // Valc_2,19.23 //
A <s>Vaiśya</s> woman with a <s>Śūdra</s> begot an <s>Āyogava</s> son;
from a <s>Kalupāla</s> with a <s>Kuvinda</s> (weaver) woman, a <s>Śauṇḍika</s> (distiller) is born. // Valc_2,19.24 //
A <s>Raṅgājīva</s> (dyer) is the son born of a <s>Śauṇḍikī</s> (distiller woman) by a <s>Vardhaki</s> (carpenter);
from the mixing of mixed castes, and from that further mixing again and again, // Valc_2,19.25 //

children.text: jātyānantyantu saṃprāptaṃ sarvvaṃ vaktuṃ na śakyate /
children.translated_text: the infinity of castes has been reached — it is not possible to enumerate all of them.

children.text: pauṇḍrāḥ suhmāśca palhāśca pulindāśca kinārayaḥ // Valc_2,19.26 //
children.translated_text: The <s>Pauṇḍras</s>, <s>Suhmas</s>, <s>Palhāśas</s>, <s>Pulindas</s>, and <s>Kināras</s>, // Valc_2,19.26 //
the <s>Kolas</s>, <s>Bhūṣāras</s>, <s>Varaṭas</s>, <s>Turkas</s>, <s>Śavaras</s>, and <s>Śakas</s>,

children.text: pāradā daradā vyādhā niṣādāḥ pukkaśā amī // Valc_2,19.27 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Pāradas</s>, <s>Daradas</s>, <s>Vyādhas</s> (hunters), <s>Niṣādas</s>, and <s>Pukkaśas</s> — these // Valc_2,19.27 //
of <s>Mleccha</s> speech or of <s>Ārya</s> speech — are remembered as the sixteen <s>Dasyus</s> (outcasts). // Valc_2,19.28 //
The washerman, the leather-worker, the actor, the <s>Varuḍa</s>,
the fisherman (<s>Kaivarta</s>), the <s>Meda</s>, and the <s>Bhilla</s> — these seven are considered <s>Antyajas</s> (lowest born). // Valc_2,19.29 //

children.text: antyajānāṃ gṛhe toyaṃ bhāṇḍe paryyuṣitantu yat /
children.translated_text: Water in the house of <s>Antyajas</s>, that which has been left standing in a vessel —

children.text: prāyaścittaṃ yadā pītaṃ tadaiva hi samācaret // Valc_2,19.30 //
children.translated_text: when it is drunk, expiation (<s>prāyaścitta</s>) should be performed immediately. // Valc_2,19.30 //
Thus in the <s>Vallālacarita</s>, the nineteenth chapter called 'The Account of the <s>Śūdra</s> Classes.'
Now, the twentieth chapter.
<s>Vyāsa</s> said:
Hereafter, the <s>Rudragītā</s> is recounted, O lords of men;

children.text: śṛṇatāvahitā bhūtvā imāṃ gītāṃ sanātanīm // Valc_2,20.1 //
children.translated_text: listen attentively to this eternal song. // Valc_2,20.1 //

children.text: namaste manyave rudra utota iṣave namaḥ /
children.translated_text: Salutation to your wrath, O <s>Rudra</s>; and salutation to your arrow;

children.text: namāmi tava vāhubhyāṃ giriśanta girīśvara // Valc_2,20.2 //
children.translated_text: I bow to your arms, O dweller on the mountain, O lord of mountains. // Valc_2,20.2 //
O <s>Rudra</s>, with your auspicious, non-harmful, <s>Śivā</s> form, though of terrible appearance,

children.text: tanvāno 'bhi cākaśīhi sukhaṃ śantamayā śiva // Valc_2,20.3 //
children.translated_text: manifesting, shine upon [us]; may there be happiness, peace — O <s>Śiva</s>, by your grace. // Valc_2,20.3 //
The arrow that you hold in your hand, O mountain-dweller, which you bear —

children.text: tāṃ giritra kuru śivāṃ mā hiṃsīḥ puruṣaṃ jagat // Valc_2,20.4 //
children.translated_text: make it auspicious, O protector of the mountain; do not harm man or the world. // Valc_2,20.4 //
With auspicious speech we address you clearly, O lord of the mountain, O master,

children.text: yathā yakṣmaṃ sumanaso jagatsarvvamidaṃ bhavet // Valc_2,20.5 //
children.translated_text: so that all beings may be well-disposed, [free from] disease, and this whole world may be [at peace]. // Valc_2,20.5 //
He who spoke and speaks first, the foremost divine physician —

children.text: ahīṃśca jambhayan sarvvān yātudhānīḥ parāsuva // Valc_2,20.6 //
children.translated_text: crushing all serpents, drive away all the <s>Yātudhānīs</s> (sorceresses). // Valc_2,20.6 //

children.text: asau yastāmra āditya uta vabhrūḥ sumaṅgalaḥ /
children.translated_text: That copper-hued <s>Āditya</s> (sun), and also the tawny one, most auspicious —

children.text: ye cainaṃ rudrā abhito dikṣveṣāṃ heḍaīmahe // Valc_2,20.7 //
children.translated_text: and those <s>Rudras</s> who are around him in all directions — we appease their anger. // Valc_2,20.7 //
He who descends — the blue-throated one, the crimson one —

children.text: gopāḥstriyo 'pyadṛśran yaṃ sa dṛṣṭomṛḍayāti naḥ // Valc_2,20.8 //
children.translated_text: Whom even the cowherds' wives have seen — may he who has been seen grant us happiness! // Valc 2,20.8 //
Salutation to the blue-throated one, the thousand-eyed one, the bountiful one!

children.text: santyatho ye 'sya satvā nastebhyo 'hamakaraṃ namaḥ // Valc_2,20.9 //
children.translated_text: And those who are his attendant beings — to them I have made obeisance. // Valc 2,20.9 //
Of your bow, O lord of <s>Umā</s> (<s>Umādhava</s>), release the string from both [ends];

children.text: yāśca te hasta iṣavo bhagavan tāḥ parā vapa /
children.translated_text: And those arrows in your hand, O lord — scatter them far away;
The divine bow of the matted-haired one — may it be free from arrows, arrow-less;
And may his arrows be rendered harmless, and his quiver be at peace. // Valc 2,20.10 //

children.text: yā mīḍhuṣṭama te hetirhaste pravidyate dhanuḥ /
children.translated_text: O most bountiful one, whatever weapon is in your hand, whatever bow is displayed —

children.text: ayakṣan yā tathāsmān tvaṃ viśvataḥ paripālaya // Valc_2,20.11 //
children.translated_text: With that, which is non-destructive, protect us on all sides! // Valc 2,20.11 //

children.text: asmān te dhanvano hetiḥ parivṛṇaktu viśvataḥ /
children.translated_text: May the weapon of your bow encompass us on all sides;

children.text: atho yaśceṣudhī rudra asmadāre nidhehi tam // Valc_2,20.12 //
children.translated_text: And that quiver of yours, O <s>Rudra</s>, place it far away from us. // Valc 2,20.12 //
Having unstrung the bow and having scattered the arrow-tips,

children.text: śateṣudhe sahasrākṣa śivo naḥ sumanā bhava // Valc_2,20.13 //
children.translated_text: O thousand-eyed one, possessor of a hundred quivers — be auspicious to us, be well-disposed! // Valc 2,20.13 //
Salutation to your weapon, to the bold one, to the one whose bow is unstrung;

children.text: ubhābhyāmuta vāhubhyāṃ namaste 'stu ca dhanvane // Valc_2,20.14 //
children.translated_text: And salutation to both your arms, and salutation to your bow! // Valc 2,20.14 //

children.text: mā no mahānta muta mā no arbhakam
children.translated_text: Slay not our great ones, nor our small ones,
Nor the growing one, nor the one already grown;
Slay not our father, nor our mother,

children.text: mā naḥ priyāstanvo rudra rīriṣaḥ // Valc_2,20.15 //
children.translated_text: And do not harm our dear bodies, O <s>Rudra</s>! // Valc 2,20.15 //

children.text: mānastoke ca tanaye gavāśveṣu ca rīriṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: Harm not our offspring or descendants, our cattle or horses;

children.text: āyūṃṣi bhāmino vīrān māvadhīstvāṃ havāmahe // Valc_2,20.16 //
children.translated_text: Slay not our heroes, O wrathful one — we invoke you with oblations! // Valc 2,20.16 //
To the commander of armies, to the lord of the quarters, salutation! To the one with a golden chariot!
To the trees with green tresses, to the lord of cattle — salutation! // Valc 2,20.17 //
To the clanking one, to the resplendent one, to the lord of pathways — salutation!
To the charioteer, to the green-haired one, to the lord of the well-nourished — salutation! // Valc 2,20.18 //
To the tawny one — salutation! To the hunter, to the lord of food — salutation!

children.text: bhavasya hetyai jagatām pataye ca namo namaḥ // Valc_2,20.19 //
children.translated_text: To the weapon of <s>Bhava</s>, to the lord of all beings — obeisance again and again! // Valc 2,20.19 //
To <s>Rudra</s>, to the one who strings his bow, to the lord of fields — salutation!
Salutation to the slayer, to the charioteer, to the lord of forests — salutation! // Valc 2,20.20 //
To the red one, to the chief architect, to the lord of trees — salutation!
Salutation to the one who supports, to the one who gives service! // Valc 2,20.21 //
To the counselor, to the trader, to the lord of thickets — salutation!
To the one who makes a loud noise, to the one who cries aloud, to the lord of foot-soldiers — salutation! // Valc 2,20.22 //
To the one who runs, to the one who pervades all, to the lord of beings — salutation!

children.text: namo 'stu sahamānāya namo nivyādhine namaḥ // Valc_2,20.23 //
children.translated_text: Salutation to the overpowerer, salutation to the piercer — salutation! // Valc 2,20.23 //
To the lord of the piercing ones, to the one prominent, to the one bearing a quiver,
To the creeper, salutation to you — to the lord of thieves, salutation! // Valc 2,20.24 //
Salutation to the lord of the forests! Salutation to the attendant!
To the lord of stealthy ones, to you — to the deceiver and the great deceiver! // Valc 2,20.25 //
I bow to the one bearing a quiver; salutation to you, the one with arrows;

children.text: taskarāṇānte pataye namāmi ca punaḥ punaḥ // Valc_2,20.26 //
children.translated_text: To the lord of robbers, I offer obeisance again and again. // Valc 2,20.26 //
To those bearing daggers, to those wishing to slay, to the lord of plunderers — salutation!

children.text: asimadbhyo vikṛntānām pataye te namonamaḥ // Valc_2,20.27 //
children.translated_text: To those bearing swords, to the lord of those who cut apart — obeisance again and again! // Valc 2,20.27 //
To the night-wandering <s>Rudras</s>, to the running ones — obeisance again and again!
To the turbaned one, to the lord of cultivators — obeisance again and again! // Valc 2,20.28 //
To those bearing bows, to those with arrows — salutation! To you who roam the mountains!
To those who stretch [the bow], and to those who take aim — obeisance again and again! // Valc 2,20.29 //
To those drawing [the bowstring] — salutation! To those hurling — to those releasing — obeisance again and again!
To those who pierce, and to those who sleep, and to those who are awake — obeisance again and again! // Valc 2,20.30 //
To those lying down, to those seated, to those standing — obeisance again and again to you!

children.text: namaḥ sabhāpatibhyo vaḥ sabhābhyaśca namonamaḥ // Valc_2,20.31 //
children.translated_text: Salutation to the lords of assemblies among you, and to the assemblies — obeisance again and again! // Valc 2,20.31 //
To the horses, to the lords of horses, and to the piercing ones — obeisance again and again!
To the piercers — salutation! To the fierce hosts — obeisance again and again! // Valc 2,20.32 //
To the crushing hosts, and to the bands, and to the companies — obeisance again and again!
Salutation to <s>Gaṇapati</s>, and to the lords of companies — obeisance again and again! // Valc 2,20.33 //
To the lords of the wise, to the wise ones, to the deformed ones — obeisance again and again!
To the all-formed ones — salutation! To the armies — obeisance again and again! // Valc 2,20.34 //
To the army-leaders, to the charioteers among you, to the chariot-less — obeisance again and again!
To the charioteers, to the gatherers, and to the great ones — obeisance again and again! // Valc 2,20.35 //
To the children, to the carpenters, to the chariot-makers — obeisance again and again!
To the smiths, to the potters, to the <s>Niṣāda</s> (tribal) hunters — obeisance again and again! // Valc 2,20.36 //
To the trap-setters, to the dog-keepers, and to you the huntsmen — salutation!

children.text: śvabhyaśca śvapatibhyaśca rudrāya ca bhavāya ca // Valc_2,20.37 //
children.translated_text: To the dogs, and to the lords of dogs, and to <s>Rudra</s>, and to <s>Bhava</s>! // Valc 2,20.37 //
To the blue-throated one, to the all-pervading one, to the lord of cattle — salutation!
Salutation to you, O dark-throated one! Salutation to you, O matted-haired one! // Valc 2,20.38 //
To the thousand-eyed one, to the one with disheveled hair, to the one with a hundred bows;

children.text: giriśāya namastubhyaṃ śipiviṣṭāya te namaḥ // Valc_2,20.39 //
children.translated_text: To <s>Giriśa</s> (mountain-dweller) — salutation to you! To <s>Śipiviṣṭa</s> (the pervading one) — salutation! // Valc 2,20.39 //
To the most bountiful one, the arrow-bearer, to the short one and the dwarf one,

children.text: vṛhate ca varṣīyase vṛddhāya savṛdhe namaḥ // Valc_2,20.40 //
children.translated_text: To the great one and the greater, to the old one and the one who grants growth — salutation! // Valc 2,20.40 //
Salutation to the first one, to the foremost! To the swift one and to the agile one,

children.text: namaḥ śīghrāya śībhyāya ūrmmāyāvasvanāya ca // Valc_2,20.41 //
children.translated_text: Salutation to the rapid one, to the quick one! To the surging one and the resounding one! // Valc 2,20.41 //
To the one of the rivers — salutation to you! To the one of the islands — obeisance again and again!

children.text: jyeṣṭhāya ca kaniṣṭhāya pūrvvajāya namonamaḥ // Valc_2,20.42 //
children.translated_text: To the eldest and to the youngest, to the first-born — obeisance again and again! // Valc 2,20.42 //
To the middling one, to the bold one, to the one of the depths, to the later-born;

children.text: jaghanyāya ca somyāya pratisaryyāya te namaḥ // Valc_2,20.47 //
children.translated_text: To the hindmost, to the gentle one, to the one who moves against [the current] — salutation to you! // Valc 2,20.47 //

children.text: namo yāmyāya kṣemyāya ślokyāya ca namonamaḥ /
children.translated_text: Salutation to the one of the south, to the one of safety, to the one worthy of praise — obeisance again and again!

children.text: urvaryyāyāvasānyāya khalyāya ca namastu te // Valc_2,20.44 //
children.translated_text: To the one of fertile fields, to the one at the boundary, to the one of the threshing floor — salutation to you! // Valc 2,20.44 //

children.text: namo vandyāya kakṣyāya śravāya ca namonamaḥ /
children.translated_text: Salutation to the one worthy of veneration, to the one in the thicket, to the one who hears — obeisance again and again!

children.text: pratiśravāya ca namaḥ āśuṣeṇāya te namaḥ // Valc_2,20.45 //
children.translated_text: Salutation to the echo! To the one with a swift army — salutation to you! // Valc 2,20.45 //
Salutation to the one with a swift chariot! To the hero, to the one who pierces;

children.text: vilmine ca kavacine varmmiṇe ca varūthine // Valc_2,20.46 //
children.translated_text: To the one wearing a helmet, to the one wearing armor, to the one clad in a coat of mail, to the one with a shield! // Valc 2,20.46 //
To the famous one, to the one with a famous army, to the drummer — obeisance again and again!

children.text: ahanyāya dhṛṣṇave ca pramṛṣāya namonamaḥ // Valc_2,20.47 //
children.translated_text: To the one who strikes, to the bold one, to the one who destroys — obeisance again and again! // Valc 2,20.47 //
To the one with sharp arrows, to the one bearing weapons, to the one with good weapons, to the one with a good bow;

children.text: namaḥ satyāya pathyāya kāṭyāya ca namonamaḥ // Valc_2,20.48 //
children.translated_text: Salutation to the one on the path of truth, to the one on the right path, to the one of the thorny places — obeisance again and again! // Valc 2,20.48 //

children.text: nīpyāya ca namastubhyaṃ kulyāya ca namonamaḥ /
children.translated_text: To the one in the low-lying water — salutation to you! To the one by the streams — obeisance again and again!
To the one of the lakes, to the one of the rivers, to the one of the ponds — obeisance again and again! // Valc 2,20.49 //

children.text: avaṭyāya ca kupyāya vīghrāya ca namonamaḥ /
children.translated_text: To the one in the pit, to the one in the well, to the one in the fast-flowing [water] — obeisance again and again!

children.text: ātapyāya ca medhyāya vidyutyāya namonamaḥ // Valc_2,20.50 //
children.translated_text: To the one in the heat, to the one in the rain, to the one in the lightning — obeisance again and again! // Valc 2,20.50 //

children.text: avarṣyāya ca varṣāya vātyāya ca namonamaḥ /
children.translated_text: To the one in the drought, to the one in the rains, to the one in the storm — obeisance again and again!

children.text: namo brātyāya reṣmāya vāstavyāya namonamaḥ // Valc_2,20.51 //
children.translated_text: Salutation to the outcast, to the one in calamity, to the one who dwells in houses — obeisance again and again! // Valc 2,20.51 //

children.text: vāstupāya ca somāya rudrāya ca namonamaḥ /
children.translated_text: To the protector of dwellings, to <s>Soma</s>, to <s>Rudra</s> — obeisance again and again!

children.text: aruṇāya ca tāmrāya śaṅgave ca namonamaḥ // Valc_2,20.52 //
children.translated_text: To the reddish one, to the copper-colored one, to <s>Śaṅga</s> — obeisance again and again! // Valc 2,20.52 //
Salutation to the fierce one, to the terrible one, to the slayer from near — salutation to you!

children.text: dūrevadhāya hantre ca namo hanīyase namaḥ // Valc_2,20.53 //
children.translated_text: To the slayer from afar, to the destroyer — salutation! To the most destructive one — salutation! // Valc 2,20.53 //
To the one who is the source of existence, to <s>Śaṅkara</s> (the beneficent one), to the one who grants bliss — salutation to you!

children.text: mayaskarāya ca śivatarāya ca śivāya ca // Valc_2,20.54 //
children.translated_text: To the bliss-maker, to the most auspicious one, and to <s>Śiva</s>! // Valc 2,20.54 //

children.text: avāryyāya ca pāryyāya namaḥ prataraṇāya ca /
children.translated_text: To the irresistible one, to the one who leads beyond, salutation! To the one who carries across,

children.text: uttaraṇāya tīryyāya kubjāya ca namonamaḥ // Valc_2,20.55 //
children.translated_text: To the one who leads over, to the one who crosses, to the hunchbacked one — obeisance again and again! // Valc 2,20.55 //
Salutation to the one of the grain, to the one of the foam, to the one of the sand — obeisance again and again!
To the one of the streams, to the one of the rocks, to the one of the dwelling — obeisance again and again! // Valc 2,20.56 //
To the one of the wasteland, to the one of the paths — salutation to you, O son of <s>Pulastya</s>!

children.text: namo vrajyāya goṣṭhāya talpāya ca namonamaḥ // Valc_2,20.57 //
children.translated_text: Salutation to the one of the pastures, to the one of the cowsheds, to the one of the couch — obeisance again and again! // Valc 2,20.57 //

children.text: gehyāya ca hṛdayyāya niveṣyāya ca te namaḥ /
children.translated_text: To the one of the house, to the one dear to the heart, to the one of the settlement — salutation to you!
To the one dwelling in caves, to the one in dry places, to the one in green lands — obeisance again and again! // Valc 2,20.58 //

children.text: pāṃsavyāya rajasyāya lopyāya ca namo 'stu te /
children.translated_text: To the one of the dust, to the one of the mist, to the one of the ploughed land — salutation to you!

children.text: ulapyāya ca ūrvvāya sarvvāya ca namonamaḥ // Valc_2,20.59 //
children.translated_text: To the one of the meadow, to the one of the plain, to the all-pervading one — obeisance again and again! // Valc 2,20.59 //
To the one who makes leaves fall, to the one of the leaves — salutation! To the one who strikes — salutation!

children.text: nama udguramāṇāya namaḥ ākhidate namaḥ // Valc_2,20.60 //
children.translated_text: Salutation to the one who rises up! Salutation to the one who digs! // Valc 2,20.60 //
To the arrow-makers, to the bow-makers — salutation! To the one who burrows — salutation!
To the <s>Kirikā</s>-beings, to the hearts of the gods — obeisance again and again! // Valc 2,20.61 //
To those who search, to those who scatter — obeisance again and again!

children.text: ānirhatebhyo yuṣmabhyaṃ namāmi ca punaḥ punaḥ // Valc_2,20.62 //
children.translated_text: To those who strike — to you I bow again and again! // Valc 2,20.62 //
O lord of food, O <s>Drāpi</s>! O impoverished one! O blue-and-red one!

children.text: prajānāṃ naḥ paśūnāñca mābhermārok kathañcana // Valc_2,20.63 //
children.translated_text: Of our people and our cattle — do not frighten them, do not harm them in any way! // Valc 2,20.63 //
These our praises we offer to <s>Rudra</s>, for [his] strength;

children.text: grāme viśve yathā śaṃsvādvipade ca catuṣpade // Valc_2,20.64 //
children.translated_text: So that in village and domain he may grant welfare to both the bipeds and quadrupeds! // Valc 2,20.64 //
That auspicious body of yours, O <s>Rudra</s>, which is auspicious, the remedy of all the universe,

children.text: rudrasya bheṣajī rudra tayā no mṛḍ jīvase // Valc_2,20.65 //
children.translated_text: O <s>Rudra</s>, with that healing [form] of <s>Rudra</s>, grant us happiness for [our] living! // Valc 2,20.65 //

children.text: rudrasya hetiḥ parito vṛṇakta tveṣasya cāsmāsu na durmmatiśca /
children.translated_text: May the weapon of <s>Rudra</s> turn away from us on all sides, and also the fierce one's ill-will toward us;

children.text: sthirāṇi rudra avatāraya tvam tokāya pautrāya sukhaṃ yathā syāt // Valc_2,20.66 //
children.translated_text: O <s>Rudra</s>, loosen your firm [arrows] — may there be happiness for our children and grandchildren! // Valc 2,20.66 //

children.text: mīḍhuṣṭama śivatama śivo naḥ sumanā bhava /
children.translated_text: O most bountiful one, O most auspicious one, be gracious to us, be well-disposed!

children.text: nidhāya parame vṛkṣe āyudhaṃ tava śaṅkara // Valc_2,20.67 //
children.translated_text: Having placed your weapon upon the highest tree, O <s>Śaṅkara</s>! // Valc 2,20.67 //

children.text: kṛttiṃ vasāna āgaccha pinākaṃ dhārayan śivaḥ /
children.translated_text: Wearing a hide, come near; holding the <s>Pināka</s> (bow), O auspicious one!
Salutation to you, O lord, O scatterer, O crimson one! // Valc 2,20.68 //
Those weapons of yours that are a thousand — may they strike another than us!

children.text: yāstava hetayo vāhvoḥ sahasrāṇi sahasraśaḥ // Valc_2,20.69 //
children.translated_text: Those weapons of yours in both arms, thousands upon thousands — // Valc 2,20.69 //
Of those, O sovereign lord, turn their faces away [from us]!

children.text: asaṃkhyātāḥ sahasrāṇi ye rudrā adhi bhūtale // Valc_2,20.70 //
children.translated_text: Innumerable thousands of <s>Rudras</s> are upon the face of the earth — // Valc 2,20.70 //
At a distance of a thousand leagues, we unstring their bows.
Those <s>Bhava</s>-forms of his that exist in this great atmosphere and ocean — // Valc 2,20.71 //
At a distance of a thousand leagues, we unstring their bows.

children.text: nīlagrīvāḥ śvetakaṇṭhāḥ divaṃ rudrā upaśritāḥ // Valc_2,20.72 //
children.translated_text: The blue-throated, white-necked <s>Rudras</s> who have resorted to heaven — // Valc 2,20.72 //
At a distance of a thousand leagues, we unstring their bows.
The blue-throated, white-necked <s>Śarvas</s> (Rudras) below, who roam the earth —
At a distance of a thousand leagues, we unstring their bows. // Valc 2,20.73 //
Those who are tawny-green in the trees, blue-throated and crimson —
At a distance of a thousand leagues, we unstring their bows. // Valc 2,20.74 //
And those who are lords of beings, with loose hair, with matted hair —
At a distance of a thousand leagues, we unstring their bows. // Valc 2,20.75 //
Those who are protectors on the paths, life-fighters, and guardians against <s>Rākṣasas</s> —
At a distance of a thousand leagues, we unstring their bows. // Valc 2,20.76 //

children.text: ye ca caranti tīrthāni sṛkāhastā niṣaṅgiṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: And those who roam the sacred fords, with daggers in hand, bearing quivers —
At a distance of a thousand leagues, we unstring their bows. // Valc 2,20.77 //

children.text: ye cānneṣu vividhyanti pātreṣu pivato janān /
children.translated_text: And those who pierce people in their food and in their vessels while they drink —
At a distance of a thousand leagues, we unstring their bows. // Valc 2,20.78 //
So many and even more <s>Rudras</s> have taken their stations in all directions —
At a distance of a thousand leagues, we unstring their bows. // Valc 2,20.79 //

children.text: namo rudrebhyo duḥsthebhyo yeṣāṃ varṣantu sāyakāḥ /
children.translated_text: Salutation to the <s>Rudras</s> in distress, whose arrows rain down;

children.text: sarvadik vidikṣu ca teṣāṃ kurvve daśāṅgulīḥ // Valc_2,20.80 //
children.translated_text: In every direction and intermediate direction, to them I make the ten-fingered [gesture of obeisance]. // Valc 2,20.80 //

children.text: namo 'stu tebhyo no 'vantu tathāsmān mṛḍayantu te /
children.translated_text: Obeisance to them; may they protect us, and may they be gracious to us.

children.text: jambhe dadhmastameteṣāṃ yandviṣmo yaśca dveṣṭi naḥ // Valc_2,20.81 //
children.translated_text: We crush in the jaws those whom we hate and who hate us. // Valc_2,20.81 //
Obeisance to those <s>Rudras</s> who are in the atmosphere, whose arrows are the winds;

children.text: sarvvadikṣu vidikṣveva teṣāṃ kurvve daśāṅgulī // Valc_2,20.82 //
children.translated_text: in all directions and intermediate quarters, I make the <s>daśāṅgulī</s> (ten-finger salute) to them. // Valc_2,20.82 //

children.text: namastu tebhyo no 'vantu tathāsmān mṛḍayantu te /
children.translated_text: Obeisance to them; may they protect us, and may they be gracious to us.

children.text: jambhe dadhmastameteṣāṃ yaṃdviṣmo yaśca dveṣṭi naḥ // Valc_2,20.83 //
children.translated_text: We crush in the jaws those whom we hate and who hate us. // Valc_2,20.83 //

children.text: namo rudrebhyo ye pṛṣvyāṃ yeṣāmannantu sāyakāḥ /
children.translated_text: Obeisance to the <s>Rudras</s> who are on the earth, whose arrows are food;

children.text: sarvvadikṣu vidikṣeva teṣāṃ kurvve daśāṅgulī // Valc_2,20.84 //
children.translated_text: in all directions and intermediate quarters, I make the <s>daśāṅgulī</s> (ten-finger salute) to them. // Valc_2,20.84 //

children.text: namastu tebhyo no 'vantu tathāsmān mṛḍayantu te /
children.translated_text: Obeisance to them; may they protect us, and may they be gracious to us.

children.text: jambhedadhmastameteṣāṃ yaṃdviṣmo yaśca dveṣṭi naḥ // Valc_2,20.85 //
children.translated_text: We crush in the jaws those whom we hate and who hate us. // Valc_2,20.85 //

children.text: imāṃ gītāṃ naro raudrīṃ paṭhaṃścāpi śravan smaran /
children.translated_text: A man who recites, hears, or remembers this <s>Raudrī Gītā</s> (Hymn of <s>Rudra</s>)

children.text: prayāti rudrasālokyaṃ na cāsau jāyate punaḥ // Valc_2,20.86 //
children.translated_text: attains the world of <s>Rudra</s> and is not born again. // Valc_2,20.86 //
Thus ends the twentieth chapter, the <s>Rudragītopaniṣad</s>, in the <s>Vallālacarita</s>, a <s>Vyāsa Purāṇa</s>.
Chapter Twenty-One
<s>Siṃhagiri</s> said:
O lord of men, I have narrated to you, O <s>Vyāsa</s>, this <s>Purāṇa</s>,

children.text: rājarṣibhyo yathā prāha purā vyāso mahāmuniḥ // Valc_2,21.1 //
children.translated_text: just as the great sage <s>Vyāsa</s> formerly told it to the royal sages. // Valc_2,21.1 //

children.text: bhuṅkṣa bhogān yathākāmaṃ pitḥn devān ca tarpaya /
children.translated_text: Enjoy pleasures as you wish; satisfy the ancestors and the gods,
and always gratify the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, O lord of the people, with gifts of many kinds. // Valc_2,21.2 //
Perform the <s>piṇḍayajña</s> (ancestral offering sacrifice) together with your new queen,

children.text: śilādevyā mahīpāla tasyāṃ putro bhaviṣyati // Valc_2,21.3 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śilādevī</s>, O protector of the earth — a son will be born to her. // Valc_2,21.3 //
And the <s>tulāpuruṣadāna</s> (gift of one's weight in gold) at the sacrifice, O scorcher of foes —
perform it with discipline, having observed the <s>kṛcchra</s> (austerity), O lord of the earth. // Valc_2,21.4 //
May you fare well; I shall depart for the city of <s>Jagannātha</s>.
I shall return again whenever you remember me. // Valc_2,21.5 //
<s>Śaraṇadatta</s> said:
Having thus instructed the king, the sage <s>Siṃhagiri</s> then

children.text: jagāma tairvṛtaḥ śiṣye ryaiḥ sa rājan samāgataḥ // Valc_2,21.6 //
children.translated_text: departed, accompanied by those disciples with whom he had arrived, O king. // Valc_2,21.6 //

children.text: gate siṃhagirau rājā cintayan manasi kṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: When <s>Siṃhagiri</s> had gone, the king, reflecting for a moment in his mind,

children.text: piṇḍayajñe ca dāneṣu mano dadhre punaḥ punaḥ // Valc_2,21.7 //
children.translated_text: set his heart again and again upon the <s>piṇḍayajña</s> (ancestral sacrifice) and the gifts. // Valc_2,21.7 //

children.text: yajñādīnāṃ phalaṃ dhyāyan mantriṇā ca purodhasā /
children.translated_text: Contemplating the fruits of sacrifices and the like, the king
deliberated with his minister, his family priest, <s>Valadeva</s>, and the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>. // Valc_2,21.8 //

children.text: mantrayitvā tato rājā tadānīṃ brāhmaṇaiḥ saha /
children.translated_text: Having thus deliberated with the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, the king then
set about preparing the means to perform the sacrifice and the gifts. // Valc_2,21.9 //
The king thereupon commanded <s>Ādideva</s>, his trusted

children.text: mantriṇaṃ sadguṇairyuktaṃ karttavyāni ca sarvvaśaḥ // Valc_2,21.10 //
children.translated_text: minister endowed with good qualities, regarding all that was to be done. // Valc_2,21.10 //
The king said:
Let them bring, as prescribed by <s>Valadeva</s> and the other <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>,

children.text: sarvvadravyaṃ yathāyogaṃ yajñe caiva vihāpite // Valc_2,21.11 //
children.translated_text: all the materials as appropriate, when the sacrifice has been announced. // Valc_2,21.11 //
<s>Haradāsa</s>, <s>Viṣṇudāsa</s>, and <s>Durgāsiṃha</s> — quickly
let them arrange the supplies of food and other provisions by carts in proper order. // Valc_2,21.12 //
Let the sacrificial enclosure be prepared, adorned with banners and flags,
and let lodgings be built for the noble princes and kings. // Valc_2,21.13 //
A hundred cooks for the cooking and serving,
and let <s>vīṇā</s>-players play and singers sing, and let dancers and actors dance. // Valc_2,21.14 //
Let viewing galleries be prepared for all the women of the inner apartments,
and let the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>Kṣatriya</s>, <s>Vaiśya</s>, and virtuous <s>Śūdra</s> communities be invited. // Valc_2,21.15 //
Let shelters be prepared, well-stocked with food and provisions,
where <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> who are learned in the <s>Vedas</s> may dwell, honored. // Valc_2,21.16 //

children.text: āhūya lakṣmaṇaṃ rājā prāhedaṃ vacanaṃ tataḥ /
children.translated_text: The king then summoned <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> and spoke these words:

children.text: āmantrayasva yajñāya gatvā tvaṃ vikramaṃ puram // Valc_2,21.17 //
children.translated_text: Go to <s>Vikramapura</s> and invite them to the sacrifice — // Valc_2,21.17 //
<s>Śrī Sukhasena</s>, the paternal uncle, and prince <s>Dhruva</s> as well;

children.text: āgacchantu ca sarvvāṇi tayo rantaḥpurāṇi ca // Valc_2,21.18 //
children.translated_text: let them come with all their inner households. // Valc_2,21.18 //
<s>Śaraṇadatta</s> said:
Having gone to <s>Vikramapura</s>, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, the slayer of enemy heroes,
joyfully extended the invitation, bowing with joined palms. // Valc_2,21.19 //
<s>Dhruva</s> and <s>Sukhasena</s>, honored and joyfully invited,
set out for <s>Gauḍa</s> for the sacrifice, taking their inner households with them. // Valc_2,21.20 //
Hearing of the sacrifice of <s>Vallālasena</s>, Vedic <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>
went with delighted hearts — those knowers of sacrifice — to the sacrifice. // Valc_2,21.21 //
Uninvited and half-invited, <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> eager for wealth
arrived from all directions, in hundreds and thousands. // Valc_2,21.22 //
Feudatory kings also came, bearing tribute gifts,
with their retinues in various conveyances, to partake in the great festival. // Valc_2,21.23 //
The king's officers assigned lodgings to them —
numerous, handsome in appearance, and well-supplied with food and refreshments. // Valc_2,21.24 //

children.text: vallālaṃ te tato dṛṣṭvā tenātha pratipūjitāḥ /
children.translated_text: They then beheld <s>Vallāla</s>, and having been honored by him,
those provincial lords went to their assigned lodgings. // Valc_2,21.25 //
Having rested at leisure, the kings and princes and others

children.text: dadṛśuste prajānāthaṃ pāṇḍavaṃ taṃ sadogatam // Valc_2,21.26 //
children.translated_text: came to see the lord of the people, that descendant of the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>, seated in his court. // Valc_2,21.26 //
Then, at the appointed time, <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> who had mastered the <s>Vedas</s> and <s>Vedāṅgas</s>
consecrated King <s>Vallāla</s>, son of <s>Malhana</s>, with the <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation). // Valc_2,21.27 //
The lord of the earth went forward to receive <s>Sukhasena</s> and <s>Viṣṇumalla</s>,
and having bowed to those worthy of salutation, he spoke these words: // Valc_2,21.28 //
<s>Dharasena</s>, <s>Yajñasena</s>, <s>Dharmasiṃha</s>, and <s>Dhruva</s> —
may you all be pleased to assist me in the rites of sacrifice and gifts. // Valc_2,21.29 //
Having spoken thus, that righteous lord of the earth
assigned those officers to their appropriate duties. // Valc_2,21.30 //
He appointed <s>Bhīmasena</s> to the supervision of food and refreshments,
and appointed <s>Vṛhaspati</s>, the master of gifts, to the administration of donations. // Valc_2,21.31 //
He assigned men to other duties as well,
and charged <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> with the reception of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>Kṣatriya</s>, and <s>Vaiśya</s> communities. // Valc_2,21.32 //
The king's sacrificial hall in <s>Gauḍa</s>, adorned with various trees,
was resplendent, equipped with rest-houses, beautiful and lovely in form. // Valc_2,21.33 //
With various gems and mineral treasures, embroidered carpets and canopies,
with couches, banners, and flags, it shone magnificently. // Valc_2,21.34 //
Separate places were arranged for each group —
for the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, the <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, the merchants, and those of the lowest birth. // Valc_2,21.35 //
<s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, <s>Vaiśyas</s>, and likewise the virtuous <s>Śūdra</s> communities —

children.text: nṛpeṇāmantritāḥ sarvve tatra rāse rasaṃ gatāḥ // Valc_2,21.36 //
children.translated_text: all were invited by the king, and there in the festive assembly they savored the delights. // Valc_2,21.36 //
Chieftains, princes, kings and sub-kings,
all the great feudatory lords, the inner circle, and high dignitaries — // Valc_2,21.37 //
they sat on seats appropriate to their rank, duly honored

children.text: vallālena sabhāyāṃ te divīva tridivaukasaḥ // Valc_2,21.38 //
children.translated_text: by <s>Vallāla</s> in that assembly, like the dwellers of heaven in the celestial court. // Valc_2,21.38 //
Shining in the midst of the assembly like <s>Indra</s> in <s>Sudharmā</s> (the divine court),
the king worshipped the gods and ancestors with a sin-destroying sacrifice. // Valc_2,21.39 //
Then, bearing his sword, wearing his turban, adorned with all ornaments,
desiring prosperity, the king gave gifts like another <s>Karṇa</s>. // Valc_2,21.40 //
There, with gold equal to his own weight, he delighted
the earthly gods (<s>Brāhmaṇas</s>) with the <s>tulāpuruṣadāna</s> (gift of one's weight in gold), along with thousands in <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (ritual fees). // Valc_2,21.41 //
At the conclusion, the king then feasted handsome <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>
and others as well, in hundreds and thousands. // Valc_2,21.42 //

children.text: devā vabhūvuḥ pitaraśca tatra hṛdyaiśca kavyai rnitarāṃ sutṛptāḥ /
children.translated_text: The gods and ancestors there were thoroughly satisfied with pleasing <s>kavya</s> (ancestral offerings),
and the hosts of earthly gods (<s>Brāhmaṇas</s>) were gratified with gifts of gold, food, drink, and abundant <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (ritual fees). // Valc_2,21.43 //

children.text: ityānandabhaṭṭaprokte śaraṇadattīye vallālacarive yajñotsavo nāma ekaviṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus ends the twenty-first chapter, called 'The Sacrificial Festival,' in the <s>Vallālacarita</s> composed by <s>Ānandabhaṭṭa</s>, narrated by <s>Śaraṇadatta</s>.
Now begins Chapter Twenty-Two.
On another occasion, kinsmen and family members gathered together,
and the princes and <s>Rāṇakas</s> (minor chiefs) entered the dining hall. // Valc_2,22.1 //
When those noble persons had taken their seats

children.text: bhujyamāneṣu sarveṣu vallālena mudā saha // Valc_2,22.2 //
children.translated_text: and all were dining together with <s>Vallāla</s> in joy, // Valc_2,22.2 //
groups of virtuous <s>Śūdras</s> entered the other dining halls

children.text: sparddhayā viviśurbhoktuṃ viśāṃ na dṛśyate sthalī // Valc_2,22.3 //
children.translated_text: eagerly to eat — no space of the <s>Vaiśyas</s> could be seen. // Valc_2,22.3 //
At that moment, the <s>Vaiśyas</s> (merchants), consulting among themselves,
rose up, wishing to leave the royal palace. // Valc_2,22.4 //
When some had already gone outside and others were about to leave,
then <s>Bhīmasena</s> followed them and spoke respectfully: // Valc_2,22.5 //
"Why do you, O good people, leave without eating?

children.text: asmāsu vo yadākūtaṃ sarvvathārhatha bhāṣitum // Valc_2,22.6 //
children.translated_text: Whatever your concern with us, you should speak it fully." // Valc_2,22.6 //

children.text: tacchrutvā vaṇijaḥ prāhuḥ śrūyatāṃ bho mahāśaya /
children.translated_text: Hearing this, the merchants said: "Listen, O noble sir —
there has been contact-pollution (<s>spṛṣṭāspṛṣṭi</s>); therefore we are unable to eat." // Valc_2,22.7 //
Thereupon, without striking them, the exceedingly wrathful <s>Bhīmasena</s>
reproached those <s>Śūdras</s>, saying "Such is the insolence of <s>Śūdras</s>!" and rebuked them. // Valc_2,22.8 //
Then arguments and counter-arguments arose, and the enraged
<s>Bhīmasena</s>, the king's favorite, spoke harsh words. // Valc_2,22.9 //
Thereupon all the merchants departed from the royal palace,

children.text: ākrośanto vikrośanto varṣānte vāridā iva // Valc_2,22.10 //
children.translated_text: crying out and wailing, like rain-clouds at the end of the rainy season. // Valc_2,22.10 //

children.text: ityānandabhaṭṭaprokte śaraṇadattīye vallālacarite vaṇijāvamānanaṃ nāma dvāviṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus ends the twenty-second chapter, called 'The Humiliation of the Merchants,' in the <s>Vallālacarita</s> composed by <s>Ānandabhaṭṭa</s>, narrated by <s>Śaraṇadatta</s>.
Now begins Chapter Twenty-Three.
Then on the following day, approaching the king who was seated in court,
<s>Bhīma</s>, the king's favorite, spoke with his knees placed on the ground: // Valc_2,23.1 //
"O lord, all the <s>Śūdra</s> communities have been satisfied with the feasts,
but the <s>Suvarṇa</s> merchants, out of arrogance, departed without eating. // Valc_2,23.2 //
Those merchants are extremely wicked, ill-mannered, and proud of their lineage;
those evil-minded ones desire to dine in the same row as <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and <s>Kṣatriyas</s>. // Valc_2,23.3 //
Even upon seeing the dining area free of <s>Śūdra</s> people,
they disdained the prosperous host and left just as they had come. // Valc_2,23.4 //

children.text: sarvveṣāṃ vaṇijāṃ netā vallabhaḥ sa durāśayaḥ /
children.translated_text: The leader of all those merchants, that evil-minded <s>Vallabha</s>,

children.text: pālairhṛto mahārāja tvayā saha virudhyate // Valc_2,23.5 //
children.translated_text: was brought by the guards, O great king — he quarrels with you. // Valc_2,23.5 //
His son-in-law is the king of <s>Magadha</s>, of which he boasts;

children.text: dharāṃ sa manyate tena śarāvamiva garvitaḥ // Valc_2,23.6 //
children.translated_text: because of that, the arrogant man regards the earth as a mere potsherd. // Valc_2,23.6 //
Hearing these words of <s>Bhīmasena</s>, the king

children.text: jvalano havaneneva prajajvāla sa manyunā // Valc_2,23.7 //
children.translated_text: blazed forth with fury, like a fire fed with oblations. // Valc_2,21.7 //
Gnashing his teeth, the king upon his throne
appeared like a thundering cloud risen in the sky, flashing with lightning. // Valc_2,23.8 //
From his head fell the diamond-studded crown,
from his trembling body, like a mass of meteors from the evening sky. // Valc_2,23.9 //
Then King <s>Vallāla</s>, his eyes rolling with rage,

children.text: vaṇijāṃ darpacūrṇārthaṃ śapathaṃ kṛtavān bhṛśam // Valc_2,23.10 //
children.translated_text: took a terrible oath to crush the pride of the merchants. // Valc_2,23.10 //

children.text:
rājovāca:
yadi dāmbhikhān suvarṇān vaṇijaḥ śūdratve na pātayiṣyāmi, vallabhacandrasaudāgirasya durātmano daṇḍaṃ na vidhāsyāmi, tadā gobrāhmaṇaghātena yāni pātakāni bhavitavyāni tāni me bhaviṣyantīti / dhārttarāṣṭrāṇāṃ vināśāya bhīmasenena yādṛśaḥ śapathaḥ kṛtaḥ eteṣāṃ pātanāya śapatho me tādṛśo jñātavyaḥ, adyāvadhi ete satre śūdravadgrāhyāḥ / vyarthameṣāṃ yajñasūtnadhāraṇamataḥparameteṣāṃ yājanādhyāpane pratigrahañca ye brāhmaṇāḥ kariṣyanti, te jvalanto 'pi patiṣyanti, nānyathā || Valc_2,23.11 ||
children.translated_text:
The king said:
"If I do not degrade the fraudulent gold-dealing merchants to <s>Śūdra</s> status, and if I do not punish the wicked merchant <s>Vallabhacandra Saudāgira</s>, then may the sins that accrue from the slaughter of cows and <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> be upon me! Just as <s>Bhīmasena</s> took a vow for the destruction of the <s>Dhārtarāṣṭras</s>, so shall my vow for the degradation of these be known. From this day forth, they shall be treated as <s>Śūdras</s> in all assemblies. Their wearing of sacred threads is henceforth futile. Whatever <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> perform for them the rites of sacrifice, teaching, or acceptance of gifts — they too shall fall, even if they are blazing (with learning). There is no other way." // <s>Valc</s> 2,23.11 //
This decree was soon circulated throughout the kingdom;
hearing it, the merchants gathered and took counsel together. // <s>Valc</s> 2,23.12 //
Then, their bodies trembling with anger at the king's lack of deliberation,
they blocked the industrious servant-traders from <s>Gauḍa</s> city. // <s>Valc</s> 2,23.13 //
The merchants paid two and three times the price to the servant-traders;
due to the shortage of servants, great hardship befell all castes. // <s>Valc</s> 2,23.14 //
When such great hardship arose and was reported by the groups of subjects,
the lord of the earth pondered what was to be done. // <s>Valc</s> 2,23.15 //
Seeing no other remedy, he commanded the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> thus:
"For the welfare of the people, let the <s>Kaivartas</s> (fishermen) be made to perform servant duties." // <s>Valc</s> 2,23.16 //
The <s>Kaivartas</s>, willing to serve, upon hearing the king's decree,
came to the royal court by the hundreds and thousands. // <s>Valc</s> 2,23.17 //
The king then addressed them, their hands folded with cloth upon their necks (in submission):

children.text: vṛttirvo dīyate sevā gacchadhvaṃ vyavahāratām // Valc_2,23.18 //
children.translated_text: "Livelihood shall be given to you; serve — go and engage in trade!" // <s>Valc</s> 2,23.18 //
The king then made the chief among them a great provincial lord (<s>mahāmāṇḍalika</s>)
and dispatched <s>Maheśa</s> to the southern <s>ghāṭ</s>. // <s>Valc</s> 2,23.19 //
On another occasion, the garland-makers, potters, and smiths,
with skilled hands and cloth upon their necks, stood before the king. // <s>Valc</s> 2,23.20 //

children.text: santuṣṭaḥ sevayā teṣāṃ vyājahāra vaco nṛpaḥ /
children.translated_text: Pleased with their service, the king pronounced:
"You shall be regarded as good <s>Śūdras</s> by my word." // <s>Valc</s> 2,23.21 //
"He by whose word an impure man becomes pure,

children.text: śuciścaivāśuciḥ samyak kathaṃ rājā na daivatam // Valc_2,23.22 //
children.translated_text: and a pure man impure — how is the king not a deity?" // <s>Valc</s> 2,23.22 //
With the passage of time, the king degraded from <s>Brahmin</s> status
the <s>Brahmabandhus</s> (unworthy Brahmins) of evil mind who dealt in servants. // <s>Valc</s> 2,23.23 //
He appointed a washerman to his personal service and made him a chief;

children.text: ṭhakkuraṃ ca cakārāsau prasanno rājanāpitam // Valc_2,23.24 //
children.translated_text: and, being pleased, the king also made a barber a <s>Ṭhakkura</s> (lord). // <s>Valc</s> 2,23.24 //
Then, observing that the merchants remained unbroken in their own customs,

children.text: ādiśat tān nṛpaḥ sarvvān yajñasūtrāṇi varjjitum // Valc_2,23.25 //
children.translated_text: the king commanded all of them to abandon their sacred threads. // <s>Valc</s> 2,23.25 //
"Let the merchants who dwell in the kingdom abandon their sacred threads;

children.text: tyajedyo na sa daṇḍyaḥ syāt sevakānnṛpa ityaśāt // Valc_2,23.26 //
children.translated_text: whoever does not abandon them shall be punished" — so the king commanded his servants. // <s>Valc</s> 2,23.26 //

children.text: āhatya ḍiṇḍimān bhṛtyā nagare nagare viśām /
children.translated_text: The servants, beating drums in every city and town,
proclaimed the king's decree in the squares and streets. // <s>Valc</s> 2,23.27 //
The great merchants, disregarding the king's order and fearing for their <s>dharma</s>,
hastily departed to all directions with their wives and possessions. // <s>Valc</s> 2,23.28 //
Some went to <s>Ayodhyā</s>, some to <s>Mudgagiri</s>,
to <s>Candramāyuta</s>, <s>Pāṭlī</s> (Pāṭaliputra), and some to <s>Tāmralipta</s>; // <s>Valc</s> 2,23.29 //
some to <s>Vinīta</s> city, and some to <s>Śṛṅkhalā</s>. // <s>Valc</s> 2,23.30 //
some to <s>Udayapura</s>, some went to <s>Mānagaḍha</s>,
Wherever they went, all of them, afflicted by fear of royal punishment,
abandoned their sacred threads, both the golden and the cotton ones. // <s>Valc</s> 2,23.31 //
At that time, <s>Vallāla</s>, observing the confused state of the clan
of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, consulted with Vedic scholars. // <s>Valc</s> 2,23.32 //
Examining the distinction of their lineage-greatness and then consecrating them with the proper rites,

children.text: brahmatvaṃ kṣatriyatvañca kalpayāmāsa sa prabhuḥ // Valc_2,23.33 //
children.translated_text: the lord assigned them <s>Brahmin</s> status and <s>Kṣatriya</s> status accordingly. // <s>Valc</s> 2,23.33 //

children.text: ityāndabhaṭṭaprokte śaraṇadattīye vallālacarite jātīnāṃ pātanonnayanādināma trayoviṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus ends the twenty-third chapter, named 'The Degradation and Elevation of Castes,' in the <s>Vallālacarita</s> composed by <s>Ānandabhaṭṭa</s> in the <s>Śaraṇadattīya</s> recension.
Now begins the twenty-fourth chapter.
Long ago, the illustrious King <s>Vallāla</s>, residing in the foremost city of <s>Gauḍa</s>,
initiated the worship of those worthy ones in a fitting manner, being of great renown. // <s>Valc</s> 2,24.1 //
Having constructed a beautiful monastery (<s>maṭha</s>), with an inlaid floor of painted stone,
made of baked bricks, divine, furnished with beds and seats, // <s>Valc</s> 2,24.2 //
with fine walls, enriched with a painting gallery, with sturdy pillars, charming,
with ivory pegs set in walls to serve as book-rests, // <s>Valc</s> 2,24.3 //
adorned with delightful gardens attractive with various flowers and fruits,
endowed with water-reservoirs filled with exceedingly clear and sweet drinking water, // <s>Valc</s> 2,24.4 //
furnished with doors and windows, equipped with various furnishings,
plastered with lime, gleaming white, well-stocked with food and provisions, // <s>Valc</s> 2,24.5 //
graced with halls for discourses, meditation, fire-offerings, and recitation,
and provided with lodging houses for ascetics and travelers — // <s>Valc</s> 2,24.6 //
equipped with attendants for private needs, near the <s>Pradyumneśvara</s> temple,
he duly consecrated it to the yogin <s>Śrī Siṃhagiri</s>. // <s>Valc</s> 2,24.7 //
For the procurement of loincloths, firewood, garments, and other necessities,

children.text: pradadau vipulāṃ bhūmiṃ rājā śraddhāsamanvitaḥ // Valc_2,24.8 //
children.translated_text: the king, full of faith, gave extensive land. // <s>Valc</s> 2,24.8 //
Then the best of kings, the controller of others, of excellent character with pure intellect excelling in all virtues,
had a decree prepared on a copper plate. // <s>Valc</s> 2,24.9 //
The great king gave the village of <s>Kāsāraka</s>, within the <s>Suvarṇamuktikā</s> district,
with increased annual revenue, to <s>Gautama Anantaśarman</s>. // <s>Valc</s> 2,24.10 //
Provided with prepared food, edibles, and all grains,
furnished with male and female servants, equipped with all necessities, // <s>Valc</s> 2,24.11 //
plastered with lime, well-built, fastened with door-panels and bolts,
with an auspicious entrance, gleaming, adorned with lattice-work and the like — // <s>Valc</s> 2,24.12 //
having caused many such residences to be built,
the king then settled southern <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> (<s>Dākṣiṇātyas</s>) in them. // <s>Valc</s> 2,24.13 //
The lord of the earth made gifts of gold, gifts of silver, and gifts of cows,
and performed various gifts, both regular (<s>nitya</s>) and occasional (<s>naimittika</s>). // <s>Valc</s> 2,24.14 //
Enjoying various pleasures and constantly giving gifts to worthy recipients,

children.text: jagāma kālaḥ sukhataḥ samāno bhūto na kaścidbhavitāsti cāsya // Valc_2,24.15 //
children.translated_text: time passed happily — such a one has never existed before nor will exist hereafter. // <s>Valc</s> 2,24.15 //

children.text: na yena bhuktāḥ sukhadāḥ subhogāḥ dānaṃ na dattaṃ dhaninārhatāñca /
children.translated_text: He who has not enjoyed pleasurable delights, who has not given gifts of wealth to the worthy —

children.text: avāpyate tena kaṭhoraghora duḥsahyaduḥkhamadhikaṃ paratra // Valc_2,24.16 //
children.translated_text: by him is attained in the hereafter a great excess of harsh, terrible, unbearable suffering. // <s>Valc</s> 2,24.16 //
Thus ends the twenty-fourth chapter, named 'The Performance of Charitable Acts,' in the <s>Vallālacarita</s> composed by <s>Ānandabhaṭṭa</s>.
Now begins the twenty-fifth chapter.
<s>Oṃ</s> — Salutation to <s>Śiva</s>!
O <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> (Golden Embryo), inner self of the world, of the color of the sun, beyond darkness!

children.text: tvatto 'sti jātaḥ puruṣaḥ purāṇaḥ tvatto 'pi vedā jaya deva deva // Valc_2,25.1 //
children.translated_text: From you was born the ancient <s>Puruṣa</s>, from you too the <s>Vedas</s> — victory, O God of Gods! // <s>Valc</s> 2,25.1 //

children.text: tvattaḥ prasūtā jagataḥ prasūtiḥ sarvvānubhūstvaṃ paramāṇubhūtaḥ /
children.translated_text: From you arose the source of the world; you are the all-pervading, become the atom;

children.text: anoraṇīyān mahato mahīyān ānandarupa jaya deva śambho // Valc_2,25.2 //
children.translated_text: smaller than the smallest, greater than the greatest, of the form of bliss — victory, O God, O <s>Śambhu</s>! // <s>Valc</s> 2,25.2 //
You are <s>Viṣṇu</s>, you are the four-faced <s>Brahmā</s>,
you are <s>Rudra</s>, the blessed <s>Maheśa</s>;
sky, <s>Brahman</s>, the void, both with and without qualities —
of the form of pure consciousness, victory, O God, O All! // <s>Valc</s> 2,25.3 //
You alone, O <s>Rudra</s>, create this universe;
you sustain the entirety, O One of universal form;
in you alone at the end does this universe find its resting place —
we worship you, O Victory, O God, O Primal Deity! // <s>Valc</s> 2,25.4 //
Releasing a stream of nectar,
approach and allay the torment of gods and men;
the <s>Vedas</s> declare your form to be infinite —
victory to you, O Lord of the Universe! // <s>Valc</s> 2,25.5 //
To <s>Bhava</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), the bestower of devotion and liberation,
the Great Sage, the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, the holy one —
with bowed head we worship the <s>Jagadguru</s> (World-teacher),
the Self-born — victory, O God, O Lord of the World! // <s>Valc</s> 2,25.6 //
You are the Protector, you are the Radiant One, you are the Supreme Refuge;
you are the Lord in the world — I bow before you.
You are the best of physicians, the remover of thorns (afflictions),
you are the Healer — victory, O God of Gods! // <s>Valc</s> 2,25.7 //
Pure, spotless, resembling the Silver Mountain (<s>Kailāsa</s>),
carrying one across the ocean of existence, acting for the world's welfare,
granting the five-fold liberation and the boon of sight —
we worship the Three-eyed One — victory, O God! // <s>Valc</s> 2,25.8 //
Endowed with a thousand feet, eyes, and heads,
with a thousand arms, beyond the beyond —
I bow to you, O <s>Śambhu</s>, who are beyond <s>Brahman</s>,
O <s>Pinākin</s> (Bearer of the Bow) — victory, O God of Gods! // <s>Valc</s> 2,25.9 //
To the husband of <s>Umā</s>, the fierce one, the source of existence,
I bow to you, O <s>Hara</s>, O All!
To <s>Kāla</s> (Time), to <s>Bhaga</s> (Fortune), to the Radiant One,
to the Self of All, O God — salutation to <s>Śiva</s>! // <s>Valc</s> 2,25.10 //

Thus ends the twenty-fifth chapter, named 'The Recitation of the Auspicious Victory Hymn composed by <s>Kālidāsa Nandi</s>,' in the <s>Vallālacarita</s> composed by the illustrious <s>Ānandabhaṭṭa</s>.
Now begins the twenty-sixth chapter.
<s>Dharmagiri</s>, who had been previously banished along with his community,

children.text: vṛttihīno yayau dūraṃ deśāddeśāntaraṃ bhraman // Valc_2,26.1 //
children.translated_text: deprived of livelihood, went far away, wandering from country to country. // <s>Valc</s> 2,26.1 //
Brooding upon the insult and oppression inflicted by the king's order

children.text: svasya bhraṣṭādhikārañca na lebhe nirvṛtiṃ giriḥ // Valc_2,26.2 //
children.translated_text: and his own loss of authority, <s>Giri</s> found no peace. // <s>Valc</s> 2,26.2 //
Contemplating the end of his enmity, after the passing of years,
he beheld <s>Vāyādumba</s>, a <s>Mleccha</s> (barbarian) lord, surrounded by his own forces. // <s>Valc</s> 2,26.3 //
Exciting him by promising <s>Vallāla</s>'s wealth and gems,

children.text: mleccheśaṃ niśi tat sainyairnyaruṇadvikramaṃ puram // Valc_2,26.4 //
children.translated_text: he had the <s>Mleccha</s> lord besiege the city of <s>Vikrama</s> with his armies by night. // <s>Valc</s> 2,26.4 //
Smoke-colored, bearing a bow, like a rain-cloud with its bow (rainbow),

children.text: vāyādumbaḥ sainyamadhye jagarja ca lalampha ca // Valc_2,26.5 //
children.translated_text: <s>Vāyādumba</s>, in the midst of his army, roared and leapt. // <s>Valc</s> 2,26.5 //
With axes and hatchets held high, with the tremendous sound of <s>Kurd</s> war-cries,
with bursts of laughter and splashing of water — that army resembled the ocean. // <s>Valc</s> 2,26.6 //

children.text: padghātaiḥ kampayan pṛthvīṃ huṅkāraiśca diśo daśa /
children.translated_text: Making the earth tremble with their footfalls, filling the ten directions

children.text: nādayan pañcasāhasraṃ mlecchasainyaṃ nanartta ha // Valc_2,26.7 //
children.translated_text: with 'huṃ' cries, the five-thousand-strong <s>Mleccha</s> army danced (in war-frenzy). // <s>Valc</s> 2,26.7 //
Now the king, concealed in the pleasures of the inner palace,
unaware of what had happened, awoke after a long time. // <s>Valc</s> 2,26.8 //
At dawn, the king, hearing the great tumultuous uproar,
let go of his beloved's creeper-like arm and grasped his sword. // <s>Valc</s> 2,26.9 //
Thinking of his city — its moat uncleaned, its battlements and war-engines absent —
the king considered himself already slain. // <s>Valc</s> 2,26.10 //
Then, seeing the king preparing to march out for battle,
all the royal consorts, their eyes brimming with tears — // <s>Valc</s> 2,26.11 //
<s>Śilādevī</s>, <s>Padmākṣī</s>, <s>Subhagā</s>, <s>Hemamālikā</s>,
<s>Sonadevā</s>, and <s>Caṇḍelī</s> — approached him and said:
"Let there be no misfortune in this battle; but if ill fortune should come, // <s>Valc</s> 2,26.12 //

children.text: anāthāḥ kiṃ kariṣyāmo vada nātha tadāvalāḥ /
children.translated_text: what shall we helpless women do? Tell us, O lord!"

children.text: tacchratvā vacanaṃ tāsāṃ rājā vāṣpāvilekṣaṇaḥ // Valc_2,26.13 //
children.translated_text: Hearing the words of his wives, the king, his eyes brimming with tears, // <s>Valc</s> 2,26.13 //
embracing them one by one and kissing them on their faces,

children.text: pratyūce mukhapadmāni tāsāṃ paśyan mahīpatiḥ // Valc_2,26.14 //
children.translated_text: the lord of the earth replied, gazing at their lotus-faces: // <s>Valc</s> 2,26.14 //
A pair of pigeons shall go forth, O beloveds, to the battlefield;

children.text: yadi tau pratyāgacchetām khagau prāvṛttikāviva // Valc_2,26.15 //
children.translated_text: if those two birds return, like [birds] returning during the rainy season, // Valc_2,26.15 //
then you shall know of our defeat on the field of battle;
your <s>satīdharma</s> (the duty of a chaste wife to self-immolate) shall be protected from the <s>Yavanas</s> (Muslim invaders), O beautiful-faced ones;

children.text: vahniṃ prajvālayiṣyanti bhṛtyā dattājñayā mayā // Valc_2,26.16 //
children.translated_text: the servants, commanded by me, shall kindle the fire. // Valc_2,26.16 //

children.text: ityuktā punarāliṅgya cumbitvā ca punaḥ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, embracing and kissing [them] again and again,

children.text: sannaddho yuddhayātrāṃ sa cakāra svavalairvṛtaḥ // Valc_2,26.17 //
children.translated_text: he, having armed himself, set out on the military expedition, surrounded by his forces. // Valc_2,26.17 //
His army shone forth, furnished with various weapons,
with elephant-riders, horse-riders, charioteers, and foot-soldiers. // Valc_2,26.18 //
Then a great and tumultuous battle took place, causing the destruction of the <s>Mlecchas</s> (barbarians),
the ground flooded with the blood of warriors, both slain and wounded. // Valc_2,26.19 //
When his army was destroyed there, he confronted <s>Vāyādumba</s> (Bakhtiyar), the mighty one,

children.text: rurodha kṣmāpatiryuddhe śrīrāma iva rāvaṇam // Valc_2,26.20 //
children.translated_text: and the king besieged him in battle, as <s>Śrī Rāma</s> besieged <s>Rāvaṇa</s>. // Valc_2,26.20 //
Then, rushing forward with great speed, the king, swift of hand,

children.text: mastakaṃ tasya ciccheda namūceriva vāsavaḥ // Valc_2,26.21 //
children.translated_text: cut off his head, as <s>Vāsava</s> (Indra) [cut off the head of] <s>Namuci</s>. // Valc_2,26.21 //
When the goddess of victory chose the king, garland in hand,
then the servants of <s>Yama</s> (Death), garland in hand, bound <s>Dumba</s> (Bakhtiyar). // Valc_2,26.22 //
At that time, by a stroke of ill fortune, the two birds had escaped from the cage,

children.text: unmaktau kenacidvā cet rāmapālapuraṃ gatau // Valc_2,26.23 //
children.translated_text: released by someone, or perhaps maddened — [and] had gone to <s>Rāmapālapura</s>. // Valc_2,26.23 //
Seeing the two pigeons there, as if two messengers of <s>Yama</s> had arrived,
all the king's wives threw themselves into the blazing fire-pit. // Valc_2,26.24 //

children.text: iti vallālacarite śrīmadānandabhaṭṭakṛtaṃ khilavallālacaritaṃ nāma ṣaḍvaviṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus in the <s>Vallālacarita</s>, composed by the illustrious <s>Ānandabhaṭṭa</s>, the twenty-sixth chapter called 'The Supplementary <s>Vallālacarita</s>.'
Now, the twenty-seventh chapter.
Noticing the cage empty on the battlefield, the king,
fearing the worst, turned back in haste. // Valc_2,27.1 //
Seeing the banner of fire from afar, extremely agitated,

children.text: tataḥ svaṃ prāviśadveśma sarvvanāśaṃ vilokitum // Valc_2,27.2 //
children.translated_text: he then entered his own dwelling to behold the total destruction. // Valc_2,27.2 //

children.text: dṛṣṭvārddhadagdhā jvalane svapatnī rummattarūpo nitarāṃ babhūva /
children.translated_text: Seeing his wives half-burnt in the fire, he became utterly mad in appearance;

children.text: nivāryyamānopi janaiḥ prayatnāt papāta rājā jvaladagnikuṇḍe // Valc_2,27.3 //
children.translated_text: though restrained by people with effort, the king threw himself into the blazing fire-pit. // Valc_2,27.3 //
In the <s>Śaka</s> year one thousand twenty-eight (i.e. 1106 CE), the king,

children.text: strībhiḥ sārddhaṃ mahābhāga utpapāta divaṃ prati // Valc_2,27.4 //
children.translated_text: the great and blessed one, together with his wives, ascended to heaven. // Valc_2,27.4 //
There is heard in this [tradition] a saying, handed down through the succession of venerable elders:
<s>Vallāla</s> followed his father, who was distinguished in valor, into battle. // Valc_2,27.5 //
In <s>Mithilā</s> there lived a certain <s>yogī</s> of firm vows;
<s>Vallāla</s>, on his military expedition, rashly transgressed him [by riding past]. // Valc_2,27.6 //
Struck by the hoof of a horse, the sage cursed <s>Vallāla</s>:

children.text: sakalatro vahnikuṇḍe patitvā tvaṃ mariṣyasi // Valc_2,27.7 //
children.translated_text: 'Together with your wife, you shall fall into a fire-pit and die!' // Valc_2,27.7 //

children.text: tat smṛtvā brahmaśāpaṃ sa vijayaṃ labdhavānapi /
children.translated_text: Remembering that Brahmin's curse, although he had obtained victory,
he reflected in his mind: 'The time of death has arrived.' // Valc_2,27.8 //
Overpowered by that [curse], the king assuredly entered the fire;
without a Brahmin's curse, such a calamity would never have occurred. // Valc_2,27.9 //

children.text: sa brahmadaṇḍena purā hato 'bhūt dāraiśca sārddhamavanīśvaraḥ saḥ /
children.translated_text: He was slain by the Brahmin's rod of punishment of old, that lord of the earth, together with his wives;

children.text: kapotapratyāgamanañca mṛtyau rājñaśca śoko na hi mukhyahetuḥ // Valc_2,27.10 //
children.translated_text: the return of the pigeons was the [instrument] of death; the grief of the king was not the primary cause. // Valc_2,27.10 //

children.text: rājan jānāsi bhadraṃ te iyaṃ śivajalā śubhā /
children.translated_text: 'O king, may you know — blessings upon you — this [tank], filled with auspicious water,

children.text: kīrttiśeṣaṃ gatavataḥ kīrttiṃ vadati dīrghikā // Valc_2,27*.1 //
children.translated_text: proclaims the fame of him who has departed, leaving only fame behind.' // Valc_2,27*.1 //
[verse number jumps from "1" to "4"
The king's fame having been destroyed by the eating of cows, and by the force of time — what a sin!

children.text: kīrttyānayāsāviva vidyamānaḥ hāhā gataḥ kvāvanināthavaṃśaḥ // Valc_2,27*.4 //
children.translated_text: As if by this very fame [still] existing — alas, where has the royal dynasty gone? // Valc_2,27*.4 //
Composed with effort by the poet <s>Ānandabhaṭṭa</s>, endowed with speech flowing from the lotus-mouth of <s>Vyāsa</s>,
may this chronicle of King <s>Vallāla</s>, like a new moon, cause the water-lily of the hearts of all people to bloom! // Valc_2,27*.5 //
Whatever was spoken by the revered <s>Bhaṭṭa</s> and whatever was said by other learned ones —
all that has been made manifest in this royal chronicle of <s>Vallāla</s>. // Valc_2,27*.6 //
'This earth was made devoid of Brahmins by <s>Subhauma</s>' — what was said thus,

children.text: uktaṃ tattu rājabhayāditi manyāmahe vayam // Valc_2,27*.7 //
children.translated_text: that, we believe, was [said] out of fear of the king. // Valc_2,27*.7 //
Or perhaps that was declared by the revered <s>Bhaṭṭa</s> merely in jest,
or it may be meaningless, within the <s>Vyāsa Purāṇa</s>. // Valc_2,27*.8 //
'This earth was made devoid of <s>Kṣatriyas</s> by <s>Bhārgava</s> (Paraśurāma) in ancient times' —

children.text: evaṃ hi bhārate prāha svayaṃ vyāso mahāmuniḥ // Valc_2,27*.9 //
children.translated_text: thus indeed <s>Vyāsa</s>, the great sage himself, declared in the <s>Bhārata</s> (Mahābhārata). // Valc_2,27*.9 //
From a <s>Kṣatriya</s> woman by a Brahmin, a <s>Kṣetrī</s> [is born] — he is called a prince;
the <s>Suvarṇas</s>, lacking the <s>upanayana</s> (sacred thread ceremony), are merchants who have fallen into the state of outcasts (<s>vrātyas</s>). // Valc_2,27*.10 //
The cowherd, the garland-maker, the betel-seller, the bell-metal worker, the string-maker, the conch-worker,

children.text: kulālaḥ karmmakāraśca nāpito nava śāyakāḥ // Valc_2,27*.11 //
children.translated_text: the potter, the craftsman, and the barber — [these are] the nine <s>śāyakas</s>. // Valc_2,27*.11 //
The oil-presser, the perfumer, and the physician are declared as good <s>Śūdras</s>;

children.text: satśūdrānāntu sarvveṣāṃ kāyastha uttamaḥ smṛtaḥ // Valc_2,27*.12 //
children.translated_text: among all good <s>Śūdras</s>, the <s>Kāyastha</s> is regarded as the best. // Valc_2,27*.12 //

children.text: śataṃ jīva mahārāja tasyāḥ sahajavaṃśaja // Valc_2,27*.13 //
children.translated_text: live a hundred years, O great king, born of her natural lineage! // Valc_2,27*.13 //
The <s>Gaṅgā</s>, born from the feet of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, purifies the three worlds;

children.text: yadyat priyatamaṃ loke yasmiṃśca ramate manaḥ /
children.translated_text: Whatever is most dear in the world, and whatever the mind delights in —
all that should be offered to the Brahmins, dedicating it to <s>Acyuta</s> (Viṣṇu). // Valc_2,27*.14 //
Of the lord of <s>Navadvīpa</s>, the illustrious and wise king,
of good intellect, seated in the assembly — before him, through recitation, // Valc_2,27*.15 //
in the <s>Śaka</s> year fourteen hundred, plus [the number represented by] human teeth (i.e. 32, = Śaka 1432),
on the second day of the bright half of <s>Pauṣa</s>, on the day of his birthday, // Valc_2,27*.16 //
by the learned <s>Ānandabhaṭṭa</s>, the skilled creator of noble lineages,

children.text: vallālacaritaṃ tasmai mayā dattaṃ sahāśiṣā // Valc_2,27*.17 //
children.translated_text: this <s>Vallālacarita</s> was given by me to him, together with blessings. // Valc_2,27*.17 //
He in whose house this auspicious <s>Vallālacarita</s> exists —

children.text: iha puṇyaṃ sa labhate paratra ca parāṃ gatim // Valc_2,27*.18 //
children.translated_text: he obtains merit in this world and the highest destination in the next. // Valc_2,27*.18 //

Thus the Supplementary <s>Vallālacarita</s>, composed by the illustrious <s>Ānandabhaṭṭa Mahāmahopādhyāya</s>, born of the lineage of the illustrious <s>Anantabhaṭṭa</s> from the southern <s>Drāviḍa</s> [country], is concluded.
Colophon in MS ka:

children.text:
gurave namaḥ |
śubhamastu śakābdāḥ 1629 |
kāmadevacakravarttiṇaḥ ātmaja
śrīlakṣmīnārāyaṇadevaśarmaṇaḥ svākṣaram |
śrīrāmajīvanarāyasya svīyapustakamiti |
sāhāraṃdevapañcatvābde samāptaścāyaṃ granthaḥ |
śrīkṛṣṇāya namaḥ śrīrastu mayi lekhake |
gaurīśo jayati |
children.translated_text:
Salutation to the <s>guru</s>.
May there be auspiciousness. <s>Śaka</s> year 1629.
In the hand of <s>Śrī Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa Devaśarman</s>, son of the emperor <s>Kāmadeva</s>.
This book belongs to <s>Śrī Rāmajīvanarāya</s>.
This text was completed in the <s>Sāhāraṃdeva</s> [era], year of the fifth.
Salutation to <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>. May there be prosperity upon me, the scribe.
<s>Gaurīśa</s> is victorious.
Colophon in MS kha:

children.text: nāmānyathā yadi punaśca kaścin mithyānuvādaṃ harate ca pustim /
children.translated_text: If anyone falsely alters the names or carries away the book through false copying,

children.text: netrasya hāniṃ tanayasya śokaṃ sarvvāṅgakuṣṭhaṃ labhate ca nūnam //
children.translated_text: he surely obtains loss of eyesight, grief for his son, and leprosy of all limbs.
In the year ending in <s>Rudra</s>, may there be auspiciousness, O followers of the one path;

children.text: grahastu vasunā sārddhaṃ prauṣṭhapadyāṃ divā site //
children.translated_text: the planet [is] with <s>Vasu</s>, on the bright day of <s>Prauṣṭhapadī</s> (Bhādrapada).
The scribe is the son of <s>Viṣṇu</s> and then of <s>Śāṇḍilyavandyaka</s>;
the world proclaims his name as the illustrious <s>Muralīdhara</s>.

children.text: bhādre māsi site pakṣe ekādaśyāṃ budhavāsare /
children.translated_text: In the month of <s>Bhādra</s>, in the bright fortnight, on the eleventh day (<s>ekādaśī</s>), on a Wednesday,
this auspicious <s>Vallālacarita</s> was written with care.

children.text:
śrīśrīyugādyāyai namo 'stu satataṃ mama |
śrīmuralīdharadevaśarmmaṇaḥ pustakamidam |
children.translated_text:
Constant salutation to the goddess of the beginning of the age (<s>Yugādyā</s>)!
This book belongs to <s>Śrī Muralīdhara Devaśarman</s>.
